en: The Ritual Manual for Cultivating the *Zhāi* Feast at the Great Assembly of the Holy and the Profane, Beings of Water and Land, within the Dharma Realm. Volume One.
Carefully compiled by the Śramaṇa Zhìpàn of East Lake, Siming, during the Song Dynasty;
re-edited by the junior disciple Zhūhóng of Yúnqī in Ancient Hangzhou during the Ming Dynasty.

(One day prior, the assembly bathes and changes their robes, and the master precepts the crowd in advance: "Tomorrow morning, rise early and wait for the appearance of the dawn light. After the light breakfast, proceed immediately with the opening ceremony; do not delay it so as to miss the auspicious time.
If this takes place within a monastery, the patron should arrive well in advance.)

Performing the ritual for opening the morning service (The Dharma Master leads the patron into the altar hall; the ritual of offering incense proceeds in sequence; the assembly strikes the *neng* and *bo* cymbals). (The Ritual Director intones:)
With a sincere heart, we take refuge and pay homage to the Buddhas, Dharma, and Sangha of the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm (the assembly joins in chanting):
the eternally abiding Triple Gem.

(The ritual master holds the incense burner and rings the bell, reciting the verses and mantras for purifying the three karmas; each verse consists of four lines, with the drum and cymbals struck once per line; the style should be refined and elegant, not elaborate or vulgar.)
The nature of phenomena is serene and pervades the Dharma-realm; Profound, immeasurable, and beyond the reach of words.
Since losing original luminosity in a single thought, The eighty thousand afflictions have all become veils.
On this day, practicing the fast and extending universal salvation, I purify the ground of the mind and observe solemn decorum.
Relying upon the secret words as empowerment, I shall now cause myself and others to return to primordial purity.
I, the Buddha Tathāgata, possess the mantra for purifying the three karmas; I shall now reverently recite it.
Oṃ sarvadharmāḥ śūnyatāsvabhāvāḥ śūnyatāsvabhāvaśūnyāḥ.

(Recite the mantra three times. Wait until the sound has ceased before striking the *neng* and *bo*. All subsequent recitations of mantras follow this pattern. The Dharma Master visualizes that his own body, as well as those of the assembly and the patrons—both externally and internally—are entirely pure.
He then rings the bell while reciting the *bai-biao* (declaration of purity) and intones the verse and mantra for comforting the *gālaṃ-deva*.)
The eighteen divine kings, receiving the Buddha’s command, constantly protect the monastery throughout the entire world;
within this pure palace of the Dharma King, enlightened deities surely come to dwell and guard it.
On this day, as offerings are reverently presented with impartiality, the sounds of the Dharma resound together and the assembly remains free from clamor.
Relying upon the secret words for empowerment, I shall gladden the spirits' hearts and increase their superior power.
I now reverently recite the mantra of consolation for all spirits spoken by our Buddha, the Tathāgata.
Namo Samantabhadra-buddhānām. Oṃ duru duru jivite svāhā. (Having recited this mantra three times, the assembly strikes the cymbals.

[The Dharma Master visualizes that the various deities of the monastery are all comforted and delighted, and he makes a perpetual vow for them to provide protection, whether they reside in noble families or elsewhere.]
The officiant strikes the bell and recites the verse and mantra for comforting the deities of the dwelling (which is not used if one is within a monastery).
May you diligently guard this residence and its soil; Protect and bring peace to people and things, manifesting the majestic spiritual power of all deities.
Since you act for yourselves without private interest, Rebuke and forbid all inauspiciousness according to the Dharma.
On this day, with sincere devotion, we offer equal offerings; may the holy and the mundane assemble together in a manner unlike their usual abodes.
Relying upon the empowerment of the secret words, we shall cause the spirits’ hearts to be free from fear.
The Buddha Tathāgata has a mantra for comforting all spirits; we now solemnly recite it (the mantra as before).

(After reciting the mantra three times, strike the gong. (The Dharma Master visualizes that the six deities residing in the dwelling are all comforted and delighted, and will constantly provide protection.
For the sake of the family of noble lineage, the ritual concludes here with this declaration, the ringing of the bell, and the chanting of the incense verse and mantra.)
This sandalwood from the "this-side" shore is no different thing; it originally arises from the pure mind itself.
If one can burn even a single mote of dust, all fragrances will naturally be fully present.
Today, with sincere devotion, I offer this impartial offering, desiring that the entire Dharma-realm be universally perfumed and made aware of it.
Relying upon the secret words for empowerment, I shall cause the mind of giving to reach all beings everywhere.
I now reverently recite the mantra for offering incense to convey my sincere faith to the Buddha, the Tathāgata.
Oṃ śavali-ta-ma-ni a-pra-ku-ṭha su-pa-ra-ni vi-kā-ṭhi huṃ. (Recite this mantra three times. Then, strike the gongs.

(The Dharma Master visualizes these clouds of incense pervading the entire Dharmadhātu before the Triple Gem, penetrating with faith so that there is nowhere they do not reach. [The Ritual Official] offers incense and says: Oṃ śavali-ta-ma-ni a-pra-ku-ṭha su-pa-ra-ni vi-kā-ṭhi huṃ.

(Recite this mantra three times. Then, strike the gongs. (The Dharma Master visualizes these clouds of incense pervading the entire Dharmadhātu before the Triple Gem, penetrating with faith so that there is nowhere they do not reach. [The Ritual Official] offers incense and says:)
Wherever the scriptures reside, that is the very body of the Tathāgata’s relics. That the Way of the Dharma may flourish must surely depend upon the monks of great virtue.
Since this single location possesses all Three Honored Ones, devas and humans constantly arise to provide protection; thus, the halls and buildings ought to be firmly radiant and pure.
Now, as you are about to convene a supreme assembly that shall forever differ from other times, how could it be otherwise than by establishing a boundary (*sīmābandha*) to augment its majesty?
May those who practice the fast according to the ritual strictly observe the supreme edict, thereby perfecting extraordinary merit.
May wondrous incense permeate the air and pure water sprinkle the earth, so that every region shall be as firm as a fortified city wall.

Although they secretly rely upon mantras, they truly receive the hidden support of perfect contemplation. One will soon see the jade groves stirred by the wind and the crystal halls unveiled by the clouds;
precious canopies suspended in the layered heavens and resplendent terraces rising above the vast assembly, with a thousand banners and streamers interlacing and surrounding them.
Various musical performances are arrayed around it; this is accomplished solely through the power of pure visualization. This is none other than the non-dispersion of Vulture Peak itself.
Having manifested this function, he further summons the various deities, hoping to ensure solemn stillness within the ritual arena and to expel all demonic obstacles.
△ In the following passage, the Xuansheng family takes Jiguang (the Land of Quiescent Light) as their dwelling place;
this certainly does not lie outside the ordinary abode. While among sages and worthies there may be those who differ from the common clan, [this remains the case].
It is said that when one contemplates their own body, the sense organs and objects give rise to impurity; and when one speaks of its location, dust arises from the earth and stones.
Because the causes within the mind consist of unwholesome conduct, the retributive fruits in the world are thus. Now, we shall open this supreme assembly.

This shall forever differ from other times. Were it not for the empowerment conferred by the establishment of the boundary (*sīmābandha*), how could those practicing the fast (*upoṣadha*) ensure the ritual is performed according to the rules?
One must reverently follow these supreme instructions and fully accomplish this marvelous merit. Let wondrous incense waft through the air, and let pure water sprinkle and cleanse the ground.

Throughout every corner and region, all shall share the same fortress-like solidity. Though this relies closely upon true mantras, it is in truth sustained by the profound power of wondrous contemplation.
One will soon behold the wind stirring the jade groves and the clouds parting from the crystal halls, as precious canopies hang suspended in the layered heavens.
A magnificent flower-pavilion rises upon a vast seat, surrounded by a thousand banners and streamers interlacing one another, with various musical performances arrayed at its sides;

this is accomplished solely through the power of pure visualization. This is none other than the unceasing assembly on Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa. Having manifested this function, he further summons all the deities.
I pray that the ritual arena may be hallowed and tranquil, so that all demonic obstacles may be expelled.
(The officiant holds the incense burner and vibrates the bell, invoking the various sages and binding the boundary.)
With single-minded devotion, we invoke the Tathāgata’s emanation, the Great Vajra Ucchuṣma, endowed with perfected supernatural powers, together with all his retinue.
We pray that you will not disregard your original vow, but out of compassion for sentient beings, descend upon this ritual site and protect and maintain the consecrated boundary.
(The assembly requests with incense and flowers).
I now respectfully proclaim the mantra of the Honored One;
may you deign to grant your protection. Oṃ buddhajihvā kucyemahe praraṇa ai muḥ muḥ.
Hīmaṇi, viji-vi, maṇākṣe, oṃ cakṣuṇa, uśmū, kucyut, huṃ huṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā. (Having finished reciting the mantra three times, strike the drum and cymbals.

[The Dharma Master] visualizes the majestic deportment of the Holy One and his immeasurable retinue descending into the ritual arena, standing in the center facing outward. During the reign of Emperor Taizong of the Tang dynasty, there was a person who held this mantra many times...

The court considered this a delusion of the masses and prohibited its recitation. Consequently, they issued an edict to remove ten characters from the manuscript stored in the Tripitaka. Later, the śramaṇa Huizhi of Pútí Temple on West Lake in Qiántáng encountered a man of high virtue in Shǔ who was instructed in the *Hèjì* (Vimalakīrti) dhāraṇī practice.

He recovered the complete mantra and recited it for two years, achieving great spiritual efficacy. He was able to cause his ritual pestle to ascend into the void and travel wherever he wished; when he chanted over water to cure diseases, there were none that were not healed.
The versions currently transmitted in the world are mostly these expanded editions with added phrases, which differ from the canon.
With single-minded devotion, we invoke the ten Great Vidyārājas, such as the Greatly Majestic and Wrathful Amṛtakuṇḍalī,
together with their retinues.
We pray that you will not violate your original vows, but out of compassion for sentient beings, descend upon this ritual site and protect the established boundary.
(The assembly offers incense and flowers with invitation).
I now respectfully proclaim the mantra of the Honored One;
may you deign to grant your protection. Oṃ hulu hulu tiṣṭha tiṣṭha bandha bandha.
Anānā Amṛte Oḍḍa (Recite the mantra three times. Then, ring the ghaṇṭā.
[The Dharma Master visualizes the noble one’s majestic deportment and immeasurable retinue descending into the maṇḍala and standing to the left.]
With single-minded devotion, we invoke the Great Brahmā King, Śakra Devendra, the Four World-Protecting Kings, the eight classes of devas and nāgas,
together with all their retinues.
We pray that you will not violate your original vow, but out of compassion for sentient beings, descend upon this ritual site and protect and maintain the consecrated boundary.
(The assembly joins in harmony to invite you with incense and flowers.)
I now respectfully proclaim and universally summon the mantras of the eight classes of beings;
may you deign to grant your protection. Oṃ sarva-deva-nāga-ānuli svāhā.

(Having recited the mantra three times, strike the gong. [The Dharma Master visualizes the immeasurable retinues of the eight classes of devas and nāgas descending into the ritual arena and standing to the right.]
With single-minded devotion, we invoke the great deity of merit who protects the True Dharma within this monastery at this dwelling place,
together with all his retinues.
We pray that you will not violate your original vow; out of compassion for sentient beings, guard the site of practice and protect the consecrated boundary.
(The assembly chants together: "Invitation with Incense and Flowers.")
I now respectfully proclaim this mantra of invocation. May you deign to bestow your protection.
Oṃ bhubhūri karitari tathāgatāya. (Having recited the mantra three times, strike the ghaṇṭā.

[The Dharma Master visualizes that the various deities of the monastery arrive at the entrance of the ritual hall and stand on both sides. The family of noble lineage should now invoke this position.]
With single-minded devotion, we entreat the City God of this district, the various temple lords and kings, the deities residing in the six directions,
the ancestral spirits of our households, and all their retinues.
We pray that you will not violate your original vow; out of compassion for sentient beings, guard the site of practice and maintain the consecrated boundary.
(The assembly invites you with harmonious incense and flowers.)
I now respectfully proclaim this mantra of invocation. May you deign to bestow your protection.
Oṃ buburi karitari tathāgatāya. (Recite the mantra three times; then strike the cymbals.

[The Dharma Master visualizes that the Six Deities residing in the city walls and various temples arrive at the entrance of the ritual arena and stand on both sides. (The Ritual Master addresses them as follows:)

Having been summoned as above, you have already graced us with your presence, surrounding the ritual site like dense clouds. With hearts full of courageous resolve, may you all arise to provide protection and support.
Please wait but a moment while we perform the rite of boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*).

(The Dharma Master visualizes the Infinite Vajra. The eight classes of devas and their retinues each array their weapons and encircle the four directions, guarding the interior and exterior of the *maṇḍala*. The ritual master rings the bell and recites verses, addressing the holy sages to perform the rite of boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*).
First, he binds the boundaries of the site.)

I reverently address the assembly of the Triple Gem of the ten directions, The Myō-ō and Ejisō with their majestic spirits, Brahmā, Śakra, and the Four Heavenly Kings, And the eight classes of devas and nāgas—may you all protect and mind me.
Today I shall perform an offering of universal equality; I pray that this ground may be made extraordinary and unlike any ordinary dwelling.
One must rely upon spiritual power for empowerment; may this pure radiance be equal to a buddha-field.
Now, reciting the *Kīli-krodha-mantra*, I empower this pure water and sprinkle it upon this ground to bind the boundary of the site.
May it be prayed that beneath this ground, for a depth of one hundred *yojanas*, it shall be like pure lapis lazuli, forever free from defilement and impurity.
Oṃ kili kili vajra-vajri budha pānta pānta hūṃ phaṭ. (Ki: pronounced as in "knee. Hūṃ:
pronounced as in "hu-jin" [rhyme]. Phaṭ: pronounced as in "po. Vajra: pronounced as in "ri").

(The表白 [officiant] holds two bowls filled to the brim with well-water. Having recited the mantra seven times, he sprinkles the water all around the ground. (The 法師 [Dharma Master] follows the preceding words of aspiration and visualization. (The 表白 speaks his declaration and subsequently binds the boundaries of the cardinal directions.)
I now recite the Heart Mantra of the Vajra Family. Empowering pure water, I sprinkle it in the four directions to bind the boundaries of the cardinal points.
May it be prayed that within this maṇḍala, the four surrounding directions shall be like a vajra city wall—firm and impervious to violation.
Oṃ vajra-dhṛk (light tone). (The ritual master recites this mantra seven times while holding the water vessel.

Having finished, he sprinkles the water in the four directions of the maṇḍala. The Dharma Master, following the preceding words of aspiration, visualizes [the boundary]. The ritual master says: "I three times bind the realm of empty space.")
I now recite the Susiddhi mantra and empower this sublime incense, which perfumes the atmosphere and binds the realm of space.
I pray that above this void, extending for more than a hundred yojanas, clouds of incense shall spread everywhere like a great precious canopy.
(Above are the three mantras for boundary-binding,
all derived from the Susiddhi Tantra. Oṃ susiddhi-kāri-jvalita-dhāna-mumura-ke-aye jvala jvala bandha bandha ka-ra-ka-na.
*Huṃ hūṃ phaṭ*. (The *baibiao* [officiant] burns incense, holds the censer, and recites the mantra seven times.
Holding the censer, he circumambulates the ritual site and fumigates the air. (The Dharma Master follows the preceding words of aspiration and visualization. (The *baibiao* speaks:)
The preceding boundary-binding ritual has been completed. The space above, below, and in the four directions is vast, majestic, and pure, like the buddha-fields of all the Buddhas.

It is filled with great radiance and is worthy of being offered to the Sages; it is fit for the opening of a Dharma assembly. We pray that all the worthy and holy ones will solemnly protect this site of practice.
May no malevolent spirits or demons dare to cause interference.
(The Dharma Master and the patron offer incense and recite the petition to invite the Great Being, saying:
We respectfully hear that the Holy Avalokiteśvara, in times past, when first dwelling in the First Bhūmi, encountered the Tathāgata Thousand-Rays-King.
He preached for them the Great Dharani of the Vast, Perfect, and Unobstructed Mind of Great Compassion, so as to bring great benefit to sentient beings.
At that time, upon hearing this mantra once, the Great Being immediately transcended to the eighth stage (*bhūmi*).
Up until the present time, when Śākyamuni Tathāgata and all the Bodhisattvas gathered together on Mount Potalaka, it was only this Great Being who stood face-to-face [with the Buddha].
The Tathāgata, with a heart of great compassion, has proclaimed these verses and phrases so that they may circulate throughout the world; there is no one who does not receive benefit.
You should know that this mantra is like a wondrous medicine called agada, which cures every kind of illness without exception.
Therefore, for those who recite this mantra, there is no karma of the three evil realms that it does not destroy, and there are no Buddha-lands where they cannot be reborn.
Their merit is so lofty and sublime that it is beyond all praise. On this day, we have accepted the invitation of the donor to establish a *bodhimaṇḍa* and perform offerings of equality.
First, we shall universally summon all deities to this site and carry out the rite of boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*) to ensure its solemn purity.
Therefore, at this time, we again reverently invite the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas to employ the power of mantras to once more apply consecrated water,
thereby augmenting their supreme efficacy to an inconceivable and vast degree, so that all sentient beings may universally attain liberation.
With single-minded devotion, we entreat the Great Compassionate and Benevolent Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara,
the Thousand-Armed and Thousand-Eyed One (three times).
We pray that you will not forsake your original vow; out of compassion for sentient beings, descend upon this ritual site and empower the consecrated water.
(The assembly joins in harmony with incense and flowers to invite you.)
I now recite the Great Dharani of the Heart of Vast, Perfect, and Unobstructed Great Compassion, as proclaimed by the Holy Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara;
may you graciously grant your protection.
Namo ratnatrayāya. Namo ’ryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya. Oṃ sara phaṭaye svāhā.
Nata-śe | Namo siddhārthāya īmo ’rya-vairocanāya namo narendrāya kṣe li mahā-bhaṭṭāra-samai sarva-athā-tuṣpauṃ aśiye sa...
Vasada namo vasada (these five characters are absent in the Tibetan version) namo bhagavate tadyathā oṃ aparāhite lokate karate ihele mahābodhisattva sarvasarvamāramā.
Rāmahe maheridave, kulu kulu keṭaṃ, dudu dudu vaśaje,
mahāvaśaje, dhara dhara dharani, śivaye, cara cara mamava mara.
Mùdì luè | Īhī īhī | Śiṇā śiṇā | Araṃ buddhaśarīra | Phaṣa phaṣaṃ | Buddhaśaye | Hulū hulū mara hulū hulū hīrī | Sara sara | Sirī sirī | Suru ||
Sulu bodhaye bodhaye, buddhaye buddhaye, maitriye, nara-kṣi,
dharisaniya, bhagavān svāhā, siddhaye svāhā, mahāsiddhaye svāhā.
Vaha siddhye svāhā | Nara-caye svāhā | Mara-nara svāhā | Sarva-sam-āmukhaye svāhā | Sarva-mahā-asitāye svāhā |
Vaha jīrā-asitaye svāhā | Padma-agrasite svāhā | Nārakṣe-bhagavate svāhā | Māphale-śaṅkare svāhā | Namo-harad... svāhā ||
Tadraya | Namah Arya Valokiteśvarāya Śvaramaya Svāhā | Oṃ (in the Tibetan manuscript) Siddhantu Mantradharapadaye Svāhā.

(Recite the mantra three times while holding the water basin and making the formal announcement. (The Dharma Master visualizes the Great Being seated upright in the ritual arena, emitting light from between his eyebrows that enters this water to manifest his sacred function. Regarding this mantra, those who have transmitted it in the world have lost six characters.

It is now excerpted from the *Qianshou Qianyan Dabeijing* (The Sutra of the Thousand Hands, Thousand Eyes, and Great Compassion) in the Tripitaka, so that the reciter may have the mantra complete and expect its sacred efficacy. (The Dharma Master and the patron offer incense.
(The Reciter makes the formal announcement, requesting Vairocana Buddha, saying:)
I reverently hear that the Holy Avalokiteśvara, for the sake of the great assembly, requested Śākyamuni Bhagavān to explain how all the Vairocana Tathāgatas of the lands of the ten directions,

at one and the same time, each extended their right hand to touch the crown of the head of the Pure Lotus King of Radiance (Vimalapadmavajraprabha-rāja) and together recited the mantra of the Great Empowerment Light of Amoghasiddhi. If there is...

Regarding the ten evil deeds, the five heinous crimes, and the four grave offenses committed in the past: if one hears this [mantra] twenty-one times and it passes through the faculty of hearing, they shall immediately be extinguished and eliminated.
Even if sentient beings have accumulated various evil karmas and, upon the dissolution of the body at the end of life, fall into the various evil realms, [they shall be liberated].
By means of this mantra, we empower earth and sand and scatter it upon the bodies [of the deceased], as well as upon their stupas and tombs.
Should those who have passed away be in the evil realms, they shall immediately receive light and a body at that very moment;

all retributions for their sins shall be eliminated, and their suffering bodies shall be reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss, never again falling back until they attain Bodhi. On this day, we have accepted the invitation of the donor.

He established a site for practice and cultivated offerings of equanimity. First, he universally summoned all deities to this place and performed the rite of boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*) to purify and adorn it, as well as to respectfully invite the Noble Avalokiteśvara through the verses spoken with great compassion.

Add more water to increase its superior efficacy. Therefore, at this time once again, with single-minded sincerity and reverence, invoke the Tathāgata Vairocana of the ten directions to empower this water with the light of consecration (*abhiṣeka*), so that its power may be doubled and further enhanced.
Thereafter, sprinkle this most excellent water of the Dharma throughout the maṇḍala, both inside and out, at this site.
It is not the case that whether it be the faculties or the objects, a single drop or a single touch does not cause radiant light to burst forth. One should know that this very place is a pure land;

one should know that on this day the Wheel of Dharma may be turned. The worthies and sages of the ten directions will all arrive like clouds, and the multitudes of living beings in the six realms will all hasten there.
The gift of the Dharma shall be widely opened, universally delivering those wandering in delusion; throughout the entire dharma-realm, all shall receive its grace.
Liberation!
With single-minded devotion, I entreat all the Vairocana-Abhāva Tathāgatas of the lands of the ten directions (three times).
I pray that you will not violate your original vows, but out of compassion for sentient beings, descend upon this site of practice and empower the consecrated water with your spiritual power.
(All present, invite with incense and flowers:
I now recite the Great Empowerment Light Mantra of Amogha, as taught by the Tathāgata Vairocana.
May you grant your protection.
Oṃ (1) vīramatī (2) mahāmuditāmaṇi (3) padmarūpa (4) para... (5)
Vat-kya-ya (5). (The Ritual Master holds the water basin and recites the mantra seven times.

(The Ritual Master visualizes the Tathāgatas of the ten directions seated in a circle within the *bodhimaṇḍa*, together emitting the light from the white tuft between their brows which enters this water to manifest their sacred power.

The wording transmitted by the people of the world is often incorrect; I have now transcribed this excellent version based on the *Amoghapāśakalparāja-sūtra* found in the Tripiṭaka. (The Ritual Master addresses the assembly:)
Thus far, we have invoked the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, as well as the Vidyārājas and devas, each of whom bestows their majestic spiritual power upon us.
As we recite and uphold the mantras without transgressing the rules, this consecrated water gains great efficacy.
This very dharma-gate fully manifests the three virtues; it is like a lapis lazuli jewel, pure and luminous, free from all defilement and obstruction—this is the Dharma.
The virtue of the body (*kāyaguṇa*) is like a wish-fulfilling jewel (*cintāmaṇi*): it rains down all treasures, such that nothing is lacking; this is the virtue of wisdom (*prajñāguṇa*).
Being sovereign in every direction and free from all obstructions, it is like a wheel-turning monarch (*cakravartin*); this is the virtue of liberation (*vimokṣaguṇa*).

Since the mantra possesses these three virtues and the water likewise possesses these three virtues, the mantra is entirely water and the water is entirely mantra. Essence and function are non-dual, being one and the same secret treasury. I now...
With these three virtuous secret treasury mantras, sprinkle pure water upon this site—within and without the *maṇḍala*, above and below, and throughout the four directions of the central land.
Wherever the water reaches, it shall become a consecrated boundary (*sīmābandha*). One should then make this aspiration for this place, the *maṇḍala*:
Through the power of these offerings—incense, flowers, food, drink, and all manner of services—each one is produced in measureless abundance.
By the power of performing these ritual ceremonies, every sense organ and sensory object of the assembly of śramaṇas becomes pure.
By virtue of this power, the bodies and minds of every person who serves as a patron for the *zhāi* (fasting) ritual shall become radiant and pure.

Even those coming and going from beyond the boundaries of the realm—whose bodies and robes may be impure, or who have consumed pungent meats or strong-smelling vegetables, whether intentionally or by mistake—who should enter the *daochang* (sacred precinct), shall be transformed into purity through the power of the mantras. All malevolent spirits and heretics...
As for "Ti" (those who revile): those who disparage the Triple Gem and delight in creating obstacles shall, through the power of this mantra, all give rise to the aspiration for enlightenment.
Whether they praise or slander, both serve as conditions [for liberation]. Contemplating the mind in this way is what is called "universal deliverance.
Furthermore, relying upon the assembly, recite the mantra together and sprinkle the ritual water everywhere.

(Recite the Great Compassion Mantra (*Mahākaruṇādhāraṇī*) while making the formal announcement. Holding a water vessel, lead the assembly forward, sprinkling water everywhere. This applies to places where food is prepared outside the ritual site, to the invitation ceremony, to the bathhouse, and to all locations passed through during the procession. (The Dharma Master holds an incense burner.)

The master of ceremonies leads the patron behind him and returns to the site of the ritual (the *daochang*). (The *biaobai* [officiant] addresses the various sages and worthies, proclaiming the intent. (The *biaobai* addresses the assembly: "On the left side of the *daochang*, with the patron on the right, you should each collect your minds and listen attentively as questions are posed.
(The Dharma Master stands upright in the center and poses the questions.)
The day is auspicious and the hour is favorable. We shall inaugurate this Dharma assembly. With solemn reverence for the rites of purification, what is our intention?

I venture to request that the patrons and the great assembly each listen attentively. Now we shall perform the Great Purificatory Assembly for the Universal Salvation of the Holy and the Profane of the Water and Land throughout the Dharma Realm;
by this, its name is established. Since this name has been established, it must have its underlying meaning. If the name and its meaning are correct, [the rite shall proceed].
This alone is our present school. What is meant by the "Dharma-realm"? It is because the principle is eternally one, and because the nature of all Buddhas and sentient beings is equal.

What is meant by "sages" and "ordinary beings"? It is because there are ten distinct matters. Buddhas and those of the three vehicles are called sages; the various living beings of the six realms are called ordinary beings.
Although there are ten matters, the principle is eternally one. What is meant by "water" and "land"? This refers to the "retributive environment" (*niśraya-vipāka*).

The six classes of ordinary beings have three bases upon which they rely: namely, water, land, and air; these are all places where retribution is experienced. Now, when "water and land" are mentioned, "air" is necessarily included.
Furthermore, because suffering is more intense in these two [specific] locations, they are emphasized. What is meant by "universal deliverance"? It means there is no one who is not delivered.

Although the six realms of existence differ, they are all equally liberated. What is meant by the "Great Fast"? It is because food is bestowed; for whether noble or ordinary, there is none who is not provided for.
What is meant by the "Supreme Assembly"? It is because the Dharma is bestowed; for within the six mundane realms, beings receive supreme benefit.

Since the names and meanings are thus correctly established, what are their respective positions? It is said that the upper and lower halls each have ten positions, and each position is further divided into ten, totaling two hundred.
This encompasses everything; it is detailed rather than abbreviated. As for the quantity of food, it follows the intention of the donor.

The ranks shall neither increase nor decrease; this is the established rule. Now, in instituting these laws, let there be no doubt. One must distinguish between what is in accordance with the Dharma and what is not.
The virtue of the precepts is lofty and far-reaching, while the path of contemplation is profound and subtle. If one fails in even a single point, one cannot be called a Dharma Master.
One who places faith in the Triple Gem and contemplates the suffering of the six realms—such a person who gives rise to this resolve is called a donor.

Their movements and conduct follow the Dharma, and their Brahma-voice is heard afar. If there is even one thing that does not accord with this, they cannot be said to uphold the texts. They skillfully know the proper measure, possessing both the principal and the subordinate.
It is thus appropriate; this is called an assembly of the Dharma. By binding the boundaries and maintaining purity, one prohibits the unwholesome.

If there is even one who does not conform, it cannot be called a *bodhimaṇḍa*. When incense and lamps are fully arrayed and delicacies and provisions are complete, such purity and refinement constitute the act of making offerings.
I venture to inform the donors: whether they be others or myself, we should act in accordance with the Dharma and remain far removed from all faults.

What is being performed now is no small matter; it honors the Four Noble Ones above and extends to the six classes of ordinary beings below, providing equal offerings to all at once, leaving none unserved.
The pervasive fragrance of the wind of *dāna* (generosity) can be seen herein. One who is able to practice this true Dharma-offering does not rely on the mind and does not dwell upon signs.
To "not dwell upon signs" means to transcend emotional attachments while illuminating the principle. Practicing giving in such a manner possesses a merit and efficacy that is beyond compare.
There is no one who gives, no one who receives the gift, and no intermediate object; all are ultimately empty.
Yet the giver, the receiver, and the object given are all perfectly manifest—these are inconceivable designations, neither existent nor non-existent, and neither not-existent-nor-non-existent.
The simultaneous extinction and simultaneous illumination constitute the ultimate non-referential Middle Way. Such a Dharma-giving shall continue until the end of the future;
the Dharma-realm is eternally harmonious, being solely the Three Truths.

(When the questions have been concluded, the assembly exits the maṇḍala. Since deities are densely arrayed at this site of boundary-binding, one should maintain profound reverence and awe. One must first instruct a diligent, trustworthy, and pure attendant to guard it strictly, ensuring that no miscellaneous persons enter or exit and thereby defile the pure realm.
After the assembly has finished with tea and soup, they proceed to the entrance and issue the talisman.

Performing the Ritual for Dispatching the Talismanic Messengers (First, set up the positions for the four talismanic messengers at the entrance. Prepare tea, hot water, fresh fruit, and offerings of money and horses. Then, on a separate table, arrange the petitions for invitation, memorial documents, talismanic warrants, and official notices. Once this is complete, the assembly strikes the *neng* and *ba* cymbals).
(The Dharma Master and the ritual assistants take turns offering incense. The *biaobai* [officiant] speaks as follows):
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and entreat the Buddhas, Dharma, and Sangha of the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm—
the eternally abiding Triple Gem.
(The ritual master holds the incense burner, rings the bell, burns incense as a sign of sincerity, and addresses them thus:)
Fragrance arises from the mind; the mind reaches out through fragrance. It does not abide within the three periods of time, yet it can pervade the ten directions.

Although this is so by the very nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), it is also brought about by the power of the donor. Therefore, the Buddhas hear this and bestow their protection, while all sentient beings receive its perfuming influence here.
Desiring that the full manifestation of supreme benefit be realized, one further recites the secret mantra to assist in its revelation.
The Tathāgata, our Buddha, possesses the *Dhūpa-dhūpita-saṃpratyaya-mantra*. I shall now reverently recite it:
Oṃ śvalitadhūmani aprakoṭa suparṇi vikacche huṃ.

(Recite the mantra three times. Ring the cymbals. (The Dharma Master visualizes that these clouds of incense pervade the entire Dharma-realm, so that all sages and worthies are fully aware of them and give rise to hearts of joy.
(The ritual officiant takes a portion of the previously consecrated water into a separate vessel, which has been prepared beforehand on a table, and at this point addresses it as follows:)
Jeweled vessels shimmer with brilliance; numinous springs flow and ripple. Through the three secret empowerments, one sprinkling brings refreshing coolness.

Thus, the four seats are magnificently adorned, and purity extends throughout the ten directions. Far removed from dust and free from defilement, one moves the sages and attracts the worthy—truly, this is the time for such a moment.
To personally practice this Way,
I shall now reverently recite the Buddha Tathāgata’s mantra for sprinkling and purifying: Oṃ vaśira śameye hūṃ phaṭ siri mahi.

*Saha* (recite the mantra three times; ring the cymbals). (The ritual master sprinkles water from the vessel onto the four seats, circling once around each location). (The Dharma Master visualizes that wherever the water reaches, it becomes pure, radiant, and established as a consecrated boundary [sīmābandha];
then, ringing the bell, he makes this declaration):
I have humbly heard that the Buddha, the King of Awakening, out of compassion for those suffering like the "Flaming Mouth" (Yan-kou), first commanded the offering of the ritual vessel (*hu*).

Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty, moved by the dream of a divine monk, subsequently initiated the practice of the *zhai* (vegetarian feast). Although it specifically bears the name "Water and Land," it in fact provides equal offerings to the assembly of both the holy and the ordinary.
Thus, one adds reverence toward the Triple Gem and arouses compassion for all classes of beings, reaching from the highest heavens to the lowest earth without exception.
What interval exists between those realms and this boundary? All who dwell in different destinies alike manifest true cultivation;

thus, by entrusting the matter to manifold rituals, one must ensure the success of universal salvation. Now, we reverently follow the Inner Teachings and respectfully adhere to the sacred regulations.
To open a Dharma assembly for the salvation of the deluded masses is surely the exclusive responsibility of the presiding master;

yet, to knock at the celestial gate and issue the great proclamation truly relies upon the messenger. Therefore, I respectfully intend to welcome you, hoping that upon hearing my call, you will arrive immediately.
With a sincere heart, we extend this invitation to the swift messengers who carry talismans of the Four Heavenly Kings, who possess sovereign spiritual powers and immeasurable majesty,
together with all their retinues. We pray that you will not fail your original vows, but out of compassion for sentient beings, descend upon this Dharma assembly at this very moment.
(The assembly offers incense and flowers with a request; strike the gongs. The following sections follow this pattern.
With a sincere heart, we respectfully invite the swift-moving dūtīs who hold the talismans, whose supernatural powers are sovereign and whose majestic virtue is immeasurable.
Together with all your retinues, we pray that you do not violate your original vows, but out of compassion for sentient beings, descend upon this Dharma assembly at this very moment and time.
We most sincerely entreat you— O messenger who travels the earth with swiftness, wields talismans, possesses sovereign spiritual powers, and whose majesty and virtue are immeasurable.
Together with all your retinues, we pray that you do not violate your original vows, but out of compassion for sentient beings, descend upon this Dharma assembly at this very moment and time.
We most sincerely invite you, O swift messenger who bears the talisman to the underworld, whose supernatural powers are sovereign and whose majestic virtue is immeasurable.
Together with all your retinues,
I pray that you do not fail your original vow, but out of compassion for sentient beings, descend upon this Dharma assembly at this very moment.
I shall now reverently recite the invocation mantra of our Buddha, the Tathāgata.
Oṃ buburī karītrī tathāgatāya (Recite the mantra three times; strike the cymbals).

[The Dharma Master visualizes that each messenger arrives from the sky with hundreds of thousands of retinues and stands in their respective positions]. (Ring the bell for a short while during the prose recitation; praise their virtues and state the purpose).
Clouds gathered around the banners and standards; the wind moved through the ranks of the retinue. It was as if they had descended from the Nine Heavens and were lingering amidst the four seats.
We hope Your Radiant Presence will pause for a moment, so that we may humbly convey our sincere devotion.

We respectfully venerate the Four Great Envoys: self-reliant and tireless, attaining spiritual power through the One; when employed, they act with efficacy; majestic yet not fierce. With frost-like robes and silent insight, they have already passed through...

Pervading the myriad regions, your jade-like feet have traveled afar, traversing billions of lands. As I humbly fulfill my duty of presenting these words, I am all the more mindful of your exceptional talent for diplomatic mission.
You have wonderfully manifested supernatural powers and truly mastered the skillful means of expedient teachings.
On this day, there is a Great State (and so forth).

On the fifteenth day of this month, [Name and Title of the Host], respectfully convenes at [Location] the Great Assembly of the Universal Deliverance of the Holy and the Profane through Water and Land Offerings for the Dharma Realm.

This is specifically undertaken to fulfill [the fulfillment of a heart’s vow], to repay the four debts of gratitude, and to universally deliver all sentient beings so that they may together attain liberation.
(Adapt the following according to the specific intent. Now, the holy and the profane hold different conceptions, and the realms of the unseen...
To manifest these divergent paths, how could they be fully understood without relying on emissaries? Therefore, at this juncture, I summon all the deities;
I trust that in your wisdom you will surely be able to comprehend the details.
(Recite the *baibiao* and ring the bell while distributing the food. Address them as follows:
"This mind creates the food; the entire food is the mind. Because essence and function are not distinct, one attains mastery over contraction and expansion."
Thus, the six sense-objects mutually pervade one another, and the three virtues are eternally fused. Subtle and inconceivable, they give rise to the inexhaustible.
Relying upon the path of contemplation and secretly supported by the permeation of mantras, may this skillfully guide the ritual procedures and enable the perfect accomplishment of the Dharma-gift.
Now I shall recite the *Dhāraṇī of Immeasurable Majestic Virtue, Sovereign Radiance, and Supreme Wondrous Power*, and empower [this place].
May the Dharma-food be made to pervade everywhere.
Namo sarvatathāgatavajriṇe | Oṃ | Sambhara sambhara hūṃ.

(When the assembly has finished reciting the mantra seven times together: (The ritual master sprinkles purified water upon the food. (The ritual master visualizes that these offerings of food produce various sublime offerings of the six sense objects, which are presented all at once, lacking nothing.
(The ritual master rings the bell while presenting the food and speaks:)
The fragrance of the precepts is richly perfumed; the water of meditative concentration is clear and still. The lamp of wisdom shines brightly, and one possesses the food of dhyāna-joy.
The flower of cause and practice has first blossomed, and the fruit of the true nature is already perfected. One who can contemplate in this manner is performing a Dharma-offering.
I now proclaim these secret words to hasten the arrival of the divine spirits; please grant us a moment of leisure and deign to accept our offerings.
I shall now reverently recite the True Mantra for Presenting Offerings to the Buddha Tathāgata.
Oṃ gaganasambhava vajra hūṃ. (Recite this mantra three times; then ring the bell.

[The Dharma Master visualizes that these offerings are fully presented before him. All the deities descend to partake, none of whom fail to rejoice. (The Dharma Master rings the bell for a short time and entrusts the matter to the messengers.)

The essence of the sages and the common folk is the same; it is only the minds of delusion and awakening that differ. Now, in performing this ritual of purification (zhāi) and extending our invitations, some may say that the responses to these calls are inconsistent.

They argue that while the abodes of the Triple Gem and the various devas can certainly be reached in a single thought-moment, among the classes of sentient beings within the six realms, there are those who do not hear even after repeated calls.
This is because those with heavy evil karma are still lingering in the midst of their suffering, as well as those possessed by false views.
For the majority, this constitutes a self-imposed obstacle; it does not depend on the agility of others to facilitate the donor’s arduous efforts.

As for submitting formal petitions to the Brahma King, recording their sentiments and compositions for the sake of Śakra, and aligning with the presiding authorities of the Underworld and Mount Tai, as well as the various deities of the city walls and local territories—all shall reverently embody supreme compassion and immediately offer [their support].
A great amnesty shall be proclaimed, extending the vast and boundless grace of the Sage to liberate those imprisoned in the evil realms.

Let all hasten forward and not allow themselves to retreat. In this way, the hosts of devas, humans, and asuras, as well as the multitudes of ghosts, animals, and those in the hells, shall rely upon the merit of this timely ferrying across to dissolve the karma of saṃsāra accumulated over billions of kalpas.
Thus, may the supreme transformation be greatly honored, and may we fortunately encounter this long [enduring] [blessing].
I hope that you will further elucidate this through your wisdom and faithfully abide by what has been entrusted to you. Do not delay even for a moment;

ensure that the sealed instructions are fully understood and that no violation occurs, lest you bring blame upon yourselves. Whether in the various realms of the Buddha-lands or the celestial palaces, each must be diligent in its respective office.
The human realm and the underworld are divergent paths; each must fulfill its appointed duty. Those who are muddled and ignorant are exhorted by means of the Way;
those who are violent and obstinate in their self-will are restrained by means of majesty. Should there be a request, I shall surely come; there is not one thing that I do not attend to.
All my intentions are fully contained within these ritual symbols (fuwen). I command you to proclaim them separately; pray deign to listen.

(The two monks step forward and stand to either side of the messenger’s seat. They read the documents and present the petitions in order: first for the Four Heavenly Kings, then for the Sky-Walkers, then for the Earth-Walkers, and finally for the Underworld Officials.

Two persons alternate in reading these four sections; many people must not read them at once in a chaotic manner). (The ritual master rings the bell, dispatches the spirit messengers, and speaks as follows):
Without being summoned, he moves with swiftness; when there is a resonance, there is penetration. His majestic bearing is like the radiance of the rising sun;

his supernormal power (ṛddhipāda) is comparable to the vigor of celestial travel. Mounting a cloud-chariot and raising feathered streamers, he gallops and hastens, exhausting the precious flames and penetrating to the wind-circle.

It is fitting for you to ascend and fitting for you to descend. I pray that you will not disregard my command. You must skillfully compose your parting words. This matter involves much toil and trouble; according to propriety, you ought to see me off.
The Buddha Tathāgata possesses a mantra for dismissal; I shall now reverently recite it.
Oṃ māraya mukhaṭṭa mukha. (Recite this mantra three times. Then, ring the gong and cymbals.

(Take the petition for performance, the written documents, and other materials, arrange them together, and burn them. The ritual master vibrates the bell to escort them. The Dharma Master visualizes that the four spirit-messengers take charge of the entrusted texts; having received their mandate, they immediately depart throughout the worlds of the ten directions.)

Once everything has been thoroughly understood, the talismans and the positions of the ritual officers are withdrawn, and the assembly proceeds to partake of refreshments. Upon reaching the entrance, the invitation is issued and the documents for the paper money and horses are burned.

These must be burned using clean paper along with firewood and charcoal; it is strictly forbidden to use lamps or candles to ignite them. It is heard that in the Netherworld there are piles of wax money, and the guardians say: "When people in the human world burn paper money, they often use candles to ignite it; therefore, oil-stained paper must not be used, as it accumulates here.
Furthermore, one must not use a stick to stir and crush the offerings, as such actions involve transgressions. It is appropriate to instruct those who are unaware to practice accordingly.
