The Ritual for Inviting the Assembly to Ascend the Dharma Seat (At the entrance, arrange the purification path with incense, flowers, banners, pennants, and candle lanterns; the assembly strikes the gongs). (The Dharma Master and the patrons offer incense). (The表白 *biaobai* [the ritual officiant] recites:)
With a sincere heart, we take refuge and pay homage to the Buddhas, Dharmas, and Sanghas of the ten directions and the entire Dharma-realm (the harmonious assembly).
To the eternally abiding Triple Gem.

(The Dharma Master and the donor simultaneously perform their prostrations. (The Ritual Official vibrates the bell, holds the incense burner, and recites the verse and mantra for lighting the incense.)
Contemplate this wondrous fragrance as the law of dependent origination: Primordially without substance, it is the great void of true emptiness;
Pervading everywhere, it is entirely clouds of fragrance. This inconceivable state is the sublime provisional;
Neither existent nor empty, all dependencies are severed; Simultaneously negating and simultaneously illuminating, the "middle" must necessarily vanish.
Relying upon the wondrous incense of the mind of Madhyamaka, I today diligently perform this ritual offering.
I shall now reverently recite the mantra for burning incense for our Buddha, the Tathāgata.
Oṃ śvalita mani aprakoṭa supharaṇi vikaci huṃ. (Recite this mantra three times; strike the cymbals.
[The Dharma Master visualizes clouds of incense filling the Buddha-fields of the ten directions, so that all sages and worthies universally arouse their protective mindfulness.
[The Ritual Official rings the bell and recites the verse and mantra for sprinkling purification.]
The nature of water is true emptiness, pervading the Dharma-realm; It is serene within a single vessel, inconceivable in its manifestation.
If both emptiness and conventionality are simultaneously transcended, The meaning of the Middle Way is ultimately and fully revealed.
By contemplating the mind in this way, one merges with the waters of the Dharma; Through these waters of the Dharma, all defilements are purified.
Whether as a support or as the true radiance of complete exhaustion, it penetrates the ten directions without obstruction.
I, the Buddha-Tathāgata, possess a mantra for sprinkling purification; I shall now reverently recite it.
Oṃ śavara śmāye ṅa-phe śrī-mahi svāhā. (Recite this mantra three times; strike the cymbals.

(The ritual master scatters flowers upon the purified path and sprinkles water in the four directions, above, and below to purify the paths. (The Dharma Master visualizes that wherever the water reaches, it becomes a consecrated boundary, solemn, pure, and vast.)

Extensive. Furthermore, visualize the pure path as clouds of light, with tens of millions of pavilions stacked one upon another. (The ritual master vibrates the bell and recites the invocation verse.)

I prostrate to the Unsurpassed Awakened Ones of the ten directions; To the Bodhisattvas of Great Resolve and the Mahāyāna Saṅgha who perfectly expound the three aspects of doctrine, practice, and principle;
To the assembly of the Three Jewels of Pratyekabuddhas and Śrāvakas;
And to the lineage patriarchs known as the Four Reliances who transmit the teachings, along with the celestial beings, the eight classes of spirits, and the divine kings.
I now universally deliver [beings] by establishing this altar; I pray that you extend your compassionate light to grant me secret certification.

(The Text for Invocation) I humbly submit that neither being identical nor different is how one observes with the Buddha-eye; Neither "sage" nor "ordinary person" exists—this is the nature of all phenomena.

The realms are one; subject and object are both quiescent in wisdom. The essence and its function are mutually dark and harmonious, like a box and its lid fitting together, or water and its waves being inseparable.

When it comes to expounding the teachings according to the times and establishing provisional means for the sake of the ultimate truth, although many gates are distinguished, they ultimately point back to the single path.
Thus, principle is perceived through phenomena, and transformation arises according to the capacities of beings. Within the state where all dependencies have ceased, it is certainly not...

Delving into the discourse on transcendence (*li*) and subtlety (*wei*), one reveals the nature of the true cause (*zhengyin*). This necessarily relies upon the cultivation of the conditional (*yuan*) and the contributory (*liao*) causes.

Therefore, by offering bright lamps and flowers, bowing the head and joining the palms, one seeks to adorn the myriad practices (*wanxing*) so that the three bodies (*sanshen*) may be perfected in their wondrous completeness.

Thus we know that while traces are manifested within the conditioned (*youwei*), they ultimately return to the source in the unconditioned (*wuzuo*). Only then can one reverently observe the Great Norm (*hongfan*) and honor the common way.
With many ritual observances, we honor the pure fasts of both land and water, extending universal salvation to the very limits of earth and heaven.

This ocean of wondrous offerings receives all streams and becomes ever deeper; this grove of supreme merit sprouts a thousand branches, all flourishing together. Now, a particularly auspicious assembly is convened.

Respectfully honoring the Compassionate Honored One, we invite within those who embody the four means of integration (*saṃgrahavastu*), and gather without those who manifest as noble practitioners of the two vehicles (*dviyāna*).

We summon the host of immortals possessing the five supernatural powers (*pañcābhijñā*) and the assembly of the eight classes of celestial beings. As they sit upright upon this magnificent seat, may they graciously partake of these fragrant delicacies.

Since the mind of giving has been opened and awakened wisdom is all-pervasive, we respectfully perform the rites of invitation; we pray that you will deign to descend and grace us with your presence. (The *biaobai* recites:)
With single-minded devotion, we invoke all the eternally abiding Buddhas of the ten directions throughout the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm,
together with their retinues,
and the Vairocana Buddha of the pure Dharma-body.
The Perfect Reward Body, Vairocana Buddha;
the thousand billion transformation bodies, Śākyamuni Buddha;
and the Greatly Compassionate and Merciful Amitābha Buddha of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss.
The Tuṣita Heaven Palace; Maitreya Buddha, who is in his final birth before enlightenment and shall descend to be born in the future;
and all the Buddhas of the past, such as the Tathāgata Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū.
The present Buddhas, such as the Buddha Śubhavyūhapadmottaraśrī; all present Buddhas;
and the future Buddhas, such as the Buddha Padmaprabha and the Buddha Padmavṛṣabhavikrāmin; all future Buddhas.
The Buddhas of the ten directions and the dharma-realm, such as the Buddha Good Virtue of the East;
all the Buddhas of the past Adornment Eon, beginning with the thousand Buddhas starting from the Buddha Flower Radiance.
The present Bhadrakalpa begins with the thousand Buddhas starting from Krakucchanda Buddha;
the future Tiṣya Kalpa begins with the thousand Buddhas starting from Sūryaprabha Buddha.
Throughout the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm, to all the precious stupas containing the whole-body relics of all Buddhas:
we pray that you will not violate your original vows, but out of compassion for sentient beings, descend upon this Dharma assembly at this very moment and time.
(The assembly unisonously offers incense and flowers; strike the gongs.)

(The Dharma Master visualizes the Buddhas of the ten directions mounting their precious thrones; they arrive spontaneously without being invited, filling the void of space and appearing with perfect clarity. Although those Tathāgatas are always capable of responding, it is truly through the power of my own mind that they are invoked.)
Yet this ability to evoke [the response] truly depends upon the mind’s possession [of the capacity]; it is through the mind’s possession that the response is evoked, not from anything external.
With single-minded devotion, I invite all the eternally abiding honored Dharmas of the ten directions throughout the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm, together with their retinues.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha’s Great Vaipulya; the Brahmajāla Sūtra on the Precepts; the various Dharma-treasures of the sūtras;
and within the assembly at the Deer Park, the Buddha’s collected original practices, the four Āgamas, and other such Dharma-treasures of the sūtras.
The various assemblies of the Vaipulya sūtras; the *Vimalakīrtinirdeśa*, the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa*, and other such sūtras—these precious dharmas of all the scriptures;
the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā* and the *Ratnaketudhāraṇī* (Jinwang), the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā*, and other such sūtras—these precious dharmas of all the scriptures.
The Mahāyāna Sūtra of the Lotus of the Wonderful Law, the Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra,
and various other precious Dharma treasures of the sūtras that exclusively discuss the Pure Land, such as the Sūtra on the Meditation on Amitāyus Buddha, and so forth.
The Dharma-treasures of all the Mahāyāna and Hīnayāna teachings spoken during the five periods, the various Vinaya texts and Śāstras,
and the sūtras, treatises, commentaries, and sub-commentaries composed by the noble ones of the three vehicles in India and this land.
Secreted within the dragon palaces and not yet arrived from the land of Zhuyi (India), there are all the Dharma-treasures of the sutras, vinayas, and śāstras;
and throughout the lands of the ten directions, from the waterfowl to the trees and forests, every speck of dust and every world-system proclaims the sounds of all dharmas.
I pray that you will not violate your original vow, but out of compassion for sentient beings, descend upon this Dharma assembly at this very moment and time.

(The Dharma Master should contemplate that the great thousand-fold world-system scrolls spoken by the Buddhas of the ten directions contain boundless paths of teaching that can open up wondrous understanding; these are the scriptures of teaching. Teaching is *prajñā*, for it is through the wisdom of *prajñā* that the teachings are expounded.

Furthermore, one can clearly illuminate all the gates of practice (*caryā*) explained in the various sutras; by practicing in accordance with them, one will surely attain the fruit. These are the scriptures of practice. Practice is liberation (*vimukti*), for the function of liberation arises from conditions.)

Furthermore, one knows that the boundless paths of teaching, all gates of practice, and the constant essence of every dharma are themselves the true aspect (*bhūtalakṣaṇa*). This constitutes the Sutra of Principle. Principle is the Dharma-body (*dharmakāya*), because the principle of the Dharma-body is that which is manifested.

Now, although these—teaching, practice, and principle—have three names, they do not deviate from a single essence. Those who cultivate the perfect contemplation attain this within a single mind. When performing this contemplation: it is the Ultimate Truth (*paramārthasatya*) as taught through wisdom;

it is the Conventional Truth (*saṃvṛtisatya*) as practice arises from conditions; and it is the Middle Truth (*madhyamasatya*) as one realizes this true aspect. These three truths are a single mind without before or after or distinction; this is the perfect realization of the three inconceivable Sutras. Moreover, one must clearly contemplate the eternal abiding of the ten directions.

The *Immeasurable Life Sūtra* constantly emits radiance; free from defilement and pure, it has manifested at this site of enlightenment in response to my invitation. This manifestation is brought about by my own capacity to evoke it, as well as by its inherent presence.
With single-minded devotion, we invoke all the ever-abiding Bodhisattva Saṃghas of the ten directions throughout the entirety of empty space and the pervasive Dharma-realm,
together with their retinues:
Mañjuśrī and his eighty thousand great beings, the Great Master Samantabhadra, and the boundless Bodhisattvas.
Avalokiteśvara, Mahāsthāmaprāpta, the assembly of great bodhisattvas of the Pure Sea,
Bhaiṣajyarāja, Bhaiṣajyasamudgata, and all the great bodhisattvas within the Lotus Sūtra.
The Bodhisattva Bhadramukha; the various great bodhisattvas in the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*;
the fifty-three spiritual friends and bodhisattvas whom Sudhana visited;
and the Bodhisattva Śraddhālakṣaṇa, along with the various great bodhisattvas in the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa Sūtra*.
The inner court of Tuṣita, where the great Bodhisattvas such as Asaṅga and Vasubandhu reside;
the Land of Ultimate Bliss, where the great Bodhisattvas who are in their final birth before Buddhahood dwell;
and the Dharma assemblies of the five periods, where the great Bodhisattvas assist in proclaiming the Buddha’s transformation.

I pray that all Bodhisattvas throughout the stages traversed by the *Zang*, *Tong*, *Bie*, and *Yuan* teachings, not violating their original vows, will take pity on sentient beings and descend upon this Dharma assembly at this very moment today.

(The Dharma Master should visualize the Bodhisattvas of the ten directions, each seated upon a lotus throne; though they do not come, they come, filling the void of space so clearly that they are visible. All the worthies and sages of the various ranks below this should likewise arouse a mind of resonance, possessing two meanings.)
Visualizing with focused concentration,
I single-mindedly invoke all the eternally abiding Pratyekabuddha Sanghas throughout the ten directions, pervading the entirety of empty space and the Dharma-realm,
together with their retinues.

In the *Benevolent Kings Sūtra for the Protection of the State*, it is said that when a Buddha appears in the world, eight million billion great seers and pratyekabuddhas come from the mountains; five hundred such pratyekabuddhas arrive.
After the extinction of the Buddha-dharma, seven hundred koṭis of pratyekabuddhas will appear simultaneously;
these are the great pratyekabuddhas who, having lived during the time of a Buddha, heard the Dharma and attained the Way.
The great pratyekabuddhas who attain enlightenment spontaneously in a world where no Buddha has appeared;
the pratyekabuddhas and solitary realizers who travel in groups or like a rhinoceros horn in a world where no Buddha has appeared;
and the pratyekabuddhas and solitary realizers who possess or do not possess the [major] marks.
Pratyekabuddhas and pratyekajinas who manifest supernatural powers and those who do not;
Pratyekabuddhas and pratyekajinas who preach the Dharma and those who do not;
pratyekabuddhas of the Shared Teaching who have attained the eighth stage, and pratyekabuddhas of the Tripitaka Teaching.
I pray that you will not violate your original vow, but out of compassion for sentient beings, descend upon this Dharma assembly at this very day and hour.
(The Dharma Master visualizes the Pratyekabuddhas of the ten directions, their majestic deportment solemn, as they arrive through the void.)
With single-minded devotion, we extend our invitation to all the eternally abiding Śrāvaka Saṃghas throughout the ten directions, pervading the entirety of empty space and the Dharma-realm,
together with their retinues:
from the five bhikṣus first delivered at the Deer Park to Subhadra, the last of the Arhats.
The World-Honored One’s eminent disciples— the ten great disciples such as Mahākāśyapa and Ānanda—
and the assembly of twelve thousand great bhikṣus who were arhats, all heard the Dharma on Vulture Peak.
The great assembly of śrāvakas, both those on the stage of training and those beyond training, who received their predictions at Vulture Peak;
the great assembly of śrāvakas, both those on the stage of training and those beyond training, who heard the Dharma during the five periods.
After the Parinirvāṇa of the World-Honored One, the Three Piṭakas were compiled by Ānanda and other Arhats;
sixteen great Arhats remained in the world, along with a community of sixteen thousand nine hundred disciples.
At Fangguang Monastery on Mount Tiantai dwell five hundred great arhats who possess unimpeded wisdom and realization, and who have attained the three gates of liberation;
they comprise the six types of arhats, including those who progress by faith and those who progress by dharma.
The practitioners of the Shared Teaching (*sādhāraṇa-śāsana*) have already completed their realization of the nature of phenomena.

The learners (*śaikṣa*) and non-learners (*aśaikṣa*) of the Tripitaka Teaching, as well as the seven groups of noble ones among the internal and external assemblies—may you not violate your original vows, but out of compassion for sentient beings, descend upon this Dharma assembly at this very moment today.
(The Dharma Master visualizes the Śrāvakas of the ten directions, solemn in their majestic deportment, arriving from the void.)

With single-minded devotion, we invoke all the ancestral masters and monks of the various schools of Chan and Vinaya who have transmitted and upheld the teachings throughout the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm,
together with their retinues;
as well as the twenty-three patriarchs of the West who transmitted the teachings, beginning with Kāśyapa, Nāgārjuna, and the Venerable Siṃha.
The Venerable of Northern Qi; the Chan Master of Mount Nanyue; the Great Chan Master Zhizhe of Tiantai;
the Venerable of Zhang’an; the Venerable of Jingxi, and the other nine patriarchs; as well as the Great Master Fazhi of Siming.
The Chan masters of the Dharma lineage, beginning with Bodhidharma and Yuanjue Chanshi, down to the Sixth Patriarch and other great Chan masters;
as well as the great Chan masters of the five schools: Linji, Guishan, Dongshan, Yunmen, and Fayan.
Dharma Master Yuanwu of the Lotus Society at Mount Lu; the various Dharma masters who attained rebirth in the Pure Land throughout successive generations;
National Teacher Guo Yi, the founder of the Xianshou school; and the great Dharma masters Qingliang and Guifeng.
The Great Dharma Master, founder of the Cien school; the State Preceptor of Empowerment for Yoga and Esoteric Buddhism;
the tenth patriarch of the Vinaya school; the Vinaya Master Nanshan Chengzhao; and the Great Wisdom Vinaya Master, the author of the *Abhidharmakośa-bhāṣya-ṭīkā*.
Kāśyapa Mātanga and Dharmaratna, who translated the scriptures; the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang and other Dharma masters who sought the Dharma:
I pray that you will not violate your original vows, but out of compassion for sentient beings, descend upon this Dharma assembly at this very moment and on this very day.
(The Dharma master visualizes the various patriarchs descending from the void with solemn and majestic deportment.)

With single-minded devotion, we invoke those throughout the ten directions and the entire realm of phenomena who assist in proclaiming the Buddha’s transformation: the Vidyādharas, the authors of treatises, and the siddhas possessing the five supernatural powers, together with their retinues;
as well as the Buddhas of the ten directions of the past and the siddhas possessing the five supernatural powers who practiced together with us on the grounds of the path in former times.
In the past, when Śākyamuni Buddha was on the causal ground, he practiced together with a thousand holy kings and seers possessing the five supernatural powers.
In the past, Śākyamuni Buddha practiced together with a seer possessing the five supernatural powers who had perfected patience.
The sage Gautama of the Śākya clan who protected and nurtured [the Buddha]; the sage Asita who divined the marks of the Prince;
the various devas of the Form Realm who descended to the human world to receive the Way; and the sages possessing the five supernormal powers.
The assembly of spiritual friends within the Avataṃsaka; the ten thousand great seers of Vimu-kusa;
the place where the Wheel of Dharma was turned in the Deer Park; and the ancient seers of Vārāṇasī.
He invited the ninety-nine thousand five hundred ṛṣis of the Cloud-Rain Assembly who possess the five supernatural powers,
as well as the sixty-eight great ṛṣis, including Aṣṭaka and others, to the assembly of the Vaipulya Sūtras.
Throughout all lands, those great ṛṣis who have mastered various incantations and composed treatises on the five sciences—
may you not violate your original vows, but out of compassion for sentient beings, descend upon this Dharma assembly at this very hour and moment.
(The Dharma Master visualizes the ṛṣis of the ten directions, possessing the five supernatural powers, appearing from the void with solemn and reverent countenances and attire.)
With single-minded devotion, we invoke the Ten Great Vidyārājas of the ten directions and the dharma-realm, the Vajra of Impure Traces and all the great celestial kings,
the various devas who protect the Dharma, together with their retinues.
The ten Great Vidyārājas, such as the Great Majestic and Immovable Honored One; the Holy One, Vajra Kṣitigarbha;
and the various celestial kings from the Avataṃsaka Assembly, such as the Great Sovereign Heavenly King of the Ocean of Wondrous Flames.
The Great Brahmā Heaven King of the Palace of Sublime Adornment; Śakra Devendra, Lord of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven; Vaiśravaṇa, the Heavenly King of Abundant Learning;
Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the Heavenly King Who Upholds the Nation; Virūḍhaka, the Heavenly King of Increase; and Virūpākṣa, the Heavenly King of Broad Vision.
Mahādevī, Mahāpuṇyadevī, Mahāprajñādevī, the Mother of Devas Mārīcī, the Vajrapāṇi Guhyapada Śrī-rāja,
the Great General of the Northern Heaven, and the Honored Deva Saṃjñeya.
To the South Celestial General Vajrapāṇi; to the Bodhi Tree Goddess Bhṛkuṭī;
to the Great Earth Sovereign, the Firm Earth Deity; to the Yakṣa General Nandika; and to the Goddess Haritī.
The Great General Vaiśravaṇa, together with the twenty-eight divisions of majestic and powerful celestial deities under his command—
the eight classes of beings, including humans and non-humans, devas, nāgas, and so forth— who heard the Dharma from the Buddha at the assembly of the Lotus Sūtra.
I pray that you will not violate your original vow, but out of compassion for sentient beings, descend upon this Dharma assembly at this very moment and on this very day.

(The Dharma Master visualizes the countless hosts of devas and heavenly deities—some joyful, some wrathful, their dignified demeanors manifold—who, having heard this invocation, arrive from the void.)
With single-minded devotion, we invoke all the great divine kings who protect the Buddha’s śarīra, stūpas, and monasteries throughout the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm,
as well as those who, through fasting and precepts, guard the nation and pacify the household, together with all their retinues.
The four great military commanders, Pañcika, Pāṇḍaka, Cūḍapanthaka, and Ariṣṭa, protect the Buddha’s relics.
The twelve great divine kings, including Dṛḍhaprabha, Vimalameghasvara, and others, protect the *sīmā* (ordination platform).
The five great divine kings, such as Śūlamani-bhadra, protect the Buddha-stūpas.
The eighteen great divine kings, such as Surūpa, Brahmaghoṣa, and Dundubhisvara, protect the saṃghārāma.
The *Viśvakarman* devaputra protects the land of Zhendan (China). The Great General Kāpiḷa, the goddess Amitāyus, and all the hosts of spirits protect those who have received the Three Refuges.
Mṛḍu-pīlu and others protect those who observe the Five Precepts.

Cāru-bhi-yūthani... [protects]... (Note: The final term *cāru-bhi-yūthani* appears to be a transliteration of a proper name or deity title; its precise meaning remains uncertain based on the provided fragment.)
The great divine kings such as these protect the bhikṣus;
the one hundred and seventy-two great divine kings such as Kāma, Kāla, and Khareti protect [the Dharma] after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa;
and the seven divine kings such as Taradatta protect the disciples of the Buddha.
They guard the palaces and residences. These are the chief spirit-kings of the five directions, such as Aśvaka of the east;
they observe the human realm during the six fast days, and each of the Four Heavenly Kings has ninety-one sons and eight great celestial generals.

O swift messengers of the Four Heavenly Kings, I pray that you do not violate your original vows, but out of compassion for sentient beings, descend upon this Dharma assembly at this very moment today.
(The Dharma Master visualizes the majestic and solemn countenances of the various spirit kings; hearing this invocation, they arrive from the void.)

With single-minded devotion, we offer this invocation. To those who propagate the teachings for both land and water beings and disseminate the supreme doctrine— the ten great bodhisattvas who established the rituals and laws,
together with their retinues who propagated the *śrāddha* (food-offering) rites and disseminated the supreme doctrine— and to the Venerable Ānanda, the holy teacher.
Initially, he manifested a dream to encourage the establishment of the Water and Land rites.

The venerable holy master, the divine monk of the Liang dynasty, exhorted [the Emperor] to compose the ritual for the Water and Land rites. [This was done by] the venerable holy master, Master Zhigong of the Liang dynasty.
The Ritual Manual for the Water and Land Feast was first established by the Sovereign of the Nation, the World-Saving Bodhisattva Emperor Wu of the Liang Dynasty.
He upheld the Dharma and proclaimed its texts. During the Liang era, the Vinaya Master Master You served as the presiding master.
The Ritual for the Zhongxing Water-Land Feast was established by Chan Master Fahaing of the Tang Dynasty, who was known as Loushi due to his total mastery of dhāraṇīs and his spiritual responses;
it was later transmitted by Chan Master Foyin of the Song Dynasty.
He meticulously finalized the ancient rituals and clarified the methods of the *zhāi* fast.
Chan Master Jí of Chánglú cultivated and honored these fasting rites, painting portraits and composing hymns of praise for them. The Grand Preceptor Sū Wénzhōng (Sū Shì) likewise did so.
Following the ancient rites, I have composed this text for circulation in the world.

Yang Gong, the Judicial Commissioner of Dongchuan, sincerely prays that you will not violate your original vows, but out of compassion for sentient beings, descend upon this Dharma assembly at this very hour on this very day.
(The Dharma Master visualizes that the Great Beings, whose power of aspiration is profound and weighty, having heard this invocation, immediately descend to attend.)
Above, we have invoked the Triple Gem of the Hall, the ten classes of holy sages, and the infinite multitudes; a single thought can move them, and their sacred response is manifest.
We shall further recite the secret mantras to express our earnest reverence.
Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses a mantra for invocation. I shall now reverently recite it:
*Namāḥ samantabuddhānām | oṃ uccapratīhata ti sarvadhātugarbha kuśamati oṃ śrīyamūlaprakāya sa* (I shall now reverently recite the mantra for invocation of our Buddha, the Tathāgata:
*Namo samantabuddhānām | Oṃ uccapratīhata ti sarvadhātugarbha kuśamati oṃ śrīyamūlaprakāya sa*)

*Ha* (recite the mantra three times; strike the gongs). (The Dharma Master visualizes that the Triple Gem, the various devas, and all holy sages have been summoned from above and have gathered like clouds, dwelling within the precious pavilion upon the pure path, their radiance intermingling and reflecting one another without obstruction.
He addresses them, saying:)
May the Honored Ones of the Secret [Teachings] deign to grace us with their presence together. The donor takes refuge and prostrates with utmost sincerity.
(The Dharma Master performs three prostrations together with the patron. (The Ritual Official invites all the Sages and Worthies to approach for the ritual bathing, speaking as follows:)
The adamantine true essence—how could this not be the firm and dense body? The pure light of the jade-hair—this is the mark of ultimate reality.
Ultimately, it is primordially stainless; one should know that where, then, is there any person? This is the exposition of the gateway of bathing.
Desiring to cleanse the defilements of worldly toil, we hope that you will turn your lotus-like eyes to look down upon our devotion as a sunflower inclines toward the sun.
We pray you will preside over the sacred rites and graciously attend the Warm Bath ceremony.

(Lanterns, banners, flags, incense, flowers, and offering implements precede the assembly. The congregation leads the way to the purification path and proceeds to the bathing area. The ritual officiant arrives before the bathhouse and presents the bathing offering, saying:)
The Lotus Treasury Ocean is perfected in its very essence; flowing springs and bathing pools manifest everywhere.
How profound and clear is the water of eight virtues! How majestic is the Dharma-body of five parts! One must know that the Buddhas do not originally wash away dust;
rather, they desire to cause all sentient beings to leave defilement behind. Imagine receiving this consecration: like the seal of the night moon upon a tranquil pool, it manifests all things.
With dignified deportment, as the morning sun ascends the distant heavens, he reverently proclaims the secret words and requests to bathe in the hot springs,
thereby manifesting the Dharma-gate without violating worldly truth.
Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses a bathing mantra. I shall now reverently recite it:
*Oṃ tiṣya tiṣya saṃgha svāhā*. (Recite this mantra three times.

The assembly vibrates the cymbals and offers songs of praise. The ritual master proceeds to the bathhouse to perform the purification. (The Dharma Master visualizes that this bathhouse is composed of the seven precious jewels, vast, magnificent, and pure, where all the sages and worthies accord with the donor’s offerings.)
The intent of offering the bath is for all [the Buddhas] to enter therein and bathe. (The ritual master rings the bell and proclaims the verse:
The Dharma-body of all Buddhas is eternally and fundamentally wondrous; Adorned by the conditions and causes, it is tranquil yet ever-illuminating, Transcending words and thought;
Like an echo responding to a valley, there is nothing to which it does not respond.
I look up once more to the Three Vehicles and the Eight Classes of Beings;
Manifesting compassion and majesty to benefit all according to their needs, How profound are the many gates of skillful means! All arise from the Great Expedient Power of Compassion and Wisdom.
On this day, as we practice the fast and extend universal salvation, The worthies and sages of the ten directions descend like clouds.
I perform this ritual bathing to accord with the eternal rites;
Thoroughly understanding that the Sage’s body is fundamentally free from defilement, The vast pool of his precepts has no bounds, And the tranquil waters of his concentration are ever full.
By washing away the stains of the mind, one attains refreshing purity, So as to cause all sentient beings to awaken to the wondrous realization.
(When the Sage and Worthies have finished bathing, the Ritual Master [biaobai] rings the bell and announces:

Having bathed the Vajra-body of the Tathāgata, he manifests in a manner identical to that of worldly beings; donning the precious and regal robes of Vairocana, he adorns his sublime and extraordinary countenance.
Now that the Great Sage has arrived, it is certain that his entire retinue has also assembled. Thus, like stars spread across the heavens...
The Bodhisattvas were like a dense mist surrounding the Śrāvakas; the Brahma King held a parasol aloft in the sky, while Śakra scattered flowers upon the ground.

Flying banners led the way, and sounding music followed behind, hoping that [the Buddha] would deign to descend to the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) so that the rites of the fast might be solemnly accomplished.

(The assembly shakes the cymbals. Guided by those of dignified demeanor, they proceed to the ritual arena. They circumambulate the path. The Ritual Director rings the bell and, presenting the precious seat, makes this declaration:)

Now that the Sage and the Holy One have arrived, I consider that the seating arrangements have not yet been made solemn. Illuminating the subtle contemplation of the mind within the Middle Way, one realizes that the Dharma-nature has no abiding root.

The entire body is fully manifested and arises in every thought-moment; lion thrones fill the void of space, and jeweled flower pedestals pervade all lands, none of which are not lofty and vast, all possessing radiant light.
I look up with hope for your compassion and pray that you will deign to descend.
Regarding the place of reception:
My Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses a mantra for offering the precious throne.
I shall now reverently recite it: Oṃ vimagha padma-sunārī dhara-dharani maṃ.

*Narai hūṃ* (Recite this mantra three times while striking the cymbals). (The Dharma Master visualizes that the site of practice is vast, expansive, and pure; immeasurable jewel thrones fill the entirety of space, upon which all the holy sages dwell. (The Ritual Master addresses the assembly, saying:)
By citing a single fragrance, the three contemplations are fully elucidated. Thus, when one realizes true emptiness, there is neither nature nor mark;
yet, by relying on wondrous provisionality, it becomes a canopy and clouds. Without departing from the mind of dependent origination, the principle of the Middle Way is fully manifested.
With this Dharma-offering, may the sincerity of the common person be reached; by chanting the numinous texts, may their superior utility be further augmented.
The Tathāgata, our Buddha, possesses a mantra for burning incense.
I shall now reverently recite it: Oṃ akara akara sarvabuddhādhyeṣaṇīye svāhā.

(Recite the mantra three times. Strike the gongs. (The Dharma Master visualizes that these clouds of incense produce immeasurable palaces of the seven treasures, ritual implements, clothing, exquisite music, wonderful flowers, and ambrosial delicacies, which are simultaneously offered before all the sages and worthies, pervading everywhere without exception.
(The officiant offers flowers and speaks as follows:)
It is only when the myriad flowers are in full bloom that they manifest the adornment of the ten thousand practices.
Therefore, faith and understanding plant the roots, while diligence causes the branches and leaves to flourish.

Having moistened them with the water of meditative concentration and brushed them with the wind of wisdom, one nurtures the grove of one's own merit, thereby manifesting the originally inherent fruit of perfect reality.
The Tathāgata, our Buddha, possesses the Flower-Offering Mantra.
I shall now reverently recite it: Oṃ akara akara sarvabuddhādhipataye svāhā.

(Recite the mantra three times. Distribute flowers around the seats of the sages while the assembly strikes the gongs. (The Dharma Master visualizes that the offered flowers give rise to palaces and towers made of the seven treasures, exquisite garments and necklaces, celestial music and wonderful incense, ambrosial delicacies, and various kinds of ritual implements—layer upon layer, inexhaustible—which are simultaneously offered before each of the sages and worthies, pervading everywhere without exception. He then sprinkles water for purification and speaks as follows:)
Within a single vessel of water, the three truths are fully contained. Thus, when its nature is discussed, it is rooted in ultimate emptiness;
yet according to its application, it manifests as wondrous conventionality. Neither of the two extremes can be established, and the middle way cannot be fixed.
Relying on the harmonious integration of perfect contemplation and aided by the secrets of mantra, this seat is purified and the sense faculties and their objects are cleansed. All of these...
To clarify the mind through phenomena, the essential point lies in forgetting emotional attachments to illuminate the principle.
The Buddha Tathāgata has a mantra for sprinkling purification;
I shall now reverently recite it: Oṃ vaśira śamaye hūṃ phaṭ siri mahi svāhā.

(Recite the mantra three times. Ring the gong. The ritual master sprinkles water from the vessel onto the sacred seats. (The Dharma Master visualizes that the water reaches every seat and all the offerings, making them all pure and radiant. The ritual master proclaims the intent and declares:)

We respectfully invite the Triple Gem and assemble all the devas; having already established ourselves within the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), we further seek their witness to this rite of purification.
We must rely upon the purport of these written instructions to express our own sentiments. Standing reverently before you, we humbly pray that you will deign to hear us.
(Having finished reading the intent, the officiant offers a formal prayer:
We look up and cast ourselves upon the venerable realm, reverently laying bare our humble sincerity. Such a petition is truly earnest.

As we reflect upon the period of this cultivation and veneration, we acknowledge many faults of simplicity and negligence; whether it be that the presiding master lacked the virtue required, or that the donor...

Whether it be due to the narrowness of my mental application, or a lapse in the ritual procedures of the *maṇḍala*, or a deficiency in the ceremonial observances of the offerings—truly, I rely upon Your Great Compassion to slightly forgive these manifold transgressions.
May You graciously accede to this petition from one of inferior wisdom, hoping thereby to establish the conditions for universal salvation.

Those whose merit and retribution are meager already fear they may not even hear [Your voice], so how could those whose karmic offenses are most grievous ever reach You? [I] command the Brahma King...
A general amnesty was proclaimed. He charged Śakra with bestowing grace and dispatched the swift and agile classes of beings to take charge of the messengers.
He ordered that all beings of the seven realms of existence be assembled at once;

even prisoners whose crimes were heinous and unpardonable were to be granted relief, and those whose karmic burdens bound them together were all made to arrive. For indeed, the Omniscient One constantly manifests universal response; therefore—
The pure light shines forth, leaving no hidden place unilluminated; sustained by your supernatural power, what suffering could not be uprooted?
We venture to pray that you, in your majestic dignity, will wait but a moment to accept our pure fast, so as to fulfill our most earnest aspiration.
We, the assembly, are overcome with the utmost sincerity and urgency in our supplication, trembling with trepidation.

(Strike the cymbals. (The Dharma Master, the assembly, and the patrons temporarily withdraw for refreshments; however, one person of sincere devotion must be specifically appointed to guard the ritual site, ensuring that no outsiders violate the prohibitions of the fast.

(After a short while, the Dharma Master leads the patrons back into the ritual site to offer incense. Strike the cymbals. (The Ritual Official takes up the incense burner, rings the bell, and recites verses.)
I take refuge in the Three Honored Ones, unsurpassed; may the celestial beings and the eight classes of spirits together bestow their compassion upon me.
Now, relying on the teachings, I observe the pure fast; having recited the secret mantras, I first offer the universal food.
(The Declaration of the Universal Food).

Contemplate this food with discernment: it does not exist apart from my own mind. Because one knows that all phenomena are eternally interfused, the six sense objects are found to be mutually pervasive.
This is the supreme flavor beyond even clarified butter (ghṛta), proclaiming the pure fragrance of sandalwood; it rains down the seven treasures in profusion.
Scattered flowers bloom with brilliant radiance, towering above the luminous halls and palaces. Exquisite and magnificent carriages are arrayed in rows;
celestial music resounds through the void, with the sounds of flutes and stone chimes alternating in harmony. Celestial robes gather like mist, and pearl necklaces hang down in adornment.

Because every thought-moment is perfectly fulfilled and never deficient, these various manifestations of splendor are inexhaustible. Within this very site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*), they appear in profusion.
The rituals and ceremonies are so numerous that clear water and bright lamps are offered, banners are suspended and canopies raised;
the sound of golden bells shakes the deep valleys, and the resonance of *brahmā*-chants thins the high heavens—all of these enter this school, for they are fundamentally nothing other than this.

As for realizing the wondrous Dharma before one's eyes and contemplating the permanence of worldly phenomena, the chirping of magpies and the cawing of crows are all, in their entirety, profound discourses on Prajñā.
The mountain streams and the hues of the landscape are none other than the total manifestation of Vairocana. Throughout past and present, one’s own numinous spirit remains unclouded;

from the ultimate environment to its inhabitants, all constitute the offering of Dharma. Each exists as the wondrous provisional, with a nature that is fundamentally true emptiness. Illuminating both extremes simultaneously, the Middle Way is fully revealed.
By employing the perfect contemplation of the One Mind to support the esoteric words of the Three Virtues, one may rely upon this power of auxiliary manifestation.
With the intention of awakening [the seeds] through perfuming and so forth,
I now recite the *Dhāraṇī of Immeasurable Majestic Virtue, Sovereign Radiance, and Supreme Wondrous Power*,
empowering this ritual food so that it may pervade everywhere.
*Namo sarvatathāgate vairocani oṃ sambhara sambhara hūṃ.* (The assembly recites this mantra twenty-one times in full.
As the Sūtra states:

"If one wishes to make offerings to the Triple Gem, one should empower incense, flowers, food, and drink with this mantra twenty-one times; they will then become celestial delicacies of supreme flavor to be presented as an offering.")

The Triple Gem of the ten directions is thereby brought to fulfillment through the perfection of *dāna-pāramitā*. (At the conclusion of the mantra, ring the cymbals. (The ritual master sprinkles water over the food, ensuring it is distributed everywhere.

(The Dharma Master should know that food is the *dharmadhātu*, possessing all phenomena; therefore, one can visualize this pure food as producing various kinds of ambrosial, supreme flavors and diverse delicacies. As in the previous section on the universal offering of food, the six sense objects interpenetrate and fill the entire *dharmadhātu*.

Furthermore, knowing that the adornments of the environment and its inhabitants—all phenomena—are, when viewed through wondrous contemplation, equally offerings of the Dharma, one simultaneously presents them universally before the Triple Gem of the ten directions and before the celestial beings, sages, and worthies, such that there is nowhere they do not pervade. (The ritual master rings the bell and makes this offering, saying:)
It is solely this one mind; it is solely this one food. Because there is only food, all dharmas tend toward food;
because there is only mind, all forms tend toward mind. When this mind is dissolved, form is also dissolved. That which is equal regarding dharmas is also equal regarding food.
This is the universal entry into the three periods of time, its nature eternally abiding. Vastly encompassing the ten voids, its substance is perpetually pervasive.
Because its nature eternally abides, not a single thought arises; because its substance is perpetually pervasive, it does not move from its own place.
