Constantly hearing the Mahāyāna, advancing toward Bodhi, entering the Buddha’s knowledge and vision,

and cultivating the merit of fasting offerings— these are performed in honor of and in praise of those from my high ancestors and great-great-grandfathers back through the generations of my forebears, including their births, livelihoods, and various arts and crafts.
Having established this body, I rely upon it to perform these posthumous honors, increasing merit and virtue through the cultivation of the *zhāi* (fasting) ritual.
I respectfully dedicate this to my biological parents to increase their blessings and open their wisdom; as for those still living in this world...
May they enjoy wealth, longevity, health, and peace. Should their spirits depart this life, may they immediately return to the Land of Peaceful Nurturing (An-yang).

Through the merit of practicing this vegetarian fast, we respectfully offer praise for elder brothers’ kindness and younger brothers’ reverence, for wives’ harmony and children’s filiality, and for the faithful upholding of family precepts.
My conduct has been virtuous and my reputation well-established. Relying upon these auspicious conditions, I pray that supreme merit may increase through the virtue of this vegetarian fast.
I hereby dedicate this to honor and support my teachers, mentors, and friends who have instructed me, both in worldly and transcendental matters.
Relying upon these virtuous words and exemplary deeds, I repay my gratitude. May supreme blessings increase through the merit of this vegetarian fast.
This offering is dedicated to those who have looked up to and praised my kindness from past lives, and those who have guided and supported me—may their official rank, emoluments, and wealth flourish.
May they attain great wealth and honor, so that by means of this they may repay their kindness;

may their supreme blessings increase through the merit of this vegetarian fast, offered in honor of our external relatives and kinsmen who were close in affection and who rescued one another in times of hardship.
Through these offerings and mutual exchanges, may we repay your kindness. May your supreme blessings increase through the merit of this fast.
We respectfully dedicate this to the Brahmā, Śakra, and the Four Heavenly Kings, and to the assembly of celestial saints, to protect and uphold the Buddha-dharma.
May the monasteries be glorified and those who have left the household life be protected, forever free from external insults.

Through the merit of practicing this fast, we respectfully offer praise to the celestial deities and terrestrial spirits, and to the true lords who roam the void, so that the three calamities may be utterly extinguished.
May the winds and rains be harmonious, may the grains and fruits ripen in abundance, and may the flora and fauna flourish.
Through the merit of this vegetarian fast, we reverently offer praise to the Heavenly Kings who protect the nation, as well as to the enshrined deities, so that they may preserve our realm.
May auspiciousness always descend. May rulers be sagely and ministers virtuous; may the four classes of people delight in their vocations.
Through the merit of this vegetarian fast, we reverently praise and honor the Spirit Kings who Guard the Dwelling, who preside over the incense and lamps, and maintain the household.
We invoke prohibitions against inauspiciousness; may the calamities of fire and theft never again be committed.
Through the merit of practicing this fast, we reverently dedicate it to extolling and supporting all men and women within the six realms of existence throughout the entire dharma-realm.
All are my parents. Relying upon this adornment, may merit increase and wisdom be opened through the virtue of practicing this vegetarian fast;
I respectfully offer praise for all the earth, water, fire, and wind, and all the environmental supports throughout the entire dharma-realm.
All these were my former bodies. By relying upon this adornment, they have been transformed into a wondrous realm.
Through the merit of practicing the fast, I offer praise on behalf of my servants and maidservants who attended me; may they receive this supreme blessing.
May they be delivered from their lowly station; truly, I hope that in future lives they may be spared the burden of mutual retribution.
The aforementioned donors, reverently before the Triple Gem, have with solemn intent set forth these thirty-two vows, fulfilling their hearts’ desire to repay kindness.
The merit of universal salvation is perfected; the myriad sentient beings of the *dharmadhātu* shall together achieve the Buddha-way.

(The Dharma Master and the patrons perform prostrations together, offer incense, and the Ritual Director recites verses to praise the Triple Gem and proclaims the memorial text. These twelve lines of verse are from the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra*.)
Solitary and without peer, he attained self-awakening without a teacher. An elephant-king among men and a teacher of the Great Dharma, the teachings he proclaims are most supreme and most wondrous.
These are the realms where all Buddhas roam, eternally unchanging; having received this true and authentic Dharma, he practices in accordance with it.
All sentient beings are the field of merit for our true protection. We praise the Triple Gem and respectfully request them to serve as witnesses.
Today, this Great Ritual of Universal Deliverance for the Holy and the Profane of the Water and Land throughout the Dharma Realm has been completed in its entirety.
All the written petitions shall now be read aloud. (Having finished reading the petitions, pray once more for the blessings and security of the patrons.)

The preceding text and commentaries have been read through to completion. I look up to you with reverence and pray that, out of your compassion, you will deign to take me under your protective mindfulness.

This disciple, [Name], humbly prays that the merit of the fast now being cultivated—which originates from a sincere heart and is directed upward to serve the Triple Gem and downward to deliver the beings of the six realms—shall ensure that my entire family and kin remain harmonious and joyful throughout the day, and that in all matters of eating, drinking, and daily life, we may enjoy auspiciousness, peace, and happiness, thereby adding luster to our ancestral legacy.

May his legacy be passed down as a prudent plan for future generations. May he enjoy longevity and well-being; may he possess both wealth and honor. May alarms of fire cease entirely, and may the tracks of bandit hordes vanish.

May every wish be fulfilled according to one's heart, and may there be nothing that is not accomplished. We, the multitude, can do no more than offer our utmost devotion in taking refuge and earnest prayer.

(These words of supplication may be adapted according to the person; they need not be used exclusively as written here. Both the Dharma Master and the patron perform prostrations. The assembly strikes the gongs for a short while, and then all withdraw.)

(When the meal is concluded, incense and lamps are set out on all seats. The assembly gathers in one place to recite the sutras. This is done in accordance with the memorial offering to the three masters who ascended the hall and the ten masters who descended from the hall, as well as the various positions at the banquet.

While the sutra is being recited, everyone must sit upright and still the mind, purify their verbal karma, refrain from engaging in worldly speech, and recite while contemplating the mind. The Patriarchs have issued clear instructions to this effect.)
The Ritual Manual for the Auspicious Assembly of the Dharma Realm’s Holy and Mundane Beings, Land and Water, Volume Two;
The Ritual Manual for the Auspicious Assembly of the Dharma Realm’s Holy and Mundane Beings, Land and Water, Volume Three.
Carefully composed by the Śramaṇa Zhìpán of Donghú, Sìmíng, during the Song Dynasty.
Revised by the late scholar of Yunqi in Ancient Hangzhou, Zuhong.

The Ritual for Summoning and Invoking in the Lower Hall (The morning of this day is for the Announcement of Pardon; the evening is for the Summoning and Invoking. The Announcement of Pardon must be performed at the fifth watch; do not let the appearance of dawn be seen).

(At the entrance, incense, flowers, banners, pennants, lanterns, and items for purifying the path are arranged. The assembly strikes the gongs and cymbals. (The Dharma Master and the patron offer incense. (The Ritual Director chants:)
With a sincere heart, we take refuge and pay homage to the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha of all directions and the entire dharma-realm (Chorus).
To the eternally abiding Triple Gem (The Dharma Master and the Donor simultaneously prostrate, recite the liturgy, ring the bell, and burn incense, saying):
What is called "incense" is the collective name for all phenomena (*dharmas*). To cite its essence: it is the complete manifestation of the three virtues (*tri-guṇa*).
If even a single particle is burned, it fully possesses all fragrances; without leaving its original location, it pervades the ten directions.
Were it not for its power to permeate (*vāsana*), how could the principle revealed by it be perceived? Now, relying upon this superior function to realize the ultimate truth, I spread this incense.
The light of infinite clouds gathers the multitudes of ordinary beings throughout the Dharma-realm. Upon hearing this summons, do not hesitate for a moment.
Each of you should exhort your followers to assemble at the meeting place in accordance with this agreement.
The Tathāgata, our Buddha, possesses the *Dhūpa-dhūpana-saddharma-pratītyasamutpāda-mantra*.
I shall now reverently recite it: Oṃ śvalitā-mate aprakūṭa suparṇi-vijaye huṃ hūṃ.

(Recite the mantra three times. Ring the hand-bell and cymbals. (The Dharma Master visualizes clouds of incense and an ocean of fragrance, which, through the majestic power of the Buddha, pervade the entire dharma-realm and reach before all sentient beings of the six realms, causing them all to become aware and to universally give rise to joyful hearts, vowing to hasten to the Dharma assembly.
(The Ritual Official vibrates the bell, sprinkles water for purification, and speaks as follows:)

Observe this water closely; it must surely have its source. Flowing incessantly from the Anavatapta Lake of one’s own mind, it enters the ocean of the *sarvajñā* (all-knowing wisdom) of the fundamental nature, which is profound, vast, and boundless.
It reaches the point where, when poured into precious vessels, they are filled to the brim; where, through the recitation of mantras, it flows forth abundantly.

It purifies these mats and seats, and cleanses those sense-faculties and their objects. Were it not for the constant convergence of the three types of wisdom as its primary principle, such would not be possible.
How could these functions be fully accomplished all at once?
Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses a mantra for consecration by sprinkling.
I shall now reverently recite it: Oṃ śavara śmīye hūṃ phaṭ śrīmahi svāhā.

(Recite the mantra three times; then strike the gong. (The ritual master sprinkles water from the vessel in the four directions, above, below, and upon the purified path, while scattering flowers upon the purified path. (The Dharma Master visualizes that wherever the water reaches, it becomes a vast, pure, and majestic boundary (*sīmābandha*);
he further visualizes the purified path as clouds of radiance, with thousands of myriads of pavilions stacked one upon another. (The ritual master rings the bell and recites the verse of invocation.)
I take refuge in the Three Honored Ones, unsurpassed;
The Great Vehicle Masters, the Noble Sages of the Four Reliances, who first established the ritual for the Great Water and Land Feast.
May the great beings who initiated the teaching and propagated it now accept my sincere devotion to this supreme Dharma, As I extensively open this great altar site for universal salvation.
Great grace, vast and boundless, inconceivable; All beings of the six realms and four modes of birth receive its bounty.

(Invocation for the Declaration) We humbly observe that there is no distinction between the holy and the mundane, for the principle of the Three Truths is fundamentally suchness. Yet, as emotion and wisdom momentarily diverge, the ten realms [of existence] arise.
Matters may differ; water is distinct from ice, yet both share the quality of moisture. The Hu are not Han, yet both are human.

One must know that as long as one does not lose what is fundamental, one can always attain its essence. When sense organs and objects arise in opposition, and things and self intersect and incline toward one another, the habits formed are not the same, and the fruits received as retribution accordingly differ.
Because the innate natures one has received are either beautiful or ugly, one consequently undergoes suffering.
There is the heavy and the light; they wander restlessly among water, land, and air, and continue incessantly through birth, death, and the intermediate state (*antarābhava*).
If one does not understand this, where will one ultimately return? The Buddha Śākyamuni, relying on the capacity of those to be saved, manifested the brilliant teachings.

Reaching the time of Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty, who established the unobstructed offerings (*asaṃvara-pūjā*), the true practice was further elucidated. This was not merely to lodge compassion and reverence within the two fields of merit, but moreover—

Furthermore, we have gathered both enemies and kin at this single assembly. As the breeze of benevolence vibrates and ripples through all, and the stream of grace flows everywhere, we hope to fulfill the profound conditions for universal salvation and thereby give rise to the supreme benefit of equal permeation.
Now, a special and auspicious gathering is held; with reverence, we pay homage to Your Compassionate Countenance.
Having assembled the followers of the Three Vehicles, we have further extended our invitation to the Eight Classes of Beings. Facing the midday sun, we solemnly observe the pure fast. We pray—

May grace descend upon the nine regions of the world, so that all classes of sentient beings may receive benefit. Having prepared pure offerings, we have successfully completed this on an auspicious night.
We lead them through the practice of Madhyamaka, from which arises the inexhaustible; we augment this with the method of *mantra*, subtle and inconceivable.
Here, phenomena and principle are harmonized, and the one and the many mutually encompass one another. By means of this giving that does not dwell upon signs, [the truth] is revealed...
Now, with a mind free of artifice, I summon the classes of devas, humans, and asuras, as well as the hosts of pretas, animals, and those in the hells.

With food endowed with color, fragrance, and exquisite flavor, I satiate their famished and empty bellies. May they cast off feverish affliction to attain coolness, and leave behind fear to find peace and happiness.
I pray that the Buddha’s light may illuminate them and his spiritual power may guide them. As soon as they hear this invocation—
Having spoken thus, he immediately adjusted his deportment and approached (while the ritual master recites the invocation):

"With single-minded devotion, we respectfully invite all from the ten directions and the Dharma-realm: the deities of the four emptinesses and the four dhyānas; the various devas of the six desire heavens; and the deities of the sun, moon, and stars."
The holy multitudes of the Celestial Bureaucracy, together with their various retinues;
the deities of the Formless Realm, such as those in the Sphere of Neither Perception nor Non-Perception; the assemblies of the Four Formless Heavens;
the deities of the Form Realm, such as those in the Heaven of Ultimate Form and the Heaven of Excellent Manifestation; and the assemblies of the Eighteen Brahmā Heavens of the Four Dhyānas.
The desire realm: the six classes of gods of the desire heavens, including the Heaven of Controlling Others' Emanations and the Heaven of Enjoying Emanations;
the Sun Deity, the Moon Deity, the Great Emperor Ziwei of the North Pole, and the Great Emperor Taimi of the South Pole.
The Seven Original Star Lords of the Northern Dipper; the Six Administrative Star Lords of the Southern Dipper;
the Nine Luminaries; the Three Terraces and the Flower Canopy; the Twenty-eight Lunar Mansions; and the Great Year Star Lord of the Twelve Palaces.
The Sovereign of the Nation is the primal mandate; he is that to which all living beings belong.

For each member of the donor family, there are the Star Lords of their natal destiny (*benming xingjun*) and the Lords of the Celestial Offices (*tiāncao fujun*), who preside over the rewards and punishments of yin and yang, and record all matters of life and death—these great celestial officials.
The Four Holy True Lords of the North Pole of the Celestial Treasury; the True Lord of Orthodox Unity and Spiritual Response of the Heavenly Master of the Han Dynasty;
the Three Officials of Heaven, Earth, and Water; the Judge Official of the Merit Office of the Celestial Treasury; and the Swift Messenger Who Travels Through Space.

I only pray that you will not lose sight of your original nature. By virtue of the Buddha’s majestic radiance, may you come this very evening, at this very hour, to attend this Dharma assembly (the great assembly harmoniously invites you with incense and flowers;
strike the *nāḍa* and *ghaṇṭā*; for all subsequent sections, follow this same pattern).

(The Dharma Master visualizes an immeasurable multitude of heavenly beings and sages of the noble path descending from the void, abiding within the pavilions atop the Pure Path. He then recites the liturgical invocation:)

With single-minded devotion, we invoke all those throughout the ten directions and the Dharma-realm: the deities of the Five Peaks and Four Rivers; the merit-bestowing spirits who dwell upon the earth and roam through the air;
the numinous temples that receive offerings; and all their retinues.
The Celestial Sovereign of Perfect Equality and Benevolent Sage of the Eastern Peak; the Holy Sovereigns of the Five Peaks; the True Lords Who Assist the Mandate of the Five Peaks;
the Great Emperor of Fusang of the Water Realms; the Kings of the Four Great Oceans; the Lords of the Sources of the Four Rivers; and all the deities of the Water Realms.
The Dragon Kings of the five directions; the assembly of dragon kings of the four seas, the nine rivers, the five lakes, and the seven marshes;
the Earth Lords of the five directions; the divine lords of the twelve celestial divisions; and the assembly of all earth deities from the Great Year (Taishui) downward.

The deities of thunder, lightning, wind, and rain; the Fire Department and the planet Mars (Mars); the deities who spread pestilence and disease; the various deities who oversee the production of medicinal herbs;
the deities presiding over the hundred grains, flowers, fruits, medicinal plants, and groves; and the various deities who govern droughts, locust plagues, and famines.
The various hosts of deities presiding over the protection of famous mountains and sites of practice (*dōjō*), cities, towns, houses, boats, carriages, bridges, and roads;

the deities of the provincial prefectures and city walls in their arrayed temples; and the hosts of feudal lords and kings associated with the ancestral shrines and spirit temples of counties, districts, mountains, and rivers.
The local tutelary deity of the donor’s residence; the six deities of the dwelling; the various deities to whom incense and lamps are offered within the household;
the Merit-Administering Official of the Middle Realm; the Monitoring Official of the Ritual Retreat; and the Swift Messenger of Earthly Travel.
I pray that you do not lose sight of your original nature. By virtue of the Buddha’s majestic radiance, may you come to this Dharma assembly this very night, at this very hour.

(The Dharma Master visualizes that an incalculable multitude of merit-bestowing deities descends from the void and takes their place within the pavilions upon the pure path. (The Ritual Master proclaims:)
With single-minded devotion, we invoke: throughout the Dharma-realm, the emperors and queens, civil and military officials, Confucian masters and sages, immortals, recluses, and all their retinues.
The four noble wheel-turning kings; the three supreme emperors and sagely sovereigns; the sage rulers of successive dynasties, including the five emperors and three kings;
the emperors and monarchs of all nations throughout the ten directions; their legitimate consorts and primary queens; and their princes and grandsons.
The Most Holy King Wenxuan; the Ten Sages, including Zisi and Mencius, the Confucian patriarchs of successive dynasties;
and the worthy ministers of all ages, such as Gao Yao, Kui, Ji Xue, Xi, Yi Yin, Fu Yue, and the Brothers of Zhou, who served their sovereigns to bring benefit to the people.
Kings, dukes, and ministers; feudal lords and the nine high officials; the civil and military officials of all generations and renowned statesmen;
the Brahman seers who originated the teachings; and the multitude of immortals from the Ten Continents, the Three Islands, and the various grotto-heavens and blessed lands.
Laozi and Yin Ling; Liezi and Zhuangzi—these sages and immortals of successive dynasties who established their words and transmitted their teachings.
Chao Fu and Xu You; Boyi and Shu Qi—these recluses of successive dynasties who did not serve kings or lords.

The monastics, both monks and nuns, who have not yet attained the fruits of the Way; the various Daoist practitioners and female crown officials who have not yet ascended to the ranks of the immortals;
civil and military officials; ladies of noble rank and titled wives; virtuous widows and exemplary women; and the women of all successive dynasties.
I pray that you do not lose sight of your original nature. By virtue of the Buddha’s majestic radiance, may you come this very night, at this very hour, to attend this Dharma assembly.

(The Dharma Master visualizes the emperors, officials, Confucian masters, practitioners of the Way of the Immortals, and the fourfold assembly of the monastic community—countless in number—all arriving through the air and taking their places within the pavilions upon the pure path. The表白 [piāobiǎo] then proclaims:)

With single-minded devotion, we extend our invitation to all beings throughout the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm: farmers, artisans, merchants, physicians, diviners, and those of miscellaneous occupations;
men and women of both noble and humble station—these ten classes of human relations—together with all their kinsmen and retinues.
Since the beginning of the kalpa of formation, the devas of the Ābhāsvara Heaven descended to become the human race.

Among the multitudes of men and women across the four great continents, the eight intermediate continents, and the five hundred minor continents, there have been noble and humble men and women throughout successive generations.
The Eastern Yi and Western Rong, the Southern Man and Northern Di; the nobles and commoners, men and women, farmers, artisans, and technicians;

practitioners of medicine, pharmacology, divination, and astrology; and the multitudes of men and women engaged in commerce as itinerant merchants or stationary shopkeepers throughout the various nations across the generations.
Sorcerers and practitioners of heterodox paths; idle hands engaged in menial crafts; officials, soldiers, and their male and female subordinates;
performers and courtesans who sell their beauty; slaves and beggars; and widowers, widows, orphans, and solitary individuals—both male and female.

Those men and women among the multitude who are devoted to loyalty, filial piety, benevolence, righteousness, wisdom, faithfulness, propriety, and ritual decorum, and who strive for excellence in human relations;
and those men and women among the multitude who are disloyal and unfilial, who are depraved, greedy, violent, and rebellious, and who act wickedly toward human relations.
The stubborn, the foolish, and the mediocre; the subtle, the gentle, the diligent, and the literary; those who understand the ten categories of human relations;
the donors, the ancestors of former generations, and kinsmen; those who have been enemies throughout kalpas—all these multitudes now attain liberation.
I pray that you do not lose sight of your original nature.

By virtue of the Buddha’s majestic radiance, may you come this very evening, at this very hour, to attend this Dharma assembly (The Dharma Master visualizes the countless multitude of men and women, as well as the ancestors, kinsmen, and even enemies from successive generations of the donors’ families, coming from the four quarters and dwelling within the pavilions upon the pure path).
(Recite the invocation: With single-minded devotion,
we reverently invite all those born from the four modes of birth and encompassed within the five destinies throughout the ten directions and the entire Dharma-realm,
including the hosts of asuras dwelling among the mountains and at the bottom of the ocean, together with all their retinues.
The asuras born by transformation in the celestial realm seize and maintain worlds and contend for power with the devas;
their merit is inferior to that of the devas, and they dwell in proximity to the sun and moon. The asuras born from the womb in the human realm [are likewise described].
The *asura*s of the ghost realm who protect the Dharma travel through the air by means of supernatural powers and enter the void.

The *asura*s of the egg-born class within the ghost realm wander in the empty space at dawn and return to dwell in the waters at dusk. The *asura*s of the moisture-born class within the animal realm likewise [behave in this manner].
To the north of Mount Sumeru, at a depth of twenty-one thousand yojanas into the ocean, is the host of the Rāhu Asuras.
To the north of Mount Sumeru, at a depth of forty-two thousand yojanas into the ocean, is the host of the Valiant (Vīryavanta) Asuras.
To the north of Mount Sumeru, entering the ocean eighty-four thousand yojanas, is the host of the Mālādhara asuras.
To the north of Mount Sumeru, entering the ocean one hundred sixty-eight thousand yojanas,
is the host of the Vemacitra asuras.
The inferior class of asura hosts dwell upon the ground amidst the mountains of various forms;
the asura hosts who reside in the hollows, jewel cities, and within Mount Sumeru are their constant abodes.
I pray that you do not lose sight of your original nature. By virtue of the Buddha’s majestic radiance, may you come this very evening, at this very hour, to attend this Dharma assembly.
(The Dharma Master visualizes that immeasurable hosts of asuras arrive from the four directions and take their places within the pavilions upon the Pure Path. The presiding priest proclaims:)

With single-minded devotion, we invoke the King of Ghosts from the *Yankou* (Feeding the Hungry Ghosts) ritual throughout the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm; all hungry ghost assemblies of the three grades and nine classes;
wandering spirits who died untimely deaths; and their respective retinues.
He initiated the *Yankou* (Feeding the Hungry Ghosts) rite for the King of Ghosts and his retinue of hundreds of thousands of nayutas of ghost hosts as numerous as the sands of the Ganges,
including flying yakṣas, earth-walking rākṣasas, and the various ghost hosts of yakṣa and rākṣasa females.
There are thirty-six kinds of hungry ghost hosts who eat fragrance, eat water, eat vomit, and eat blood.
Five hundred yojanas beneath Jambudvīpa lies the realm of the hungry ghosts presided over by Yama.
Within the Cakravāḍa Mountains, where neither sun nor moon are seen, there dwell the hosts of hungry ghosts who must repay their past karmic debts.

Among these hosts of hungry ghosts, those with great wealth possess superior power; those of middle grade experience both gain and loss; and those of inferior grade obtain only what they must eventually discard.
Those with little wealth: the superior class have large goiters; the middling class have foul-smelling hair; the inferior class have needle-like hair.

As for the various classes of hungry ghosts (preta): those without wealth have the superior class with foul-smelling mouths; the middling class with needle-like throats; and the inferior class with torch-like mouths. As for the various classes of hungry ghosts: [the classification continues as above].
In the air, by the seashore, in mountain valleys, at burial mounds, among grasses, trees, filth, and impurities— there dwell the hosts of *preta* (hungry ghosts) who suffered thirty-six injuries,
those who died untimely deaths or premature deaths, and the hosts of *preta* whose solitary spirits remain stranded and whose souls are lingering.
I only pray that you will not lose sight of your original nature. By virtue of the Buddha’s majestic radiance, may you come this very evening, at this very hour, to attend this Dharma assembly.

(The Dharma Master visualizes a boundless multitude of hungry ghosts, some arriving from the four directions and others emerging from beneath the earth, as they take their places to one side. (The officiant proclaims:)
With single-minded devotion, we invoke the King Yama of the ten directions and the dharma-realm; the ten kings and their sisters; the eighteen minor kings;
the presiding officials of all bureaus, together with their entire retinues.
The King Yama of the Underworld; the Great King Qin Guang; the Great King Chu Jiang;
the Great King Songdi of the Underworld; the Great King Wuguan; and the Great King Biancheng.
The Great King of Mount Tai; the Great King of Equality; the Great King of the City;
the Great King of the Wheel-Turning; the Divine Consort, the King’s Sister; the two boys who record good and evil deeds; and the assembly of female clerks.
At that time, they made a vow together to assist in governing the hells:
the eighteen ministers and their retinues of minor kings, the King of the Great Underworld, Hónggājìn, and the assembly of thirty-seven ghost kings.
The malevolent and venomous ghost kings between the Iron Ring Mountains, along with the assembly of thirty-four ghost kings, hold official registers, karmic mirrors, and fire-pearls;
they interrogate and verify [the dead] alongside the judging officials of the various bureaus.
The Great Deity of the Five Paths of the Underworld; the Great Ghost of Impermanence; the Messengers who Pursue Departed Souls;
the Judge of the Merit Bureau of the Underworld; the Swift Messengers; and the million狱卒 (yùzú) jailers with ox-heads and ashen visages.
I only pray that you will not lose sight of your original nature. By virtue of the Buddha’s majestic radiance, this very evening, at this very hour, come to attend this Dharma assembly.

(The Dharma Master visualizes the innumerable hosts of kings, officials, and functionaries of the underworld coming from beneath the earth and taking their places to one side. (The ritual master proclaims:)
With single-minded devotion, we invoke all those suffering in the eight hot and eight cold great hells,
as well as in all the solitary hells throughout the ten directions and the entire Dharma-realm, together with their retinues.
They dwell directly beneath Jambudvīpa, where the prisoners suffering in the eight hot hells— Saṃjīva, Avīci, and the others—
and the prisoners suffering in the sixteen *utsada* (adjunct) areas at the four gates of the eight hot hells, totaling one hundred and twenty-eight hells, reside.
At the periphery, dwelling within the encircling mountains at the base of the mirror, are the prisoners suffering in the eight cold hells, such as Arbuda;
as well as the prisoners suffering in the ten directions’ Avīci hell, the eighteen hells, the thirty-six hells, and the one hundred and eight hells.
The prisoners suffering in the great hells— those on iron beds and copper pillars, amidst sword-trees and knife-mountains, in the Ash River and hot sands;

those subjected to flaming arrows and flying blades, to having their tongues pulled out, their teeth sawn off, their eyes gouged, and their heads crushed— all these prisoners endure suffering in the great hells.
Furthermore,
there are solitary prisoners suffering in the void, amidst waters, in mountain valleys, and in wildernesses;
as well as those suffering in the dark prisons within the walls and moats of Mount Tai and the local shrines and temples of their respective jurisdictions.

Among the seven destinies, having just departed from the intermediate state (*antarābhava*) and being about to enter hell, the various beings of the dark realms within the various hells have already been released, yet they have not yet attained rebirth. These are the various beings of the dark realms.
"I only pray that you will not lose sight of your original nature. By virtue of the Buddha’s majestic radiance, at this very moment tonight, come to attend this Dharma assembly.

(The Dharma Master visualizes the countless hosts of prisoners from the various hells who, having previously received the imperial pardon and already attained their freedom, now hear the summons and immediately all arrive, standing to one side. The officiant then proclaims:)

With single-minded devotion, we make this invocation: To all those dwelling within the Iron Ring Mountains throughout the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm; to those dwelling at the periphery, pervading the five destinies;
and to the ten classes of animals with scales, shells, feathers, and fur, together with all their retinues.
The king of the garuḍas, the lion king, the elephant king, the great makara fish, and the various classes of meritorious animals;
the divine nāgas, precious tortoises, phoenixes, qilin, rare birds, and extraordinary beasts—all these auspicious classes of animals.
Parrots and white cranes; swallows, sparrows, crows, and vultures; roosters, wild geese, geese, and ducks—these multitudes of winged birds;
oxen, horses, sheep, and deer; tigers, wolves, pigs, and dogs; monkeys, rabbits, cats, and rats—these multitudes of four-footed beasts.
Crocodiles, sea monsters, soft-shelled turtles, and turtles; insects, fish, shrimp, and crabs; conches, shells, clams, and oysters—all such aquatic creatures;
mosquitoes, gnats, fleas, and lice; flies, stinging flies, maggots, and ants; mayflies and dung beetles—all such minute species.
Vipers, snakes, vipers, and scorpions; bees, wasps, and the venom of the *hain* bird; centipedes, millipedes, and all varieties of poisonous creatures;
those with scales, shells, feathers, or fur; those with feet, those without feet, those with four feet, and those with many feet—all such classes of animals.
Owls, jackals, foxes, and venomous creatures; those that feed on worms and those that consume what has been ingested; these rest within ten categories.
All these various classes of animals dwell primarily within the Cakravāḍa mountains, the great oceans, and the islands, while others reside throughout the five destinies.
I pray that you do not lose sight of your original nature. By virtue of the Buddha’s majestic radiance, may you come this very evening, at this very hour, to attend this Dharma assembly.
(The Dharma Master visualizes that countless multitudes of animals from the four directions arrive; they all assume human form and stand to one side. (The Ritual Official proclaims:)

With single-minded devotion, we invoke all those who traverse the various realms within the ten directions and the Dharma-realm, including the multitudes of the intermediate state (*antarābhava*) who undergo seven rebirths during the forty-nine days, together with their retinues.
All sentient beings among the classes of devas who, when their retribution is exhausted, return and receive an intermediate state body;
all sentient beings among the classes of ṛṣis who, when their retribution is exhausted, return and receive an intermediate state body.
Among all human beings, those whose retribution is exhausted and who return to receive an intermediate state body;
and among all sentient beings, those with various meritorious deities whose retribution is exhausted and who return to receive an intermediate state body.
All asuras, when their retribution is exhausted, return and receive an intermediate state body (*antarābhava*).
All sentient beings among the hungry ghosts, when their retribution is exhausted, return and receive an intermediate state body.
All sentient beings among the various animals who, when their retribution is exhausted, return to receive an intermediate state body;
all sentient beings within the various hells who, when their retribution is exhausted, return to receive an intermediate state body.
Within the city of the hells, the two aspects of sin and merit are blown by skillful winds.
Intermediate state beings (*antarābhava*) travel to and fro, taking birth across the four continents and various realms of existence; there are seventeen types of such intermediate state beings.
I only pray that you will not lose sight of your original nature. By virtue of the Buddha’s majestic radiance, may you come this very night, at this very hour, to attend this Dharma assembly.

the deity of the Wugong Pavilion that guards the sea, the deity of Lord Shi, and the host of deities from the Ten Temples of Mount Wu.

(As the donor prostrates—previously, within the realm of hungry ghosts, the spirits of those who died untimely were summoned in their entirety; now, by inviting them again according to their specific categories, it is so that they may understand the circumstances of these solitary spirits. (The Ritual Master recites:)
To do good is the greatest joy. You should cherish this humble body of yours; by reaching a very advanced age, you may hope to fulfill your allotted destiny.
Yet there are those who indulge their hearts in cruelty and whose natures are stubborn and ignorant; because they follow the patterns of perilous paths, the triggers of calamity suddenly erupt.
Though their physical forms have perished, their worldly lifespans have not yet ended, for the Underworld has no means to collect them and the Celestial Bureaucracy does not record them.
This constitutes dying without having attained one's natural end; in the end, where will they find refuge?

Although their followers are numerous and have existed for many years, their wandering spirits have no place to rest and must constantly dwell amidst the realm of humans. Since those of like nature seek one another, they will inevitably be drawn into the realm of ghosts.
If you wish to turn your thoughts toward right mindfulness, you should repent of your past causes; by means of the merit of this universal salvation tonight, may [you attain liberation].
Regarding the schemes for your rebirth, those who dwell among sudden and untimely deaths are of many kinds. I shall now fully attend to your guidance;
please listen as I discuss their circumstances in detail (the *baibiao* is recited).

With single-minded devotion, we extend our invitation to all sovereigns and ministers, queens and princesses, and lords of the various lands throughout the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm, as well as to wandering spirits who died untimely deaths and their respective retinues.
I only pray that you will not lose sight of your original nature. Empowered by the Buddha’s majestic radiance, come this very evening, at this very hour, to attend this Dharma assembly.
(The assembly joins in harmony with incense and flowers; strike the gongs. For subsequent sections, follow this example. (The Ritual Official addresses them: [The Ritual Official speaks:]

The virtue of the Nine Palaces was obscured by darkness; the hearts of the Four Seas were alienated. Consequently, the various heroes vied with one another to plot against the law, so that the Great Calendar could no longer be prolonged and was suddenly usurped by others.
The state was destroyed and the family perished; the person passed away and the ancestral sacrifices ceased.

As for those whose rank was as high as the Chief Minister, where thousands of officials stood in solemn ranks like *yuánlù* birds; or whose power was as great as the Supreme Commander, where ten thousand cavalrymen moved in disciplined order like *píxiū* beasts.

In these ranks, some spread the transformative teachings across a hundred cities, while others governed the people in a single district. Was it not because they had pledged their lives to this sovereign dynasty, desiring also to leave a name for posterity?
Yet, some found it difficult to serve as ministers; lacking integrity in their conduct, they failed to be loyal to their superiors, and thus were laid out as corpses at the two towers.
Others lost discipline while leading armies and were ultimately beheaded before the three divisions of the host. As for those who sought merit beyond the distant desert...
Returning, they were destined for the felt tents of the nomads without ever coming back; cast out as "expelled guests," they threw themselves into pestilential lands.
Engaged in royal service, they encountered bandits on perilous paths; they were stabbed by treacherous and wicked men and slandered by the mouths of sycophants and favorites.
They were given poisoned wine to die instantly, or handed swords to commit suicide. This was true even for the Empress and the Chief Consort, as well as the talented ladies and palace maids.
When beauty fades, love slackens; when fortune passes, calamity arises. Thus, some end their lives in the Yeching Palace, while others are imprisoned in the Yongxiang corridor.
From the wives of enfeoffed lords to concubines and secondary ladies, they vie for loveliness and seek favor; relying on their own kindness, they become jealous of the sovereign’s affection.

Filth originates within the inner chambers, and transformation occurs upon the bedchamber mats. Suddenly startled by the fading of their plum-like countenances, they are ultimately cast away like weeds among the tall grass.
Such is the state of affairs; it is truly pitiable and sorrowful. Now, there are those with sincere faith who respectfully prepare this vegetarian feast (*zhāi*).
We shall summon all without exception, ensuring that none are left behind from afar. It is fitting that you come together as a multitude, hoping to hear the Dharma and attain deliverance.

(The Dharma Master visualizes an immeasurable multitude of orphaned spirits summoned by his thoughts, arriving from the four directions and withdrawing to stand at one side. (The officiant recites the invocation:)

With single-minded devotion, I invoke all those throughout the ten directions and the entire dharma realm: scholars, farmers, artisans, and merchants; all members of the human community; and the orphaned spirits of those who died untimely deaths, together with their kinsmen and retinues.
I only pray that you will not lose sight of your original nature. Relying upon the majestic radiance of the Buddha, may you come this very evening to join this Dharma assembly.
There are white-haired scholars who have exhausted the classics yet met with no fortune; there are yellow-capped immortals who pursue the Way but achieve nothing.

There are those who have made a name for themselves by treating illnesses, and those who practice divination as their profession. There are those who set up shops in the marketplace, those who toil in the fields and attend to farming, and those whose various skills range from refined to coarse.

From craftsmen, both great and small, to officials and soldiers who serve the public interest, and even to performers and courtesans who sell their beauty—none do not indulge in wine that rots the intestines, nor lose their lives through greed for wealth.
They are beaten when their words clash, and they sustain injuries when competing in games of chance.
One may administer poison to harm others, or take up a blade to sever one’s own head;
suffer from hunger and cold until illness strikes and one cannot rise, or contract a pestilence so that the symptoms of realization are difficult to discern.

One may be dazed by cholera, lose one’s will through epilepsy, be seized suddenly upon encountering an enemy, or be mistakenly arrested in a panic by the ghosts of the underworld. Or one may hang oneself within a ditch or a stream. Being...
They were crushed beneath rocky walls; they stayed overnight in roadside inns, where nightmares struck them and their breath failed.
They traveled by sea, where they were plundered by bandits and perished in battle. In their daily lives, they suddenly encountered the bite of snakes;

in their meals, they unexpectedly met with poisoned insects. The strike of heavenly thunder serves to manifest one’s evil; the burning of wild fires—how could it be said to have no cause? Those who cultivate virtue still...

Thus you encounter calamity. Those who commit transgressions deserve to be punished. Although this life was taken by one's own actions, it is also the consequence of karmic retribution following upon itself.
To treat this body with such ease and to hold death in such light contempt—such a state of affairs is truly pitiable.
Now, there are those here with sincere faith who respectfully prepare these rites of purification; they have summoned all beings without leaving anyone far behind. You should join the assembly to...
Come together! We hope that you may hear the Dharma and attain deliverance.
(The Dharma Master visualizes the infinite multitude of orphaned spirits summoned from all four directions, who now stand to one side. (The Ritual Official proclaims:)

With single-minded devotion, we invoke all the military and civilian populations throughout the lands of the ten directions within the Dharma-realm, as well as the orphaned spirits who died by violent means in battle and their respective kinsmen.
I pray that you will not lose sight of your original nature. By virtue of the Buddha’s majestic radiance, may you come this very night, at this very hour, to attend this Dharma assembly.

Those who lead others toward death take up weapons as instruments of cruelty; those who possess a state maintain them constantly yet do not employ them, whereas those below who steal and toy with them are executed.
Thus, civil and military power are mutually restrained; this is called the simultaneous fulfillment of majesty and virtue. As for greedy seeking—

Regarding land matters, there are those who delight in establishing martial achievements. Like Bai Qi, they pitilessly slaughtered four hundred thousand surrendered soldiers by hurling them into mass graves;

or like Li Ling, they led over five thousand men into battle until they were all lost to the winds and dust. Alas, where can their departed souls find refuge? Truly, their grievances cannot be voiced.
To this day, such cases have not ceased, and those of this kind are especially numerous. Oh, how vast it is!... [The text continues with "Hong wei" (Alas, how great it is) and so forth.]
The Great Court unified all under heaven. Yet, some crossed horses across the Huai and Zhe regions, while others drew their bows along the bends of the rivers and seas.
They demolished public buildings and incinerated the dwellings of the people; prefectures and counties were mostly left desolate and waste, and all living beings suffered the bitterest poisons.

Fortresses and camps were shattered; the ancestral altars were overturned and destroyed. Men were slain until they filled the cities, and blood flowed until it became a marsh. Those sent eastward perished in the waters; those stationed north were scattered in exile.

Driven by imperial mandates and coerced by military might, their bodies withered away as their lives ended. Those who fled to the mountains and forests did so because they cherished their wealth, yet their leaders were divided among themselves.
Those who roamed the weeds and thickets gathered their followers because of their indignant spirit, yet they struck one another with spears and shields. They mobilized labor to construct warships.

Starving to death or perishing as travelers, they pay grain-tax to assist the army; terrified by the pursuit of unpaid levies, they face death. Jackals and wolves compete to gnaw their remains; crows and magpies scramble for their cries.
Amidst the green of spring winds and creeping vines, withered bones are barely concealed; beneath the white of moonlit cold sands at night, a solitary spirit is left to tremble alone.

Now utterly desolate and having no place to turn, we face one another in silent, dark weeping. While this may indeed be the retribution for shared karma, how could it not be a grievous injustice to involve those who are innocent?
This is especially true when a great commander governs the frontier regions and his various officers each lead their respective divisions.

They plowed their fields while guarding the borders; relying on both valor and strategy, they were suddenly executed for violating orders within the camp, or ultimately put to death for missing their muster for the frontier garrison.
Such as these companions are deeply pitiable. Now, there is one here who possesses faith.

We respectfully perform these rites of purification. May all beings be summoned and gathered, so that none are left behind in the distance. It is fitting that the entire multitude come together, hoping to hear the Dharma and attain deliverance.

(The Dharma Master visualizes the countless hosts of orphaned spirits being summoned from the four quarters, who now stand to one side. (The Ritual Master recites: *Note: This text describes a ritual for summoning and purifying wandering spirits (preta). The "Dharma Master" refers to the officiant, while the "Ritual Master" (表白) refers to the person chanting the liturgical verses.*

With single-minded devotion, we invoke all the people of the lands throughout the ten directions and the dharma-realm, as well as the orphaned spirits who have met with untimely deaths while in prison or under judicial punishment,
together with their kinsmen and associates.
I pray that you will not lose sight of your original nature. By virtue of the Buddha’s majestic radiance, may you attend this Dharma assembly this very evening at this very hour.
As those who uphold the laws throughout the empire and administer justice across the various prefectures, you should proclaim benevolent transformation and thereby assist the Great Court.

As for opening wide the gates of solicitation and specifically instigating the "fabricated" prisons—where matters are suspicious yet not investigated, and where the circumstances ought to be treated with leniency—[you must refrain from such acts].
Yet they do not reflect upon this; they merely act according to their likes and dislikes. How can they look with indifference toward those who are oppressed?

Furthermore, when governance lacks virtue and the adjudication of lawsuits is entrusted to the unworthy, these official records are left to the officials, who merely observe the quantity of bribes received.
In determining the gravity or lightness of life and death, they have entirely yielded to their private biases; thus, in the end, they could not escape public censure.
As for the excessive infliction of painful interrogations and the extreme application of deep-seated legal traps, some die from the lashes and beatings, while others perish within the prison cells.
Some remain incarcerated for life, perishing in military camps; others are banished to distant lands, dying upon the roads.

What can be said of the suffering of having one's head severed? The cruelty of being flayed alive is even more extreme. Those who have committed offenses and whose guilt is proven should certainly be punished;
yet how could those who die without having committed any crime fail to harbor resentment? It is not only in the underworld that there are times of judgment and reckoning;
one should know that in the world of men, there are many days of retribution. Such circumstances are deeply tragic. Now, there is indeed...
With faith and reverence, prepare the rites of the fast. Summon everyone without exception, ensuring that none are left behind.
It is fitting that the entire assembly should come together, hoping to hear the Dharma and attain deliverance.

(The Dharma Master visualizes an immeasurable multitude of orphaned spirits summoned by his thought, coming from the four directions and withdrawing to stand to one side. (The officiant recites the invocation:)

With single-minded devotion, we extend our invocation to all the people of every land throughout the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm, including those who have been cursed or harbored enmity, the solitary souls of those who died untimely deaths,
and all their kinsmen and associates.
I only pray that you will not lose sight of your original nature. By virtue of the Buddha’s majestic radiance, may you come this very night, at this very hour, to attend this Dharma assembly.
Observing the world at large, one finds that the most numerous are evil people who fail to restrain their minds; consequently, they constantly let their mouths run wild.

Thus, when encountering changing circumstances or navigating worldly affairs, even if they suffer only slight grievances, they immediately resort to curses and incantations. This is especially true when it comes to matters such as the trading of fields or mountains.
The *Yijing* has not yet been rectified. Debts of wealth and property remain unpaid and unredeemed; stolen or lost items lead to groundless suspicion;
litigations and accusations are joined together, resulting in the indiscriminate incrimination of others; those who have actually committed offenses take pleasure in elaborate self-justification;

and when beset by slander, they are unable to clear their names. Toward their parents, they are unfilial and constantly utter words of resentment; toward their wives and children, they fail to provide for them, thereby inviting [retribution].

In their expressions of resentment, there are none who do not call out to Heaven and appeal to Earth, invoking ghosts and summoning spirits to vent their grievances for a single day, thereby binding themselves to enmity for a thousand lifetimes.
Consequently, the Celestial Bureaus and the Netherworld each have officials who maintain records, as do the deities of Mount Tai and the City God.
There are particularly many officials who oversee and investigate. Once a person has died, they seize one another; before the charges are adjudicated, they are implicated in succession.
Consequently, both oneself and others meet with untimely death. Such factions are truly pitiable.

Now, there are those of sincere faith who respectfully prepare this rite of purification (*zhāi*). Let them summon all [the deceased] without leaving anyone far behind. It is fitting that the entire assembly should...
Come together! We hope that you may hear the Dharma and attain liberation.
(The Dharma Master visualizes that innumerable hosts of solitary spirits summoned have arrived from the four directions and stand to one side. (The Ritual Official proclaims:)

With single-minded devotion, we invoke all the people of the various lands throughout the ten directions and the Dharma-realm, as well as the orphaned spirits who have perished by drowning in the surging waves,
together with all their kinsmen and associates.
I pray that you will not lose sight of your original nature. By virtue of the Buddha’s majestic radiance, may you come this very evening, at this very hour, to attend this Dharma assembly.
The Yangtze, the Yellow River, the Huai, and the Ji, as well as all the mountain streams, marshes, ponds, and lakes—these great waterways are all exceedingly perilous.

It is only by the advantage of riding upon boats that one may avoid the hardships of traveling these roads; therefore, for the sake of those travelers coming and going, as well as those bound by official deadlines...
I have experienced such things as when a great wind arose, surging up to the heavens with tumultuous waves; a single sail was tilted and drifted away, tossed by the billows.

This is especially true for merchants traveling through maritime kingdoms or transporting goods to barbarian lands: by day they encounter bands of pirates who rain down arrows and stones in a chaotic assault;
by night they enter raging torrents and sit watching their axles and hubs sink completely beneath the water. Some, before their lives have even ended, are cast entirely into the sea; others...
Possessed by demons, they threw themselves into the abyss; together they were submerged and drowned in the surging waves. This is what is called the premature destruction of one’s life.
Thereupon, dwelling upon a chain of islands and excelling in the trades of fishing and salt, they pursue foul odors to maintain their households, casting their nets along the currents.
The boatman was not careful; he suddenly lost the rudder in the surging rapids. His companions could not escape; they were all drowned in the vast waters.
Since corpses do not remain overnight, by what means could they be interred in coffins? As their departed spirits have no place of return, who would perform the rites of sacrifice for them?
Such a class of beings is deeply pitiable. Now, having developed faith, they respectfully prepare this vegetarian feast;
let us summon them all so that none are left behind. You should come together with the entire assembly, hoping to hear the Dharma and attain deliverance.

(The Dharma Master visualizes an immeasurable multitude of orphaned spirits summoned by his thoughts, arriving from the four directions and withdrawing to stand at one side. (The officiant recites the invocation:)

With single-minded devotion, we invoke all those wandering spirits who have met with untimely deaths and their respective retinues— those who roam within the oceans and rivers of the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm,
and who are habitually engaged in robbery and plunder.
I pray that you do not lose sight of your original nature. By virtue of the Buddha’s majestic radiance, come this very evening and at this very hour to attend this Dharma assembly.
Dwelling on the shores of rivers and seas, you engaged in the business of boats and oars; yet your commercial ventures met with failure, your nets caught no fish, and your capital was entirely lost.
As your greed grew ever more intense, you called out to your companions to hatch a wicked plot, setting sail across the vast deep to go forth.
These pirates commanded massive ships numbering more than ten and gathered a band of ruffians exceeding a thousand.

Although their primary intent was the seizure of wealth, they also simultaneously committed acts of violence against living beings. Arrows and stones fell like rain; gongs and drums thundered like peals of lightning.

With swords in hand, they were like butchers entering the marketplace; with faces smeared black, they were like beasts emerging from the forest. They launched a joint assault upon the merchant vessel, slaughtering and plundering.
Not a single person remained. Suddenly encountering the government troops, they offered resistance with no small measure of daring;
they ranged across islands and burned down houses and huts. Having driven off their oxen and sheep, they further stole their children and women.

These people were indeed accustomed to accumulating evil, yet Heaven must surely bring calamity upon those who dally in lust. Some had their bodies shattered during the heat of battle, while others were bound...

On the day he was captured by hand, he was imprisoned in the official jail at night; after a single interrogation, his confession was complete, and at dawn he was delivered to the execution grounds, where his life suddenly ended within half a meal’s time.
Although there was a temporary distinction between the leaders and their followers, in the end they all shared the same destruction.
Having lived as violent, rebellious, and lawless men, they die to become powerful, arrogant, and ignorant ghosts. Such a kindred spirit is truly to be deeply pitied.
In my sorrow, I have now developed sincere faith and respectfully prepared this vegetarian feast. I shall summon all without exception, ensuring that none are left behind;
it is fitting that you come together as a community, hoping to hear the Dharma and attain deliverance.

(The Dharma Master visualizes an immeasurable multitude of orphaned spirits summoned by his thought, arriving from the four directions and withdrawing to stand at one side. (The officiant recites the invocation:)

With single-minded devotion, we invoke all those throughout the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm: malevolent ghosts and spirits, those who harm virtuous people, the orphaned souls of untimely death, and all their retinues.
I pray that you do not lose sight of your original nature. By virtue of the Buddha’s majestic radiance, come this very evening to attend this Dharma assembly.

Though living, you are no upright person; though dead, you are but a malevolent spirit. Because you possess a slight understanding of worldly affairs, you are known as a ghost endowed with the five supernatural powers (*pañcābhijñā*).
You roam among the thickets of trees and dwell in pleasure upon high towers, consorting with the wives of others.

They gratify themselves by secretly seizing the wealth of others to curry favor with people; seeking their own benefit through lustful attachment to depraved associates, they further cause indiscriminate harm to the virtuous.
There are those who have maintained the incense and lamps handed down through generations, known as "family altars" (jiatáng), which they have never neglected throughout the years and seasons.

They constantly give rise to calamities out of delusion, deceiving the ignorant masses to seek food and drink, indulging in unrestrained greed and gluttony, and performing licentious sacrifices by slaughtering oxen and sheep;
these only increase their resentment and karmic burden. Both parties are at fault, and there is no mutual benefit whatsoever; thus they remain blind and deluded.

They all fall into ruin and degradation. As for mountain sprites and water monsters, great demons and fox-essences, worn-out brooms and broken cauldrons, ancient basins and split pestles—they transform into men to seduce virgins, causing them to conceive and become pregnant in their youth; they change into beautiful women to delude young men.
Emotions cause illness; having become deeply immersed in improper influences, one ultimately meets an untimely death before reaching the end of one’s natural lifespan.
Yet, such individuals continue to engage in these very practices alongside their followers. This situation is truly pitiable.

Now, there are those with sincere faith who respectfully prepare for this rite of purification (*zhāi*). We shall summon all [spirits] without leaving anyone far behind; it is fitting that you come together as a multitude.
I hope they will hear the Dharma and attain deliverance.
(The Dharma Master visualizes the countless hosts of orphaned spirits summoned from the four quarters, who come and stand to one side. (The ritual master chants:)

With single-minded devotion, we invoke all the people of the various lands throughout the ten directions and the entire Dharma-realm, as well as the orphaned spirits of those who died untimely deaths due to wasting diseases, epidemics, or contagion,
together with their kinsmen and retinues.
I pray that you do not lose sight of your original nature. By virtue of the Buddha’s majestic radiance, may you come this very evening to attend this Dharma assembly.

Because of a lack of goodness in your learning and an improper application of the mind, the celestial Māras have found an opportunity; they fly in with subtle precision and attach themselves to the human body.

Pestilence-demons take form, and as for those who exhaust their retribution, many are reborn among the class of intestinal worms. Some transform into butterflies, while others take shapes resembling centipedes.
Alas! This root of calamity has long resided within the vital channels of the lungs, ultimately causing this fragile body to suffer the ailment of wasting disease.
His breath is labored and his voice is hoarse; he coughs up blood that cannot be stilled. His face is withered and his bones stand bare; he lacks the strength to support himself.
Half-sitting, half-lying, he experiences alternating chills and fevers. His spirit is exhausted and weary as the years drag on. [He was treated] with medicine...
It does not heal. One's life span then diminishes accordingly. Having already lost oneself through this illness, one further harms others by means of this karma.
When it reaches as far as a thousand *li*, it is called "flying corpse" (*feishi*); when it spreads locally throughout a single household, it is known as "transmitted contagion" (*chuanzhu*).
It may infect through the contact of clothing and bedding, or through the entanglement of husband and wife. At the place where the victim died, various worms emerge; while the person lies in bed—
They enter into the various apertures [of the body], beginning from the day they first fell ill and ending with the year of their passing.

They become companions to ghosts, dwelling together in shared resentment. Such a class of beings is truly pitiable. Now, there are those with sincere faith who respectfully perform this rite of *zhāi*;
we summon them all, ensuring none are left behind in the distance. It is fitting that you all come together as one, hoping to hear the Dharma and...
[They] attain deliverance.
(The Dharma Master visualizes the countless hosts of orphaned spirits summoned from the four quarters, who withdraw and stand to one side. (The Ritual Master recites:)

With single-minded devotion, we invoke all the people of the various lands throughout the ten directions and the Dharma-realm, as well as the orphaned spirits of those who died untimely deaths after being mangled by tigers,
together with all their kinsmen.
I only pray that you will not lose sight of your original nature. By virtue of the Buddha’s majestic radiance, may you come this very evening to join this Dharma assembly.

Though your innate disposition is stubborn and you do not conform to the conduct of ordinary people, and though your physical form is coarse and fierce such that you dwell among a pack of tigers, [may you nevertheless attend].
For this reason, they frequent the mountains and forests, maiming and killing sheep and swine to use as food; even in such acts, they still breed resentment.
How much more so when, on perilous and narrow roads, they harm the traveling merchants and wayfarers—how lamentable this is! Reaching such a state, what more can be said?
In recent years, reports from various places have been frequent: even amidst the clamor and confusion, these creatures roam at will.
Carrying firewood up a ridge, they suddenly appear before one; setting down their burdens on the road, they encounter them abruptly.

Having been bitten, they eventually suffer injury or death, yet they remain unaware of their own enemies and instead act as their assistants. They recklessly invade the ranks of the virtuous, unleashing their savage ferocity wherever they pass. Once encountered—
The ravenous saliva of those with venomous fangs has suddenly caused them to lose their ordinary right view; these kinsmen are truly to be pitied.
Now, having developed faith, we respectfully prepare this vegetarian feast (zhāi), summoning all without exception so that none are left behind.
It is fitting that you come together as a multitude, hoping to hear the Dharma and attain deliverance.

(The Dharma Master visualizes a boundless multitude of orphaned spirits summoned by his thought, coming from the four directions and withdrawing to stand at one side. (The officiant recites the invocation:)

With single-minded devotion, we invoke all the people of the various lands throughout the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm, as well as the orphaned spirits of those who died in childbirth with their milk dried up, those who met untimely deaths,
and all their kinsmen and associates.
I pray that you will not lose sight of your original nature. Empowered by the Buddha’s majestic light, come this very evening to this Dharma assembly.

Behold with tranquility how the ways of the world are ignorant; how people fail to reflect upon the difficulty of obtaining a human body, yet instead compete in following vulgar customs and all lose their innate compassion.
Thinking that managing a household is not yet sufficient, they are constantly filled with anxiety; thus, when they have several sons, they cast them aside.
They are not supported. Having already emerged from the prison of the womb, they are again submerged in a basin of water. Whether female or male, they are born only to die;

they occupy the inner chambers while practicing slaughter, and through wives and concubines, they bind themselves in enmity. This alone extinguishes the bonds of human ethics and violates the principles of Heaven.
It reaches even to the point where birth is inverted—head first or feet first—resulting in the death of both mother and child.

If such great enemies are not all evil adversaries—some whose lives were cut short during their childhood, or whose nursing was severed while still in swaddling clothes—it is certain that they committed no transgression as infants;
rather, they have invited this retribution due to their past karma. Such circumstances are deeply pitiable.
Now, having developed sincere faith, we respectfully perform this rite of purification and invite them all to be summoned.
Let none be left behind in the distance; it is fitting that the entire multitude come together. We hope that by hearing the Dharma, they may attain deliverance.
(The Dharma Master visualizes the innumerable hosts of orphaned spirits summoned from the four quarters, who arrive and stand to one side. (The Ritual Official proclaims:)

With single-minded devotion, we invoke all wandering spirits and orphaned souls from the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm— those who have been farmers, fishermen, or hunters, and all living beings who met with untimely deaths— together with their kinsmen and associates.
We pray that you will not lose sight of your original nature and, sustained by the majestic radiance of the Buddha, come to this Dharma assembly this very evening, at this very moment.
To embody the Way of Heaven’s love for life and to eliminate the human heart’s delight in killing, one need not speak of attaining blessings; one will at least avoid leaving behind calamity.
Why is it that the vulgar are so devoid of goodness, indulging their deluded passions and deliberately committing offenses? Thus, they cast nets for fish and shrimp in the great marshes.
They chase deer in the deep mountains; they cook rams and take their lambs; they slaughter oxen to roast them; they boil soft-shelled turtles and mince carp; they dry poultry and steam pork.
At every turn, they painfully cut away the fat and marrow to satisfy the cravings of their mouths and bellies.

Because those who seek such things in the markets are ever numerous, fishermen and hunters pursue them all the more. When their bodies are butchered upon the knife and block, their souls are terrified by the boiling water and flames.
Having encountered extreme suffering, they consequently harbor deep resentment.

This leads to plucking bees for honey, breaking oysters for pearls, shooting sparrows from the forest with slings, and drawing bows to fell eagles beyond the clouds. Knowing only how to deceive these minute lives, they never consider the retribution of their enemies.
Thus they tread upon the wandering ants by the roadside and drink in the tiny insects within the water.
Although this arises from a mistaken mind, it will nonetheless invite retribution in the future.

As for the fly that casts itself into a vessel of wine or the moth that flutters its wings into a lamp, though they truly surrender their lives to external forces, it is in fact I who have set the trap.
If one speaks of still pursuing the Way, it is already enough to cause grief for the lack of compassion. There are those of various species who each give rise to aggression and oppression;
small and large devour one another in succession. Day and night, they undergo ten thousand deaths and ten thousand births, inflicting harm upon one another without ceasing.
Therefore, retribution follows in sequence without end. Such a state of affairs is deeply pitiable. Now, there are those who possess sincere faith.

We respectfully perform this rite of purification. We shall exhaustively summon all beings, ensuring that none are left behind in the distance. It is fitting that the entire assembly come together, hoping to hear the Dharma and attain deliverance.
(The Dharma Master visualizes the countless hosts of orphaned spirits being summoned from the four quarters, who then take their places to one side. (The Ritual Master proclaims:)
The various classes of solitary spirits summoned above could not have assembled in full were it not for the power of secret mantras.
Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses a mantra for summoning; I shall now reverently recite it.
Oṃ śavara koṭi ajjha vijjha svāhā. (Having recited the mantra three times, strike the cymbals.

[The Dharma Master visualizes that the various classes of solitary spirits summoned above, by virtue of the power of the Dharma, all possess upright and majestic appearances; they ascend to the pure path and dwell within the pavilion.]
May they come to this *bodhimaṇḍa* by virtue of this secret rite; The donor, with utmost sincerity, prostrates with a devoted heart. (The donor prostrates.

(The Dharma Master contemplates the karmic obstructions of the prisoners in hell. Although they have been summoned, they are unable to escape. There is a special expedient means by which they may all arrive. (The Ritual Director rings the bell to open the gates of hell.)
He addressed them, saying:
"The Three Jewels bestow their grace, and the Nine Heavens grant a general amnesty. Among all those summoned here, there is none who does not come.

Yet, as for the prisoners confined within the Netherworld, their roots of transgression are deep and firm; they are separated by the boundaries of this realm and other realms, and distinguished by those dwelling in the central regions and those dwelling at the borders."

The distinctions [of suffering] are manifold: when iron nails are driven into the body, the entire frame becomes covered in sores; when the body is ground by stones, the whole person is shattered to pieces;
fierce flames pierce the chest until it is glowing red, and molten copper is poured into the mouth until it flows out in drenching streams.

Because one suffers such agony and is utterly bewildered, one cannot comprehend the commands heard; this arises from the obstructions created by one’s own karma, and is not the fault of the presiding officer.
They are not benevolent. As for the various offices of Mount Tai and the temples of the City God, they observe this place from the netherworld and truly have many followers;
whether it be cases of mutual enmity or matters where the facts have not yet been resolved, they are all able to obstruct and delay them, preventing them from proceeding.
Not only would this fail to fulfill the Buddha’s compassionate intent, but it would surely leave the perfection of giving (dānapāramitā) unfulfilled.

Now, therefore, we reverently proclaim these verses and mantras to fully manifest majestic spiritual power; with a single strike upon the firm gate, the throngs of those burdened by transgressions shall rush forth, regardless of their noble or humble status.
Without distinction between enemy and kin, I hope that all may reach the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) and that all may partake of the Dharma-offering.
I now respectfully proclaim the verses for shattering hell spoken by Bodhisattva Jālinīprabha within the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, as well as the mantra for shattering hell for the purpose of recitation;
these can cause all prisoners suffering in the various hells to be forever liberated.
Those in obscure realms shall be reborn in the good paths.
If one wishes to fully understand all Buddhas of the three periods of time, One should contemplate the nature of the Dharma-realm:
All is created solely by the mind. (Recite this verse together with the assembly seven times; more recitations are even more excellent.)
Oṃ kharateye svāhā. (The assembly recites this together twenty-one times; the more they do, the more excellent it becomes.

[The Dharma Master visualizes that the iron city gates of the hells in the ten directions all swing open at once. All the instruments of torture therein vanish completely. All the prisoners, hearing the sound of the mantra, regain their original minds and inform one another.
They come to the Dharma assembly, longing for liberation. The officiant rings the bell to clear the way and speaks thus:]
From antiquity to the present, across the heavens and to the ends of the earth, [the Buddha] has fully exercised his summons and has never abandoned even the most profound and subtle mysteries.

Thus, all those belonging to the class of sentient beings who possess the Buddha-nature may enter, with ease, the assembly where there are no obstacles. This includes even those who have committed the ten evil deeds.
Having long dwelt within the three miserable realms, although one may find temporary ease at this moment, the path ahead remains unopened.
One’s feet stumble upon treacherous ground, and one’s body is bound in a land of profound darkness. With such manifold hardships, how can one successfully reach the goal?
Relying once more upon the power of the secret, you manifest the banner of radiant light to illuminate the dark alleys;
may none fall into error, and may all proceed securely along the direct path, fortunately finding their way home. May your heroic spirit awaken to this skillful means.
Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses the mantra for opening the path.
I shall now reverently recite it: Oṃ bhaṇamiṃ bhagavati mudhaya mudhaya jaye mudhaṃ svāhā.

(After reciting the mantra three times, ring the hand-bell and gong. (The Dharma Master visualizes that within the three realms of suffering, countless sentient beings, obstructed by their evil karma and having lost their way, now, by the power of this mantra’s efficacy, immediately attain a level and smooth great road and arrive at the Dharma assembly.
(The Ritual Official rings the bell to dispel fear and addresses them as follows:)
The six classes of ordinary beings are numerous; they manifest both the visible and the hidden simultaneously. The Three Honored Ones are majestic and grave, truly inspiring both awe and affection.
Unless one relies on expedient means to comfort and gladden the hearts of the multitude, I fear they might hesitate and retreat to one side. Thus, he proclaimed the secret words.
