We, with great reverence, consider how our Śākyamuni Tathāgata proclaimed the Dharma-gate of the Food Offering (*śrīmaṇḍala-bali*), so that by single-mindedly reciting the *Anantavīrya-vaśitā-prabhāsa-viśeṣa-mahābala-dhāraṇī* and consecrating a single meal, it may give rise to an infinite amount, pervading the entire *dharmadhātu*, and universally manifesting offerings. Indeed...
This dhāraṇī is the secret treasury of the three virtues. This secret treasury encompasses all phenomena;
therefore, it can flow forth from this inexhaustibly, never having been depleted. Now, "majestic power and sovereignty" refers to the virtue of liberation (*vimukti*).
"Radiance" refers to the virtue of wisdom (*prajñā*). "Supreme excellence" refers to the virtue of the Dharma-body (*dharmakāya*). "Power" refers to the [virtue of]... the three [powers].
This is the power and function of virtue (*guṇa*). *Dhāraṇī* is a term for "total retention. Total retention of the three virtues depends fundamentally upon the single mind.
Within the single mind, the three virtues are inherently and naturally present. Thus, the single mind is itself *dhāraṇī*, and *dhāraṇī* is itself the Dharma-food.
There is nothing that does not take these three virtues collectively as its essence, nor is there anything that does not [rely] upon these three.

The Three Virtues (Guṇas) act together as its function. Now, because I am able to realize that the secret treasury of the Three Virtues contains all phenomena, and that all phenomena share the same essence as the Three Virtues, they are able to manifest their function through their entire substance, becoming the portioned food I now receive before me.
From each and every morsel of food, there arise all the celestial *sudhā* nectar and flavors of joy.
There were round cakes, *amṛta* (ghee), cream, curd, and every kind of exquisite flavor, all fully provided.

From within each of these flavors, there likewise emerged wondrously fragrant precious flowers, celestial garments, necklaces, various jeweled carriages and litters, all manner of articles for use, bells, chimes, golden cymbals, flutes, pipes, horns, conchs, drums, music, stringed songs, and all kinds of sublime sounds. There were flowing springs and bathing pools, and flowers...

Fruit orchards and groves, radiant terraces and palaces—every dwelling place—and furthermore, for each and every exquisite flavor, each and every article of clothing, each and every wondrous sound, and each and every dwelling, these were produced in their respective places.

As with the six sense objects mentioned above, there was no sublime offering that was not universally present, like the pearls of Indra’s net, where a thousand lights reflect one another; as one pearl approaches many pearls, so do the many pearls [reflect one].
They converge upon a single jewel; the one and the many mutually encompass and reflect one another.

Thus, although the food in a single vessel is most minute and simple, it is able to possess such inconceivable efficacy because this single thought-moment is the very embodiment of the three virtues (*triguṇa*).
I now offer this for the sake of the patrons, maintaining these subtle objects of the six sense-fields (*ṣaḍviṣaya*) perfumed by the three virtues.
I offer this universally to the infinite multitudes of sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm, so that they may all be simultaneously satisfied without any deficiency.
Although those sentient beings each receive and enjoy it, I originally have nothing to give; the sentient beings originally have nothing to take;
the objects offered are also fundamentally non-existent; and both I and the sentient beings lack any marks of selfhood. This is what it means to take emptiness as one's contemplation.
Although there is neither giving nor taking, neither thing nor self nor sentient being, yet the giver, the receiver, and the object given between them are all clearly and distinctly visible.
This is what is meant by "contemplating through the conventional":
within a single mind, one thoroughly understands that the giver, the receiver, and the object given are neither existent nor non-existent, such that the three spheres are entirely transcended.

This is what it means to take the Middle Way as one's contemplation. When the three contemplations are perfectly illuminated and attained within a single thought-moment, there is neither after nor before;
there is no thinking and no deliberation. One who practices giving while contemplating in this manner is practicing the "giving that does not dwell on signs.
When these sentient beings receive such giving, each and every one naturally attains the joy of dhyāna and the delight of the Dharma. Because of this, they abide in the heavenly realms.
Thus, their superior merit increases further. Among human beings, they suddenly awaken to the true homecoming; asuras subdue their minds of anger;
hungry ghosts all obtain full satisfaction; animals naturally gain wisdom; and those in hell are forever liberated from confinement.

At this very moment, they all repent for the causes of their karma and advance toward seeking transcendence. You should know that it is precisely for you all that [the Buddha] takes refuge in the Triple Gem and offers [this teaching].
They perform repentance, resolve upon the bodhicitta, and establish the four great vows. They are shown the Threefold Pure Precepts and revealed the wondrous essence of the three virtues.
Thus they become clear, penetrating, and thoroughly enlightened, with no further obscurations remaining.
Furthermore, at this time, they are provided with the benefit of the Dharma-food; as both the Dharma and the food serve as benefits, it is as Tiantai said:
It is like medicated incense: as the fire’s power carries the medicine into a person’s body, the ailment is removed and health is restored;
the Dharma entering through food is likewise. Whether near or far, it ultimately destroys ignorance.
All this is achieved by relying upon the power of the Dharma-gift on this day.
I now respectfully proclaim the *Dhāraṇī of Immeasurable Majestic Virtue, Sovereign Radiance, and Supreme Wondrous Power*.

By means of this empowerment, may the ritual food pervade the entire Dharma-realm and achieve great efficacy, as previously described. I rely upon the assembly of practitioners to recite it together in unison.
Namo sarvatathāgatāvalokite | Oṃ saphara saphara hūṃ | (The assembly recites this mantra in unison. According to the *Ullambana Sūtra*:
when offering food to the hosts of hungry ghosts, have them recite it seven times;

when offering to the hosts of Brahmins and ṛṣis, have them recite it fourteen times (two sets of seven); when making offerings to the Triple Gem, have them recite it twenty-one times (three sets of seven). As for people nowadays...)

When bestowing food upon the six realms of existence, recite the mantra up to seventy times; its efficacy will be even more sublime. Upon finishing the recitation, shake the cymbals. (The Dharma Master visualizes that from within each morsel of food, the supreme flavor of nectar and all manner of delicacies arise.

As described previously in the section on the universal pervasion of the six sense objects, they fill the entire Dharma-realm. All phenomena of both the primary and secondary realms become wondrous offerings, universally bestowed at once upon the six realms of the Dharma-realm, so that each receives their enjoyment without exception or lack of pervasion.
(The Ritual Official rings the bell and bestows the water of nectar, saying:)
This profound water emerges from that lofty source; clothed in secret mantras, it becomes this ambrosia.
It is the divine medicine of immortality, capable of extinguishing the parching heart of extreme thirst and bringing refreshing coolness, universally bestowing benefit.
Upon this prepared food, the power of consecration is bestowed; since its transformation follows a prescribed method, its production—

It is inexhaustible; there is no realm of existence that it does not satisfy, and it brings joy to all sentient beings. May they all attain clear awakening within their own spirits and immediately experience an increase in the bliss of the Dharma.
Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses a mantra for bestowing the nectar of immortality; I shall now reverently recite it.
*Namo surupāya tathāgatāya tadyathā | oṃ suru suru prasuru prasuru svāhā.* (After the assembly has chanted this mantra in unison, ring the hand-bells and cymbals.

(The Ritual Master holds water and sprinkles it everywhere over the four seats of offerings and the *hu* food in the center. (The Ritual Master visualizes that through the power of the mantra, this ritual water immediately becomes the supreme...)

The sublime celestial nectar is sprinkled as an offering for the food; how could it merely be pure, clean, fragrant, and delicious, beyond anything found in the world? It further produces various kinds of delicacies in limitless abundance.

From these delicacies, there further arise the subtle five sense objects (*pañca-viṣaya*), layer upon layer without end, pervading the entire Dharma-realm, so that all sentient beings of the six realms may each receive and enjoy them. (The ritual officiant vibrates the bell and recites the names of the four Tathāgatas, saying:)

The Buddha said: "If there are members of the fourfold assembly who constantly recite this mantra and the names of the four Tathāgatas, and empower food and drink to bestow them upon hungry ghosts, then once these beings have received the food, they shall all be fully satiated. The practitioner who performs such giving will be able to fulfill immeasurable merit and virtue;
it will be no different from the merit of making offerings to hundreds of thousands of koṭis of Tathāgatas."
Furthermore, it is said that this mantra-dharma is bestowed not only upon spirits, but also upon immortals (*ṛṣi*) and the Triple Gem.
By extending this principle, one should know that it must also be bestowed upon the other five destinies; only then will the meaning of the *dharmadhātu* be fully revealed.
I now specifically chant the names of the four Tathāgatas to manifest their supreme efficacy.
Homage to the Tathāgata Prabhūtaratna. Homage to the Tathāgata Suvarṇavarṇa.
Homage to the Tathāgata Vipulaśarīra. Homage to the Tathāgata Abhayadatta.

(The assembly recites these Buddha-names in unison, three times each. (The Dharma Master visualizes that each of the four Tathāgatas arouses thoughts of compassion and gathers in all sentient beings, enabling them to manifest their bodies and perfect their virtues, endowed with complete physical marks and characteristics, receiving all things as they desire.)
[The mantra for] eating: "Free from all fears. (Ring the bell during the *biaobai* [ritual recitation], and offer the oblation according to the prescribed positions.
Recite: "The nature of the myriad dharmas abides nowhere; thus they can be rolled back into the single void. The substance of the six sense-objects is eternally pervasive;
thus they can be extended forth into all existences. This is to create by fully embodying principle (*li*); there is nothing that does not arise from the mind. Thus we know this food..."
Pervading the ten directions, it is truly present at this very moment, universally perfuming all classes of beings.

Now that you have encountered the precious banquet of the Great King, you ought to listen to the sacred verses of our Buddha. It is not merely that the enjoyment involves many formalities; indeed, true satiation must come through the Teaching.

May all equally partake of the supreme flavor, and may all realize the perfect and eternal. May this occasion of the vegetarian feast serve as a cause for all to together achieve this assembly of Dharma-giving.

With single-minded devotion, we offer this sustenance to the entire Dharma-realm of the ten directions: to those in the four emptinesses and the four dhyānas, the various devas of the six heavens of desire, and the deities of the sun, moon, and stars.
The Sage Kings of the Celestial Court, together with all your retinues, we pray that you do not lose sight of your original nature;
receiving the majestic radiance of the Buddha, may you accept this offering this very evening at this present moment.

(The assembly offers harmonious incense and flowers; the *nāṇ* and *ghaṇṭā* are sounded. The following sections proceed by this example. The ritual master strikes the bell and recites verses, along with the hymns of praise.
The world reveres the four formless concentrations (*ārūpyasamādhi*) And the eighteen classes of the Brahma heavens of the four dhyānas;
Yet among these, the six Heavenly Kings of the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*) Delight themselves in the five desires beyond compare.
The sun, moon, and five planets align with the seven luminaries;
the North Star, the Big Dipper, and all the heavenly bodies—the Horn, the Neck, and the arrayed constellations—comprise the entire celestial sphere.

The eighty-four thousand calamitous transformations, along with the twelve palaces of the lunar stations and the six stems, are the rewards and punishments of the Celestial Bureau within the various heavenly palaces.
The myriad immortals and seers of the heavenly realms throughout the ten directions all simultaneously offer their service and support.

Now, having reached the summit of the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu*), one gazes upon the supreme state of ultimate reality; yet harboring a mind still subject to outflows (*āsrava*), one declines together with the passing of long years.
Furthermore, the four dhyānas belong to the category of false concentration, and the six heavens of desire do not transcend the sentiments of ordinary beings. Although [one may] follow...
Having long cultivated the ten wholesome deeds, how could one avoid being moved by the manifestation of the five signs of decay?

When the thousand lights shine upon the two paths and the myriad phenomena hang within the single heaven, one laments alone that the flower atop the crown has withered; yet how could one perceive that the arrow from the void has already fallen?
Possessing sovereign power and autonomy, you are a true immortal in the palaces of the upper realms; yet when rewards and punishments must be executed, you are truly [a being of] the lower...
Earth is the arbiter of human destiny; yet one may lose the power of merit after long cultivation. One must believe that the demon of death is certain and difficult to escape.
For those who lead toward the ultimate through skillful means, they surely reach the primordial source; for those who take birth according to karma, it is merely a transient, deluded retribution.
Amidst clouds concealing the towering jade palaces and winds raising the shimmering *zhuyi* robes, one holds the wondrous flower.
Wandering at ease, they savor the nectar of immortality to their heart's content; their minds are perpetually at leisure, and their joy is boundless.

Yet, when eighty thousand kalpas have ended, all shall vanish into emptiness, and the three-thousandfold world system will utterly submerge. When one assumes form within the mundane world, one still knows the time of hearing the Dharma and attaining the Way;

yet while seated cross-legged in the dark regions of existence, how could there be a place for liberation from suffering or release from transgression? Now, therefore, this extraordinary and supreme assembly is specially convened.
Universally delivering those wandering in the stream of delusion, may they, by the light of the Buddha-sun, come to partake of the offerings of this donor family.

May they personally receive the gift of the Dharma and豁然 (huò wù) awaken to the emptiness of nature. Let them not linger in attachment to the high heavens, but immediately ascend to the Land of Bliss. (The assembly joins in:
We take refuge and pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem.

With single-minded devotion, we offer this sustenance to all throughout the ten directions and the Dharma-realm, to the Five Peaks and Four Rivers, to those who dwell upon the earth and roam through the air, and to all deities of merit and virtue.
To the spirits enshrined in this temple, together with all their retinues:
we pray that you do not lose sight of your original nature, but, receiving the majestic radiance of the Buddha, may you accept this offering this very evening, at this very hour.
(Proclamation with Bell-Ringing and Verses of Praise) The Holy Lords of the Five Peaks together assist the Mandate;
The myriad perfected immortals of Fusang and the Water Palace;
The dragon deities of the Yangtze, Yellow, Huai, and Ji Rivers; And the Kings of the Four Great Oceans with all their retinues.

Flowers, fruits, gardens, groves, and the hundred grains; Droughts, locusts, calamities, and diseases—all are governed by the gods of the five directions and the Earth Deity Lords of their respective provinces.

Winds, rains, thunders, and lightnings, as well as the class of Mars (Yinghuo) and all the city-gods and temple-deities throughout the world— For those who have performed meritorious deeds and bestowed the Dharma, the imperial edict grants them temple enfeoffments.
The majestic spiritual power of the assembly of merits from the ten directions—on this single occasion, may they all together receive our offerings.
We humbly observe that the Honored Form is as a mountain peak, a great bulwark held in the highest esteem; its service is like thunder and lightning, and its supreme spirit is worthy of veneration.

It is the presiding lord over grain, fruits, gardens, and groves, and the official in charge of water, fire, wind, and rain. As the Dragon Lord dwelling in the seas and marshes, it guards the quarters.

In the earth-administrative offices of the quarters, the temples of city deities stand in rows; in the shrines of the neighborhoods, ancestral spirits gather. They stabilize the state and pacify the people, recording their great meritorious deeds in the annals of history.

They ward off calamities and protect against afflictions, binding their profound virtue to the hearts of men. They enjoy the titles of honor associated with princes and lords, manifesting the divine efficacy of Heaven and Earth.
They penetrate the Yin and Yang so that all things follow their proper order, and they ensure that rewards and punishments are surely executed. Thus, they assist...

Transformed during a flourishing era, it is fitting that its name be perpetuated in the regular sacrifices. To speak of "skillful means" (sankuśala-upāya) implies a temporary conformity with worldly affairs;

to speak of "true retribution" (vipāka) implies falling directly into heterodox thought. Thus we know that sacrificing with blood to nourish the flesh does not compare to purifying oneself through a disciplined mind.
There are many among the followers of excessive greed who have extensively constructed halls and pavilions, falsely claiming auspicious signs to manifest their own majesty and valor.
Being fundamentally ignorant of the True and Eternal, they ultimately fail to recognize where to take refuge; their evil habits increase ever more, and they are on the verge of hastening toward ruin.

Now, therefore, a supreme assembly is specially convened to universally deliver those wandering in delusion. We pray that, by the light of the Buddha-Sun, you will come to partake in the offerings of this donor family.
Having personally received the gift of the Dharma, one realizes the emptiness of nature. Do not harbor lingering attachments to the mundane world; immediately ascend to the Land of Bliss.
(Chorus: We take refuge in and pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem.
(The donor prostrates and the ritual master recites:

With single-minded devotion, we offer this sustenance to the kings and queens, the civil and military officials throughout the ten directions and the entire Dharma-realm, and to Confucius, the sage and founder of the Confucian tradition.
"O sages and recluses, together with all your retinues, we pray that you do not lose sight of your original nature;
by virtue of the Buddha’s majestic radiance, may you accept this offering this very evening."
(Statement of Intent, Ringing the Bell, and Verses of Praise).
The Four Holy Wheel-Turning Kings and their allied nations, The sovereign emperors, the principal consorts,
and the primary queens, The dukes, ministers, officials, and all renowned sages— All those of the hundred ranks, both civil and military.
The Supreme Sage and Great Confucianist honored the Way of Kong; the Four Categories and Ten Exemplars manifested the source of the Ru tradition.

The multitude of Brahmins are themselves the Rishis; here in this land, Laozi, Zhuangzi, and the other sages and immortals—such as Chao Fu and Xu You and the various recluses—as well as noble ladies, titled wives, and enfeoffed lords [are likewise included].
The lords and ministers of all lands in the ten directions simultaneously offer their service and offerings here at this one time.

For it is when the Sage Kings appear from time to time that they govern with wheels of gold, silver, copper, or iron; when enlightened sovereigns arise in succession, they grasp the scepter of the altars of soil and grain and the mountains and rivers.
Founding their bases and establishing the ultimate principles, they succeed to the throne and maintain the cultural legacy. They take the six realms as their home and unify the common people.

Originally, one becomes a son; yet if the ruler lacks virtue, he loses his station, and if the minister is not discreet, he ruins himself. Since these matters are so perilous, how can one not stand in awe?

To sustain the way of the world and look up to the Confucian tradition, one must rectify the mind and cultivate sincerity to manifest the subtle beginnings of things, and establish ritual and music to exalt its transformation.
Thus, the high officials and all the ministers shall possess the virtuous talent necessary to govern the state.
The generals and officers of the six armies possess the brilliant strategies for securing the borders;

the retired scholars and recluses, as well as the transcendents and those of feathered lineage, stand out with marks that transcend the mundane and sever worldly ties, having attained the arts of fixing destiny and prolonging life.

As for the multitude of queens, consorts, and ladies, along with the ranks of palace attendants and virtuous women: within the inner quarters they observe the conduct prescribed by the *Neize* (Inner Regulations), and within their private chambers they provide assistance in domestic affairs. Some emerge...

In various states of existence, whether wise or foolish, all are ultimately subject to the same end: death. Now, a preeminent assembly is specially convened to universally deliver those wandering in delusion.
We pray that you may receive the light of the Buddha-Sun and come to partake in this offering from the donor’s household.
Having personally heard the sublime Dharma, one suddenly awakens to true emptiness. Do not linger in the mundane world, but immediately ascend to the Land of Bliss.
(The assembly joins in: We take refuge in and pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem.
(The donor performs a prostration. The officiant recites:

With single-minded devotion, we offer this sustenance to those throughout the Dharma-realm of the ten directions: farmers, artisans, merchants, physicians, diviners, and those of miscellaneous occupations; the noble and the humble, men and women alike.
The ten classes of human beings, together with all their retinues, we pray that you do not lose sight of your original nature;
by receiving the majestic radiance of the Buddha, may you accept this offering this very evening, at this very moment.
(Confession, Ringing the Bell, and Recitation of Verses of Praise).
The ten classes of humanity follow ten habitual tendencies; Whether dull-witted or enlightened, they each form their own groups:
Farmers who toil in the fields, artisans of a hundred crafts, Sedentary merchants, itinerant traders, physicians, and diviners.

Serving superiors and honoring the public, from the various officials and soldiers down to the slaves and even the courtesans and performers—those who are truly loyal and filial have nothing to be ashamed of;
those who are unrighteous and lacking benevolence deserve punishment.
Poverty and wealth come from Heaven and are all predetermined; success and failure are matters of fate, not of human effort.
The countless multitudes of human beings throughout the ten directions, at this one moment, all together offer their service and offerings.
Since they descend from Heaven as its seed, they are ranked alongside the Three Powers; having received a human form, they have maintained the Five Precepts through past lives.
Thus, they possess not only the capacity for the Way, but it must be known that they are fully endowed with the conditions for attaining Buddhahood. As for loyalty and filial piety...

Those who strive in cultivation and those who are corrupt and greedy cannot be transformed by one another; this is because their natures and habits are so far apart that good and evil result in such different outcomes.
Among the four classes of people—scholars, farmers, artisans, and merchants—there are ten categories distinguished by their dullness or intelligence and their insight or proficiency.

As for those engaged in medicine, divination, and astrology, as well as those in technical arts, performance, and entertainment, men and women each find their own kind, and the hierarchy of high and low does not lose its proper order.
Within the lands of the named teachings (Confucianism), there are none who are not of the gentry class; yet in distant and neighboring foreign states, there are many of simple and upright conduct.

That longevity and brevity of life, or poverty and success, are met with such retributions—how can one speak of the suffering of the widowed, the orphaned, and the solitary? They know only to tread the wheel of birth and death;
how could they enter the realm of the sages and worthies? With their original clarity shining outwardly, they ultimately turn their backs on and lose their fundamental mind.

As various karmas converge and incline, one is about to drift and fall into other realms of existence. Now, a supreme assembly is specially convened to universally deliver those wandering in delusion.

May they, by virtue of the light of the Buddha-sun, come to partake of the offerings of this donor family; may they personally receive the gift of the Dharma and attain the sudden awakening to the emptiness of nature.
Do not cling to this decaying body; ascend immediately to the Land of Bliss. (The assembly chants in unison: We take refuge in and pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem.
(The patron prostrates. The ritual master recites:)
With single-minded devotion, they offer worship to all beings throughout the ten directions and the Dharma-realm— those born from the four modes of birth, those comprised within the five destinies,
the hosts of asuras dwelling among the mountains and at the bottom of the ocean, together with all their retinues.
I only pray that you will not lose sight of your original nature. By virtue of the Buddha’s majestic radiance, may you accept this offering at this very moment tonight.
(The presiding priest rings the bell and recites the verses of praise.)
Know that those included among the gods of miraculous birth sustain the world and dwell as neighbors to the heavens, rivaling the sun and moon;
those of womb-birth protect the Dharma and possess supernormal powers, sharing the realm of spirits;
some dwell in the void by day and return to the waters for their lodging at night—be certain that these types are comparable to the animal realm.
The four modes of birth and five destinies encompass all beings; those dwelling north of Mount Sumeru, who have entered deep into the ocean, form one class among the various realms.
Known as the most inferior and possessing little majestic power, the hosts of the Asura path are immeasurable; at this very moment, they all together offer their worship.

I humbly reflect that by practicing the ten wholesome deeds in past lives, I merely established the causes for the lower grade of rebirth. By distinguishing myself from the four modes of birth, I have consequently experienced the fruit of an inferior mind.

I have focused exclusively on benefiting myself and frequently acted to surpass others; thus, though my merit was strong, its retribution was not of the celestial kind. Though my physical form was immense, my hands could only obstruct the sun.
Dwelling amidst the mountains of various forms, my majesty was perhaps deficient; yet residing at the bottom of the great salt ocean, [my power remained vast].

The depths they enter are most profound. There, jeweled nets and carved railings reflect the dappled shadows of swaying trees; wondrous flowers and famous gardens resound with the harmonious calls of various birds.
Yet, when they dwell in the palace and burn incense, the instruments of suffering appear before them during the three periods of the day;

when they partake of food and drink, it turns into green mud within a single mouth. This is what is meant by being encompassed by the evil realms (durgati). It is surely due to the stubbornness of their false views (mithyādṛṣṭi). Those who possess...
Upon hearing the words of the maiden Manoharā, he suddenly gave rise to anger and went to battle with Śakra.
In the end, he suffered defeat and fled into the hollow of a lotus stalk. He must have felt great shame; yet, taking the moon as an ear-ornament was merely an act of arrogance.

He thought only of what was unwholesome; how could he be said to understand non-contention? Constantly harboring violence and cruelty, he took ghosts and beasts as his companions, utterly devoid of a compassionate heart.
Who among the heavenly beings has not looked with hope? Now, this extraordinary and supreme assembly is specially convened to universally deliver those wandering in delusion.

We pray that, by the light of the Buddha-Sun, you will come to partake in the offerings of the donor family, personally receive the gift of the Dharma, and awaken to the emptiness of inherent nature. Do not cling to this wretched body;
may you attain rebirth in the Land of Bliss. (The assembly chants in unison: We take refuge and prostrate ourselves before the eternally abiding Triple Gem.
(The donor prostrates. The ritual master recites:

With single-minded devotion, we offer this sustenance to the King of the Flaming Mouths throughout the ten directions and the dharma-realm, and to the various classes of hungry ghosts of the three grades and nine categories.
May the spirits of those who died untimely deaths, together with all their kinsmen and retinues, by no means lose sight of their original nature;
through the majestic radiance of the Buddha, may they receive this offering this very evening at this present moment.
(Proclamation with Bell and Verses of Praise):
Among all hungry ghosts, this is named "Flaming Mouth. Because the provisional leads to the ultimate, it is called the "King of Wealth.
How could these three grades of distribution lack a cause? One sees here the thousandfold differences in karmic retribution.
Those who consume blood and those who consume incense are not of a single class; they take their names from whether they dwell among the mountains or by the waters.
Beneath Jambudvīpa lies a dark and secluded region, where some reside within the Cakravāḍa mountains to expiate their past offenses.
There are also yakṣas, rākṣasas, and other spirits, including those who have met with untimely deaths or perished in various injuries.
The hungry ghosts and solitary spirits of the ten directions all receive offerings at this one time.
For they have practiced the karma of stinginess and greed; being no longer auspicious persons, they have received these hideous forms and are thus called "hungry ghosts."
Consequently, their throats hang down with massive goiters, their bellies rise up like high mountains, their feet resemble withered firewood, and their faces are like those of malevolent beasts.
Torches burn perpetually from their mouths, and needle-like bristles constantly pierce their bodies. Not only is their suffering beyond words, but their ravenous hunger cannot be told.
They dwell in the subterranean realm beneath Jambudvīpa, occupying separate abodes within the Cakravāḍa Mountains. These are the common denizens...
In desolate regions where trees and grasses grow wild, as well as in bustling city streets and marketplaces, such cases are indeed numerous.

When will they find liberation? Lacking skillful application of the mind, what benefit is there in whipping a corpse beneath a tomb? They still know how to seek their livelihood, making a plan by begging for food among men;
yet when it comes to losing their lives through being burned or drowned, or taking their own lives by cutting their throats or hanging themselves—[what can be done then?]
As for those whose bodies have been harmed—those who have met with untimely death or perished—all are victims of injury and loss. Their solitary spirits drift aimlessly without support;
the long night stretches on interminably without dawn. To cry out "water, water" would be of no avail here within this city of ghosts; to mutter "knife, knife" in one's sleep is likewise futile.
"In the treasuries of our King, there is nothing like this. Now, a particularly sublime assembly is convened to universally deliver those wandering in delusion.

Do not linger in the dark regions, but immediately ascend to the Land of Bliss. (The assembly chants in unison: "We take refuge and pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem."
