With single-minded devotion, we offer this tribute to the King of Yama, the Ten Kings of the Underworld, and their divine sisters throughout the Dharma-realm of the ten directions.

May all the officials of the various bureaus, together with their kinsmen and retinues, never lose sight of their original nature; may they receive this offering this very evening, sustained by the majestic radiance of the Buddha.
(Proclamation and Bell-Ringing for the Recitation of Verses of Praise) Truly, the Ten Kings dwell beneath the earth; Yama is the most honored title they receive.
Even this divine sister shares in their authority, Along with the two youths of good and evil and all the female officials.
The eighteen great ministers once took an oath, Together administering justice to repay their original vows.
Hóngjiājin and the others are firm and majestic; A host of malevolent spirits all assist in governance.
The karmic mirror and fire-pearls constantly reflect and illuminate, While the officials of the various bureaus maintain impartiality.
The various deities and officials of the underworld in the ten directions all present offerings at this one time.
For it is when a virtuous mind first arises that the precious palace of the heavens is first completed; when an evil thought merely sprouts, the fiery city of the lower realms is already prepared.
Thus we know that the karmic actions currently arising may be used to prognosticate the conditions for future retribution. Only Yama...
The supreme deity Māra dwells in the dark realm of the *naraka* hells. There, lotus ponds are arrayed in four directions and networks of bells hang in seven tiers.
Flocks of birds sing in harmony and fragrant breezes waft with perfume. Here, suffering and pleasure are experienced in alternation.

Because the elder brother and his younger sister were both kings, yet lacked virtue from the start, they made a wicked vow out of extreme anger; now the fruit has ripened upon themselves, and they are struck down.

To pour molten copper upon heated iron—let alone eighteen great ministers and a million elite soldiers—was made possible because they possessed at that time the vow to assist in the administration of justice;
thus, on this day, each has attained the title of presiding official over their respective domains.
As for the judges who oversee the court dockets and the youths who hold the legal documents, there is certainly no need for further interrogation or cross-examination.

In the realms of wrongful punishment, excess, burning heat, and freezing cold, how could there not be bitter suffering? That these powers are not exclusively wielded by various deities, but are truly the force of sentient beings' own karmic resonance, is clear.
Long entangled in delusive habits, they have needlessly remained imprisoned throughout vast kalpas. To turn back toward true cultivation, nothing is required but the illumination of one's own mind.
Now, this extraordinary and supreme assembly is specially convened to universally deliver the wandering stream of beings; may you all fortunately avail yourselves of the light of the Buddha-sun.
Having come to attend the offerings of this donor family, you have personally received the gift of the Dharma and attained a clear realization of the emptiness of nature.
Do not linger in the dark realm of Yama, but ascend immediately to the Land of Bliss. (Chorus: We take refuge and pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem.
(The donor prostrates. The ritual master recites:
With single-minded devotion, we offer this sustenance to all within the ten directions and the Dharma-realm, including those in the eight hot and eight cold great hells, and all solitary hells.
May the suffering prisoners, together with all their kinsmen, remain undeluded regarding their original nature;
through the majestic radiance of the Buddha, may they receive this offering this very night at this very hour.
(Proclamation with Ringing of the Bell and Recitation of Verses of Praise) The eight hot hells reside precisely in Jambudvīpa; At the four gates, sixteen increase-lands surround them.
One must know that the peripheral dwellings lie beyond the Cakravāḍa Mountains; These are the locations of the eight cold hells.
Upon the Sword-Trees and Knife-Mountains one suffers one’s own calamities; From the iron balls and molten copper, suffering is hard to escape.
In this great Avīci Hell for the wicked and rebellious, There has been no liberation for countless kalpas.
Separately, there is the Tai Shan Prison for the Orphans and Solitary, Where the City God and Temple Spirits oversee those who have recently died.
The multitude of prisoners in the hells of the ten directions simultaneously present offerings at this one time.

Having formerly slandered the Triple Gem, they lacked any sincerity of refuge and reverence; they were rebellious toward their two parents and failed to mind the foundation of their own birth and upbringing.

Whether it be the full commission of offenses through the six sense faculties or the solitary performance of a single karma—even for those whose transgressions are slight, the retribution is likewise severe.
Subtle! Yet when a transgression is great, the punishment is likewise great. This is produced by the mind; it is summoned by oneself. It is like writing at night:

though the fire is extinguished, the characters remain. Or like a mirror at dawn: when the form approaches, the reflection appears. There are the karmic maturations of extreme heat and extreme cold, where evil causes and evil effects correspond with one another.
Between the two *Kakara* mountains, neither the sun, the moon, nor the divine deities shed their light. [In] Jambudvīpa...
Descending into the eight hells, iron, copper, stones, and fire are arrayed in succession. When the wind blows upon the sword-trees, the entire body is pierced and wounded;
when the boiling cauldrons and the ash-rivers surge, the whole body is mangled and putrefied. Having already been hacked by axes and hatchets, one is further bitten by jackals and wolves.
The *naraka* are called "evil persons," and Yama-rāja is the progenitor of the hells.

As for those solitary and desolate wildernesses, they arise from the lightness and frivolity of individual karma. Because one does not understand the true emptiness of self-nature, one cannot escape the false retribution of this time.
For vast and distant kalpas, who knows the period of liberation? The souls sink away into infinity.
Who would have thought that those dwelling in delusion could now be specially gathered for this supreme assembly to universally deliver these captive souls?
We pray that by the light of the Buddha-Sun, we may attend the offerings of the donors, personally hear the wondrous Dharma, and suddenly awaken to the Perfect Vehicle.
May we never again enter the dark regions, but immediately ascend to the Land of Bliss. (The assembly joins in: We take refuge and pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem.
(The donor performs a prostration. The ritual master recites:

"With single-minded devotion, we offer this sustenance to all beings throughout the ten directions and the Dharma-realm, within the Iron Ring Mountains and across the five destinies—namely, the ten classes of animals with scales, shells, feathers, and fur, together with their retinues."
I only pray that you will not lose sight of your original nature. By virtue of the Buddha’s majestic radiance, may you accept this offering at this very moment tonight.
(The ritual master rings the bell and recites the verses of praise.)
The lion and the elephant king manifest great merit and virtue; the tortoise, dragon, qilin, and phoenix respond to auspicious omens.
Crows, ravens, swallows, and sparrows are among the winged birds; oxen, horses, dogs, and sheep are the running beasts.
Crocodiles, turtles, fish, and shrimp are named the aquatic species; mosquitoes, gadflies, flies, and ants are the most minute of living beings.
Vipers, snakes, bees, and scorpions possess hearts of potent venom; scales, shells, feathers, and fur are received according to one’s karma.
Dwellings within the Iron Ring Mountains and the islands of the sea surround the five destinies on the periphery.
All the various classes of sentient beings throughout the ten directions simultaneously present offerings here.

I humbly reflect that, having been endowed with a nature of ignorance and folly, my right view is utterly contrary [to the truth]. Having received a base and inferior form, I am designated as a "sideways-born" being (*tiryagyoni*).

Our dwellings differ—whether in water, on land, or in the air—and we are divided into the various groups of fish, birds, and beasts. Among the four modes of birth—womb, egg, moisture, and transformation—there are ten categories of beings who experience fortune or misfortune.
When a phoenix cries, it portends auspicious signs; when a great Peng bird gathers, it indicates calamity and decline. [Even those who] swallow the hook...

The bait for the fish reveals its excessive greed; the light of the fire exposes the moth’s lack of awareness. Though one possesses the wisdom of prior knowledge, how can one avoid having one's intestines carved out?
Though one has the merit of carrying heavy burdens, it ultimately ends in the dissolution of the body. By using the great to control the small—
Thus they devour one another, meeting their retribution according to their karma and repaying each other in turn. To lament this mutual destruction, when will it ever come to an end?

As for those who set out nets and spread snares to prematurely end their lives, or trigger traps and lay pits to injure their existence—when their blood stains the blade and chopping block, and their bodies are ultimately ground to pulp in cauldrons and vats—they harbor extreme suffering within them forever.
They bind themselves with deep-seated resentment; thus, with their own fat and marrow, they satiate the mouths and bellies of the unrighteous.
Such cruel punishment is not inflicted as a random retribution; when one examines its prior causes, it is truly the result of one's own evil cultivation.

Now, this extraordinary and supreme assembly is specially convened to universally deliver those wandering in delusion. May we, by the light of the Buddha-sun, be granted the opportunity to attend the offerings of the donor family;
may we personally receive the gift of the Dharma and attain the clear realization of the emptiness of nature. Let us not cling to this wretched body, but immediately ascend to the Land of Bliss.
(The assembly joins in: We take refuge and pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem.
(The donor prostrates and the ritual master recites:

With a single mind, we offer this sustenance to all beings throughout the ten directions and the entire Dharma-realm who have undergone seven births and seven deaths, wandering through the various realms of existence within these forty-nine days.
To the beings of the intermediate state and their retinues:
we pray that you do not lose sight of your original nature; by receiving the majestic radiance of the Buddha, may you accept this offering this very evening.
(Statement of Declaration, Ringing the Bell, and Verses of Praise) The *pudgala* is a being who undergoes repeated rebirth;
having been born for seven days, it was all too hurried.
Now that these seven times seven days have just concluded, it will certainly undergo rebirth, turning according to its karma.
Wandering through the seven realms of rebirth without a moment’s rest, Traversing the four continents with no leisure to dwell;
Briefly categorized as seventeen types of conventional names, These beings are perceived solely by the divine eye.
Distinct hells further divide merit and demerit, Where one receives retribution according to the mind, stirred by the subtle winds.
Alas, these multitudes in the intermediate state (antarābhava) are infinite; at this one moment, they all together present offerings.

We humbly observe that their appearance and disappearance follow conditions, like the presence or absence of reflections in a mirror; their ascent and descent according to karma are like the rising and falling of a waterwheel.
We contemplate the arrival of the five signs of decay in the heavens, the transition of the four marks in the human realm, and the emergence from the three miserable paths.
There is no confusion regarding the chaotic comings and goings among the various realms of existence. Those whose good or evil karma is extremely heavy will immediately experience retribution;

however, for those whose causes and fruits are somewhat lighter, they must wait for the proper time. Since they have not yet obtained a physical body, they temporarily return to the intermediate state (*antarābhava*).
How are the cycles of birth and death determined? They arise from the shifting of sins and merits. In an instant they come to an end; their lifespan is fixed at seven days.
They exist through transformation, their physical form resembling that of a small child. From moment to moment there is no stability; one form follows after another in succession.

Although consciousness is sharp and acute, its nature is fundamentally obscure and dull. It does not exist apart from the midst of the myriad dharmas, yet it is forcibly designated as being outside the six realms.
While those with the divine eye should certainly be able to see it, none but the Buddha-mind can know it exhaustively. If it has no refuge such as this, it is truly pitiable;
it wanders through delusive realms, following its emotions in a continuous chain. Only by turning back to enter the gate of cultivation can one reach the attainment of the Way.
Only now has this period of cessation concluded; we now specially convene this supreme assembly to universally deliver those lost in delusion.

We pray that you will avail yourselves of the light of the Buddha-sun to attend the offerings of this donor family. May you personally receive this Dharma-gift and suddenly awaken to the Perfect Vehicle, no longer clinging to this decaying body.
They immediately ascend to the Land of Bliss. (The assembly recites in unison: "We take refuge in and pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem.
(The patron performs prostrations, recites the formal declaration, chants the dhāraṇī, and presents offerings.)
Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses a mantra for making offerings. I shall now reverently recite it:
*Oṃ gaganasvabhāva-vajra hūṃ*. (Having recited the mantra three times, ring the hand-bell.
(The Dharma Master visualizes that the ten ranks of holy and mundane beings below the hall, by virtue of this Dharma-power, all receive the offerings. (The Ritual Official addresses them, saying:)
May, by means of this secret and inconceivable perfuming, cause all subtle delicacies to be transformed into Dharma-offerings for the six realms of existence.
May the myriad spirits of the ten stages be universally sustained at once, with nothing left unreached.
(The donor prostrates; the ritual master recites:)
With single-minded devotion, we make offerings to the City God and the deities of the various temples, the spirits enshrined in the ancestral shrines of the counties,
districts, and wards, and the assembly of Princes, together with all their retinues.
We pray that you will not lose sight of your original nature and, receiving the majestic radiance of the Buddha, accept these offerings this very evening at this very hour.
(Statement of Intent, Ringing the Bell, and Reciting Verses of Praise) At the Temple of the Spirituous Protection of the Prefectural City God:
Majestic is the Prefectural Lord, manifesting his awe-inspiring divinity;
From antiquity, he has been enshrined for his auspicious administration of justice, like Gao Yao; His meritorious virtue is now honored here with this consecrated temple.
The Great Ming Kings and the various sages of antiquity; The Generals with their banners atop the prefectural towers;
These worthies and saints, honored as the most venerable within the city; The majestic Sea Deities who receive offerings in their temples;
The local deities of monasteries, pagodas, and government offices; And even the Five-Attainment Spirits of every alleyway.
The various spirit shrines throughout the city walls and its subordinate counties all simultaneously offered their worship and offerings here.

We humbly submit that the rainbow-colored beams press down upon the waters, commanding the vital thoroughfares both above and below; the battlements reach toward the clouds, magnificently marking the capital of the southeastern region.
With its towering official buildings and densely packed private dwellings, there must surely be true spirits who together provide protection and shelter. For this reason:
In the temples arrayed for the City God and the shrines clustered in villages and towns, all the various deities manifest themselves so that their sacrifices may be successfully offered.
Monumental steles stand prominently to clearly display their honorary titles, while deep halls open wide to reverently enshrine their true images.

Without exception, they establish merit and bestow the Dharma, assisting the state and bringing peace to the people. To respond in humility to prayers for protection, they invariably manifest their great majesty and prowess. As for all military...
During times of martial calamity and hardship, as well as periods of flood, drought, disease, and pestilence, whatever one seeks, there is nothing that is not answered.
Yet, they merely enjoy offerings of blood; they have never ceased from taking life. Possessing no heart of compassion, what consideration do they have for repaying such service?

Now, a special and supreme assembly is convened to universally save all classes of beings. We pray that, by the light of the Buddha-sun, you will come to partake in this offering from the donor family, personally hear the wondrous Dharma, and suddenly awaken to the Perfect Vehicle.
Do not linger in the mundane world, but ascend immediately to the Land of Bliss.
(The assembly joins in: We take refuge and pay homage to the Three Jewels, which abide forever.
(The donor prostrates and the ritual master recites:

With single-minded devotion, we offer this sustenance to the various temple lords and kings within our neighboring districts and local jurisdictions, to the six deities who dwell therein, and to the ancestral spirits of our households.
Together with all your retinues, we pray that you do not lose sight of your original nature. By virtue of the Buddha’s majestic radiance, may you accept this offering at this very moment tonight.
(The ritual master rings the bell and recites the verses of praise.)
The local Magistrate Wang has recently been enshrined to receive offerings at the various temples;

furthermore, all the myriad deities residing within our borders dwell in the central chamber as Great Bright Kings. The various deities of the gates and doors, along with those presiding over the hearth, the well, and the courtyard, all perform their duties:
the Father of the Bedchamber, the Mother of the Bedchamber, and the Lady of the Latrine.
The deities of the cardinal directions and the Tai-sui, the local chieftains and tutelary spirits, the various gods of the household hearth and the ancestral altars,
those residing in storehouses and shops, as well as those of the fields, mountains, vegetable gardens, and burial grounds—
may all these spirits of merit and virtue be honored with offerings here and now, at this very moment.

I humbly reflect that by manifesting supreme spiritual power, one protects all creatures and provides great shelter to one's local community; by clarifying and making manifest the faith with which one serves the deities, one establishes the ancestral temple rites.
Considering how we gather under a roof to dwell, we recognize the honored status of the *zhongliu* (central chamber); thus, we observe the prohibitions and taboos within each quarter of the dwelling.
I respectfully enter and exit through the gates; the hearth is dedicated solely to the preparation of food and drink; the well provides for the needs of water and springs;
the bed ensures constant peace and security; and the latrine relies upon its secret protection. Having personally received the Buddha’s entrustment, do not recklessly disturb human dwellings.
The spirits of non-action feel shame; we hope they will silently assist in supporting the world’s blessings.

As for the installation of image-positions within households, the presence of earth-deities at gravesites, the demarcation of boundaries for fields and mountains, and the great abundance of stores in granaries and treasuries—in all such locations, there are presiding officials.
If they are upright and pure, they merely receive incense and lamps; however, if they are corrupt and greedy, then...
They seek flesh and blood at will; such evil habits are difficult to describe in full. If this is a provisional bestowal, then its practice lies in benefiting others.
If it is a true retribution, then the karma invites suffering upon oneself. Having been endowed from birth with intelligent wisdom, yet one cannot avoid perverse thoughts;

not knowing the eternally abiding mind, how can one seek awakened insight? Now, a supreme assembly is specially convened to universally deliver those wandering in delusion. May [this merit], by reason of...
The light of the Buddha-sun has come to attend the offerings of the donor’s household. Greatly benefiting from this Dharma-gift, one realizes the emptiness of inherent nature.
Do not linger in the mundane world, but ascend immediately to the Land of Bliss. (Chorus: We take refuge and prostrate to the eternally abiding Triple Gem.
(The donor performs a prostration. The ritual master recites:

With single-minded devotion, we offer this tribute to the spirits of our ancestors and deceased kin of former generations, as well as to the various divine presences of teachers, friends, and relatives.
Together with all your retinues, we pray that you do not lose sight of your original nature. By virtue of the Buddha’s majestic radiance, may you accept this offering at this very moment tonight.
(The ritual master rings the bell and recites the verses of praise.)
When heaven and earth were divided, the Way of Humanity was established; the first to receive a surname was the beginning of all.
We reverently offer blessings to our primordial ancestor, as well as our great-grandparents, grandparents, and parents.
Should they still be alive, may they be sustained with fortune and longevity; should they have already passed away, may they surely ascend to higher realms.

As for uncles and paternal aunts, elder brothers and younger brothers—wherein there is no lack of mutual affection and respect—and likewise teachers, friends, and maternal relatives, as well as mothers and their kin:
now, having opened [the gates of liberation], I do not neglect even those far away;
all men and women of this world are my kin, and at this very moment, I offer them all sustenance.
I humbly submit that it is because of the ancestral blessings bestowed by our imperial lineages that we are able to leave enduring prosperity for future generations;

and through the subtle influence of Buddhist merit, one may achieve posthumous honor for one’s ancestors. Thus, in honoring the predecessors and contemplating filial piety, nothing compares to exalting their virtue and recompensing them for their achievements.
Thus, from those who followed their ancestors and great-grandparents down to their own parents, once their spirits have been transferred to a bright age, some may attend to them in their later years.
If they maintain right views, they will return to the human realm; if they commit grave transgressions, they will ultimately sink into the lower realms.

Even if they indulge in celestial pleasures, how can they escape the five signs of decay? Even if they attain the body of an immortal, they must still return to the various destinies. This is the reality of the struggle.
They contend and give rise to great fury; they pursue what flies and runs to create erratic movements. When the numinous wind blows with solemnity, they recognize it as a spirit;
when the fire of hunger blazes fiercely, they call it a ghost. Appearing and disappearing within the realms of the four modes of birth, they fail to consider transcending these boundaries;

revolving upon the wheel of the six paths of existence, when will they ever find rest? There are those who diligently cultivate supreme practice and deeply realize the Perfect Vehicle, contemplating the mysteries...
Realizing the state of non-arising, one shall surely ascend to the highest grade. Throughout the entire earth, there are none who are not kin; all become conditions for deliverance.

Across kalpas of time, even those who were enemies shall all be moved to thoughts of reconciliation. Now, this extraordinary and sublime assembly is specially opened to universally ferry across the deluded masses.
We pray that, by the light of the Buddha-sun, you will come to partake of the offerings of this donor family. We rejoice to hear [your arrival].
Through the wondrous Dharma, one suddenly awakens to true emptiness; do not linger in the mundane world, but immediately ascend to the Land of Bliss.
(Chorus) We take refuge and pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem.
(The donor prostrates and the officiant recites:
With single-minded devotion, we offer this tribute (to the spiritual form of the deceased, [Name]).
We pray that you shall not lose sight of your original nature, but by receiving the majestic radiance of the Buddha, partake of this offering this very evening.
(The donor performs prostrations, recites the declaration, and offers mantras and offerings.
The Tathāgata, our Buddha, possesses a mantra for making offerings.
I shall now respectfully recite it: Oṃ gaganasvabhāva-vajra hūṃ.

(After reciting the mantra three times, ring the hand-bell and cymbals. (The Dharma Master visualizes that the assembly of deities present at the altar, as well as the deceased spirits, receive these offerings by virtue of this Dharma power. (The Ritual Master addresses them, saying:)
By virtue of this secret, inconceivable perfuming, may all coarse and inferior offerings be transformed into sublime provisions.
May they universally sustain the assembly of deities and the departed spirits alike, reaching everywhere without exception.
(Recite the ritual prose while ringing the bell to present the six kinds of offerings. Speak as follows:)
The lamp of wisdom dispels the radiance of the night moon; the water of meditative concentration reflects the hue of the autumn sky.
The myriad practices of the *Avataṃsaka* bring the fruit of the One Vehicle to fulfillment. Those who enter this chamber hear only the fragrance of the virtues of all Buddhas;

those who cultivate such contemplation see only the food of dhyāna-joy and Dharma-delight. There is nothing that is not simultaneously phenomenon and principle, neither form nor mind, as all converge upon the True Source.
May this perfect and wondrous offering be accomplished.
Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses a mantra for universal offering which I shall now reverently recite: Oṃ akara akara sarvabuddha-dharmapūjye svāhā.

(Recite the mantra three times. Then, strike the gongs. (The Dharma Master visualizes all sentient beings of the six realms within the dharma-realm, as well as the various deities present at the assembly and the spirits of the deceased, who, by virtue of this dharma-power, shall all receive these six kinds of sublime offerings.)
All are fully provided for. (The ritual master strikes the bell and performs the rite of offering, saying:

Having fully practiced the methods of the fast and entered the gates of the teachings, one must recognize that all phenomena are but manifestations, which ultimately return to the ultimate principle (*tattva*).

Therefore, with focused resolve and intent, kneeling and bowing the head, burning incense and scattering flowers, lighting lamps and presenting food—all these acts serve to support and perfect the realization of the Perfect [Dharma].

Contemplation: May all together assist in manifesting the True Cause. Although there are many aspects according to the ritual procedures, if one follows wisdom, none of them fail to be the Three Truths.

Thus, if one wishes to know this Way, how could it lie outside this school? To realize that the nature and characteristics of the myriad dharmas are all empty is itself the contemplation of reality in a single thought-moment.
Furthermore, one must recite the scriptures spoken by the Sage so as to bring them into accord with one's own self.
Having attained the spiritual insight of understanding and awakened to the locus of practice, this is what constitutes the truth. Within all forms of offering, this is shown to be supreme.
The Buddha Tathāgata possesses a mantra for the offering of Dharma; I shall now reverently recite it.
Oṃ sarvatathāgatābhisekamahāpūjāmudrāspharaṇasamaye hūṃ.

(After reciting the mantra three times, strike the gong. (The Dharma Master should know that all the offerings presented previously were material gifts (*āmiṣadāna*). Now, reciting the Mahāyāna is the gift of Dharma (*dharmadāna*). Material wealth sustains life and serves only to support meritorious deeds.)

The Dharma is used to open up one's nature; this is the Perfection of Wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*). When these two forms of giving operate together, they are then called the Way of Universal Salvation. Furthermore, since all preceding material gifts are embodied through the skillful means of wise observation, one knows that every act of service is nothing other than the gift of Dharma.

Outside of the Dharma there is no material gift, and outside of material gifts there is no Dharma. The two gifts are equal, both being identical with the Three Truths. When one contemplates in this way, the myriad beings of the six realms all receive the joy of the Dharma and each attains liberation.
(Recite a scripture or a mantra as the ritual master leads the assembly in circumambulation. Upon completion, recite verses for the dedication of merit; there is no need for elaborate words.)
May these merits be universally shared with all; may we and all sentient beings together attain the Way of the Buddha.
(The assembly sounds the hand-bells and gongs; they invite the Dharma Master to ascend the seat and deliver the essential teachings.)
The Ritual Manual for the Auspicious Assembly of the Dharma Realm’s Holy and Mundane Beings on Land and Water, Scroll Five.
The Ritual Manual for the Auspicious Assembly of the Dharma Realm’s Holy and Mundane Beings on Land and Water, Scroll Six.
Respectfully compiled by the Śramaṇa Zhìpán of Donghú, Sīmíng, during the Song Dynasty.
Revised by the later student Zuhong of Yunqi in Ancient Hangzhou.

(The Dharma Master ascends the seat at the site of practice and expounds the essentials of the Dharma for the sake of the six realms of existence. He points the way back to the Pure Land and instructs them to cultivate the samādhi of Buddha-recitation, seeking rebirth through aspiration.)
You disciples of the Buddha within the six realms of existence, since entering the Dharma hall, have repeatedly heard the essential teachings.
These include the arousal of perfect and eternal right faith, taking refuge in the Three Jewels of the Single Essence, practicing the Mahāyāna repentance, and establishing the Four Great Vows.
Furthermore, you have obtained the hearing of the wondrous precepts of the Mahāyāna—the law of non-action—and even offered a single incense stick, a single flower, a bright lamp, or food.
Banners, pennants, and necklaces; songs, hymns, and praises; and offerings of the six sensory objects—all these interpenetrate one another in a pervasive adornment.
Each and every one of them clearly elucidates the matter of the *Lotus Sūtra*’s revelation and manifestation, ultimately and perfectly fusing the principle of the three truths.

This is intended to cause you all to develop wondrous understanding and realize that these myriad phenomena are nothing but the single mind. Contemplate this single mind with precision: it is fundamentally ungraspable.

All things are created according to the mind; they do not obstruct dependent origination. Whether relying on the objective support or the subjective focus, whether form or mind—when observed through sublime contemplation, there is nothing that is not the sublime Dharma.
However, this land is turbid and evil, with heavy hindrances and dull faculties; thus, even if one makes progress in cultivation, it is difficult to achieve realization.
I look up with gratitude to the Tathāgata’s extraordinary skillful means, namely the Samādhi of Contemplating the Buddha, which enables one to [focus] upon Amitābha.
The Buddha’s Land of Ultimate Bliss is a pure land; by focusing the mind with single-minded devotion, one attains rebirth there.

Our Śākyamuni World-Honored One, however, dwells in this Sahā world, which is called an extremely painful and defiled land. Because it is characterized by subduing [afflictions], its ground is filled with sand, mud, thorns, and brambles, and it is replete with the evil realms.
At that time, cold and heat, day and night, shift and change in impermanence. Its inhabitants are born from a womb, and as for males—
Women are crowded together; their clothing and food are meager, and they labor diligently at their tasks. Their sustenance is coarse and fragmented, which only increases their karmic obstructions.
Their lifespans are short and precarious, uncertain from morning until evening. By demonstrating these various sufferings, he teaches people to give rise to a mind of great revulsion.
He then gathers them in by means of that Buddha-world called the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss (*Sukhāvatī*). Its ground consists of jewel-pools and crystal...
The garden was free of the three evil realms and possessed pure radiance. At that time, there were no cold or heat, nor day or night.

Those people were born by transformation within lotus flowers, possessing exclusively the marks of a great man (*mahāpuruṣa*). Their food and clothing arrived according to their thoughts, being rare, exquisite, and wondrous;
they experienced only the joy of the Dharma (*dharmaprīti*). Their lifespan was equal to that of the Buddha, long and immeasurable. Having displayed such various matters of bliss, he taught them.

When people give rise to this thought, they develop great admiration and longing. Therefore, the World-Honored One, prompted by Vaidehī, expounded the sixteen sublime contemplations as the essential method for seeking rebirth.
First, the contemplation of the setting sun is intended to establish a mental image of the Western Quarter, thereby directing one’s mind toward that Buddha.
This is truly because the mind capable of such visualization inherently possesses all phenomena of both the environment and its inhabitants (*niśraya-vastu* and *sattva-vastu*). Now...
With a mind that is like the sun, one contemplates the sun within this very mind, causing the sun of its original nature to manifest before one.

Since both the mind and the sun are the Dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), one who performs this contemplation is said to have perfected the "contemplation of the sun. As it is with the contemplation of the sun, so it is with the others.
The remaining contemplations follow this same pattern. Next, one contemplates the water, the earth, the trees, the ponds, and performs a general contemplation;
these six contemplations all observe the environment and resources (*niśraya-vipāka*) of that land. Next, one contemplates the seat, the image, the Buddha, and the two bodhisattvas.
The Universal Contemplation and the Miscellaneous Contemplation—these seven contemplations all observe the primary retribution (*vipāka-phala*) of that land.
The subsequent three contemplations observe the rebirth of the three grades and nine ranks, causing them to abandon inferior states and attain the superior. Furthermore, the Sūtra says:
"This mind makes the Buddha; this mind is the Buddha. To say "this mind makes the Buddha" reveals that Buddhahood arises from cultivation and is not spontaneous; it is entirely...

It is thus created. Because the inherent nature (xing) is fully realized through cultivation (xiu), it is said that "the mind creates. To say "this is the Buddha" reveals that the Buddha is fundamentally and inherently possessed;
he is not obtained through cultivation. Because the entirety of creation is this [Buddha], and the entirety of cultivation perfects the nature, it is said that "the mind is [the Buddha].

You multitudes of spirits within the six realms, if you understand this wondrous meaning, you should practice contemplation according to the Dharma and cultivate this samādhi. This is then, by virtue of—
Through the power of samādhi, through the power of the Buddha’s sustaining grace, and through the power of one's own original merit—

by uniting these three powers at once and perfecting the fruition in a single thought-moment— one may, without leaving one's current location, sit upon a precious lotus flower, not exceeding a single kṣaṇa.
To be reborn in that land, one must immediately practice mindfulness of the Buddha, aspiring for the fruit while cultivating the cause. Our Patriarchs have left words of sincerity;
how could we not exert ourselves? Now, on behalf of the children of the Buddha throughout the six realms, let us all with one mind recite the Buddha’s name, seeking birth in the Pure Land.
I pray that the Buddha, out of his great compassion, will graciously extend his protection and salvation.
This concludes the discourse on the Samādhi of Contemplative Mindfulness of the Buddha by the later student Yunqi Zhu Hong.
Now, I shall further explain the practice of mindfulness of the Buddha through the recitation of the Name.
Samādhi. I humbly reflect that as for the teaching of the Pure Land: it originated with the World-Honored One Śākyamuni and was propagated by the sages and saints of successive generations.
Consequently, the single gateway of mindfulness of the Buddha is divided into four types, the first of which is called mindfulness of the Buddha by reciting the name.
It is said: mindfulness through contemplating the image; mindfulness through contemplating the visualization; and mindfulness through the true mark (*dharmatā*).

Although there are these four distinct types, they ultimately converge in the true mark alone. Furthermore, the first three may be condensed into two: first, contemplative visualization; second, the recitation of the name.
Regarding contemplative visualization, the *Sūtra on the Sixteen Contemplations* explains it in detail. This treatise concerns the recitation of the name.

Thus, the *Amitābha Sūtra* states: "If one hears the name of Amitābha Buddha and holds it fast, whether for one day, two days, or even up to seven days, with single-mindedness and without distraction, then at the time of that person's death, Amitābha Buddha, together with a multitude of holy beings, will appear before them.
At the moment of death, this person’s mind will not be inverted, and they shall immediately attain rebirth in the Pure Land."
The Land of Ultimate Bliss of Amitābha Buddha is the great source from which this ten-thousand-year practice of reciting the Name has emerged;

it is the wondrous Dharma personally proclaimed by the Golden Mouth. An ancient master said: "The principle of the contemplative method is subtle, while the minds of sentient beings are杂 (variegated and distracted)."

In the *Saṃyuktābhidharmahṛdaya*, it is taught that the cultivation of visualization is difficult to accomplish. Out of great compassion, the Great Sage directly exhorted [practitioners] to single-mindedly uphold the Name.

This is because the recitation of the Name is easy, and through its continuous practice, rebirth occurs. This exposition of the merit of mindfulness of the Buddha by upholding the Name is the most essential method for rebirth in the Pure Land.
If one upholds the Name while deeply penetrating the true nature of reality (*dharmatā*), then its efficacy is equal to that of the sublime contemplation (*vimalakīrti-samādhi*). Superior.
One will certainly not doubt that they will be born in the highest grade. O present sons of the Buddha:

as in the previously explained section on repentance, even the noble ones of the two vehicles, the bodhisattvas of the perfect mind, and even those at the stage of Equal Enlightenment must still perform repentance. Since they all equally ought to repent, [so should you].

If even those [who have attained higher stages] should all necessarily attain rebirth there, how much more so those who remain in the stage of ordinary beings (*pṛthagjana*) and dwell on the level of learners (*śaikṣa*)?
I now, on behalf of these sons of the Buddha before us from the six realms, call upon the names of the Buddhas with a single mind, seeking rebirth in the Pure Land.

I pray that the Buddhas, out of their great compassion, will specially extend their grace to gather us in and save us. (The Dharma Master, together with the assembly and the sons of the Buddha from the six realms, shall chant the names of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the Western Quarter in unison.)

The title of the Sutra. One practices the method of ten recitations. The Dharma Master visualizes the Buddha-sons of the six realms; because they hear the Dharma, their minds open and their intentions are resolved, and they all together practice mindfulness of the Buddha, seeking rebirth there.

Amitābha Buddha and the various Great Beings, through the power of their compassion, take them into their care, so that these sentient beings of the six realms who practice mindfulness of the Buddha may, in an instant, ride upon jeweled lotus pedestals and attain birth in that land. (The ritual master, on behalf of the patron, expands the spirit of giving and makes the vow to deliver all beings, saying:)

I reflect with tranquility upon all the multitudes throughout the ten directions: though they dwell amidst the flourishing of civilization and culture, and though many among them have received the transmission of the Buddha-dharma, those whose six sense faculties are shrouded in darkness do not know it, and those who are submerged in the five sufferings do not awaken to it here.
How much more so for those in distant and remote lands—fools and the deaf-mute—who seek only the constant abundance of their own livelihood and clothing;
how could they have heard of the benefit of universally saving all beings of water and land?

As for those who are impoverished and stalled, entangled by illness, imprisoned in dungeons, or subjected to control in lowly stations, though they harbor longing and admiration, how can they attain it?
In undertaking this construction, one has already abandoned excellent conditions for oneself; how, then, could one receive the benefit of wholesome merit?
Now, on account of this vegetarian assembly, I have specially resolved upon a spirit of giving. Leading the deluded multitudes of the six realms, I set forth the great vow of a single mind.
Whether through doubt or faith, whether by myself or others, may all be fully satisfied in their expectations, so that this aspiration may be perfectly fulfilled.
(On behalf of the donor, for those among the multitudes of beings in the six realms who have not yet taken refuge in the Triple Gem, one exhorts them with the Ten Vows).

One portion of the merit from practicing this fast is dedicated to all sentient beings throughout the ten directions and the six realms of the Dharma-realm (hereafter, this phrase shall be recited as an example for each subsequent section).
For those who have never taken refuge in the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, I offer refuge on their behalf; may the compassionate light of the Triple Gem always descend to grant its protection.

For those who have never paid homage or offered praise to the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, I perform homage and praise on their behalf; may the compassionate light of the Triple Gem [ever shine upon them].
May you always extend your protective mindfulness.

For those who have never made offerings to the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, may you offer them on their behalf. We pray that the compassionate light of the Triple Gem will always extend its grace and sustain them.
For those who have never repented of the grave offenses of the three periods of time, I repent on their behalf;
may all karmic obstructions immediately become purified.
For those who have never exhorted the Buddhas to remain in the world, I exhort on their behalf; may they turn the sublime wheel of Dharma.
Universally benefiting the Dharma-realm,
may I, on behalf of those who have never rejoiced in or practiced the Mahāyāna, extend my own practice; may it be vowed that both myself and others shall perfectly fulfill our conduct and vows.

For those who have never dedicated their merit toward the diligent pursuit of the Buddha-way, I dedicate it on their behalf: may they universally share with all sentient beings the common entry into Buddha-wisdom.
For those who have never made the aspiration to seek the Way above and transform those below, I make this vow on their behalf: may the Buddha-way be perfectly accomplished.

For all sentient beings who have been universally delivered but never yet practiced mindfulness of the Buddha to seek rebirth in the Pure Land, may I on their behalf seek such rebirth for them; may they vow to be swiftly entrusted within a lotus womb and behold the Buddha upon the blossoming of the flower.

For those who have never yet resolved their minds to seek the path to Bodhi, may they resolve on their behalf; may they vow to cultivate it single-mindedly and completely until ultimate perfection is attained.

Thus far, for the sake of those whose karmic obstructions are profound and heavy—who have not heard the Dharma of the Triple Gem or the living beings of the Dharma-realm—I have exhorted these ten vows.
By means of this, may we form superior conditions and plant the seeds of Bodhi, aspiring for the fruit of enlightenment.

(The presiding priest acts as the donor, on behalf of all sentient beings of the seven realms and ten classes, individually repenting their karmic causes, striving for liberation, and exhorting them to cultivate the Ten Vows.)
The merit of practicing this fast, one portion is offered to the ten directions and the entire Dharma-realm (the subsequent sections follow this formula).

Among the various heavenly realms, beings are attached to pleasure without satiety; yet when the five signs of decay suddenly arrive, all sentient beings should aspire to advance toward the true and eternal, and quickly receive liberation.
Among the paths of the various sages, they set their aspirations upon the void and preserve their illusory physical forms.
May all sentient beings vow to advance in the study of non-arising and swiftly receive liberation.
All the merit-bestowing spirits preside over the Yin and Yang, bringing forth calamities or bestowing blessings.
May all sentient beings aspire to advance toward true cultivation and swiftly receive liberation.
Among all classes of people, those who seek fame and crave profit are submerged in the dust and wind of the world;
may all sentient beings aspire to advance in the study of the Mahāyāna and swiftly receive liberation.
Among all the asuras, there are those who delight in practicing anger and engage in incessant combat.
May all sentient beings vow to cease contention and give rise to loving-kindness, so that they may swiftly attain liberation.
Among all the hungry ghosts, who are tormented by hunger and thirst and undergo suffering throughout kalpas,
may all sentient beings have their parching afflictions eliminated and quickly attain liberation.
The chief officials of the underworld record births and deaths and adjudicate the prisoners in hell.
May all sentient beings pray that these officials uphold the law with broad compassion, so that they may swiftly attain liberation.
Within all the hells— both those with intervals and those without— where sentient beings endure suffering throughout kalpas,
may they all wish that the nature of their offenses is fundamentally empty, so that they may swiftly attain liberation.
Among all the animals, they devour one another and suffer death upon blades and block-and-presses.
May all sentient beings wish that the karma of enmity be suddenly emptied and that they quickly receive liberation.
Among all those in the intermediate states, wandering through the seven realms of rebirth and repeatedly undergoing birth and death,
may all sentient beings vow not to obscure their own spiritual luminosity and quickly receive liberation.
The immeasurable merit from the fasts observed above is dedicated to all sentient beings of the seven destinies and ten classes.
With earnest diligence, they are exhorted to cultivate the ten great vows, so that all may be covered by this vast grace and fully accomplish the perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*).

(On behalf of the donor, I declare that for the sovereign, ministers, and commoners of the Dharma-realm—noble and humble, male and female—each shall repent their karmic causes and advance toward liberation, vowing forty-eight aspirations.)
Of the merit from practicing this fast, one portion is offered to the Dharma-realm of the ten directions (hereafter, all subsequent instances shall follow this formula).
May the sovereign rulers of the central realm and the distant borderlands, whether they possess the Way or not,
compassionately regard their subjects and transform the world through virtue.
From the Empress and the Chief Consort down to the Ladies and Palace Maidens who serve within the inner quarters— all women of noble rank—
should aspire to model themselves after the Mother of the Four Quarters, serving their sovereign with the path of gentleness.
Members of the imperial household and the feudal states, sons and grandsons of emperors and kings, and all noble relatives, whether male or female, old or young—
may you serve your superiors with loyalty and long preserve your wealth and honor.

Those who assist the sovereign in governing the state, proclaiming the transformative teachings and guiding the people— whether stationed at court or serving in the provinces— all officials and functionaries should aspire to maintain loyalty,
empathy, and sincerity, thereby bringing peace to others and aiding all beings.

Personally leading the armies to govern the frontier regions, he sacrifices his own person for the sake of the state. May all generals and soldiers wish that military administration be rectified and clarified, so that the four quarters may be brought into awe and submission.
Those who served as ministers, such as Sun Ce, who were slandered and exiled, or met untimely deaths—
may all officials and bureaucrats wish that their deeds be made manifest and that they may fully preserve their loyalty and integrity.
If a general loses discipline while leading his army and violates military orders, thereby incurring severe punishment,
may all the officers and soldiers vow to keep loyalty and righteousness in their hearts and preserve their own lives and families.
Having clarified the scriptures and cultivated practice, he lived in seclusion to teach, seeking neither fame nor status.
All worthy scholars should wish that his Way be honored and dignified, and that his long-studied learning be clearly illuminated.
Having left the household life with right intention and reverently cultivated the three trainings, though the fruits of the Path have not yet matured,
may all monks and nuns vow never to retreat from their original resolve and ultimately achieve perfect enlightenment.

Their aspirations are set upon longevity, and they cultivate their minds with focused diligence. As the Great Elixir has not yet been perfected, all practitioners of the Way should wish that they first achieve success through skillful means and then turn their hearts toward the Buddha-way.
Tilling the fields and raising silkworms, gathering firewood and picking fruit, they sustain themselves through manual labor.
May all such farmers wish that the land yield abundant harvests and that their entire families be warm and well-fed.
The myriad artisans and those of various skills depend on the four quarters for their sustenance; though they toil with hardship, they achieve nothing.
May all people in human society wish that their trades be successfully sold and that they never lack clothing or food.

Physicians specialize in treating illnesses, and diviners resolve doubts through their arts; before these professional skills are perfected, one should aspire to study all human relations with clarity and precision, so as to benefit others and assist all things.

When traveling by boat to maritime lands, amidst the rows of stalls and marketplaces where one's desires remain unfulfilled, and regarding all human relations, one should wish that goods and wealth circulate freely,
bringing abundance to households and prosperity to the nation.
Those who crave fame and pursue profit travel to the four quarters, toiling and rushing about.
May all people of every station in life wish to purify their minds and diminish their desires, finding joy in Heaven and understanding their destiny.
May all officials, clerks, attendants, and laborers; those who manage private households; slaves and servants;
and all members of the human community, resolve to be loyal and faithful in their hearts and maintain integrity and prudence in their conduct.
In besieging cities and seizing territory, they take pleasure in establishing feats of achievement and delight in killing living beings.
Regarding all human relations, one should aspire to hold compassion within one's heart and to revere the lives of creatures.
Those who fish, hunt, slaughter, and butcher, killing for the sake of profit and living by selling meat— among all such human beings,
they should aspire to swiftly give rise to a heart of compassion and immediately cast off their evil karma.
As for shamans and sorcerers who employ left-handed paths to delude the masses, and those who harbor deceit under the guise of mysterious secrets—
may all such people among the human community resolve to cease their deviant minds and turn toward the Great Way.
Regarding the lewd music of actors and performers, the seductive songs and alluring dances, and the deceptive display of female beauty— all such matters of human conduct—
one should vow to feel self-reproach and shame, reforming one's way to follow right action.
Those who have gone out to serve in the military and died in battle, or those who were unjustly executed by the army—
all such members of the human community should resolve to repent for their past transgressions and forever eliminate their evil karma.
Amidst the turmoil of war and weapons, we may be forced to migrate to distant lands; encountering bandits, we may suffer injury.
Regarding all human relations, one should pray that one may encounter virtuous people who will guide and protect us, enabling us to survive and thrive.

For those subjected to blades, staves, shackles, and fetters; to unlawful imprisonment; or to the calamities of the sovereign—may all such people encounter upright and enlightened rulers, and may they be swiftly granted release and pardon.
Tigers, wolves, and venomous snakes; rākṣasas and wicked bandits; the perils of wind, fire, and water;
and all members of the human race—may they always give rise to a heart of compassion and not dare to cause harm.
Those who have been poisoned by sorcery, those who have committed suicide by cutting their own throats or hanging themselves, those crushed by walls or burned or drowned—
may all such human relations see their past karma extinguished and return once more to the path of goodness.
May those struck down by heavenly thunder, those summoned for litigation from their graves, and those whose departed spirits have returned to haunt their kin—
may all such human relations resolve their past karmic causes and each seek transcendence and deliverance.
When seized by enemies, mistakenly imprisoned by hell-wardens, or oppressed by malevolent spirits— among all such human conditions— one should pray that past roots of goodness may provide support,
so that one may be released at the proper time.
Those who possess worldly wisdom and eloquence, who delight in literary composition, and who disparage and profane the Buddha-dharma among all classes of people—
may they all vow to turn their praise toward the Mahāyāna and instantly eliminate their false views.
Foolish, ignorant, vulgar, base, and inferior, and lacking faith in the Triple Gem—
all such human beings should aspire to have deep faith in Bodhi and bring forth sublime wisdom.
One’s four limbs do not labor; all day long one is dissolute, neglecting all affairs and the duties of human relations.
One should wish to maintain the body with diligence and care, and to manage one's righteous vocation.
Subjected to the service of others, they run to and fro upon the roads, their toil never ceasing.
May all people of every human relation wish that they may soon attain leisure and ease, and find self-sufficiency in whatever they seek.
Indulging in wine and lust, gambling and wandering about, they ruin their families and squander their fortunes.
Regarding all matters of human relations, one should vow to establish firm resolve and preserve one’s person, so as to restore the ancestral legacy.
Whether traveling by water or land, those who commit robbery with weapons, or those who steal by breaking and entering— among all such human relations—
they should vow to repent their former ways and once again seek the path of right livelihood.
Struggling over wealth and property, slandered and beset by calumny, and bound by curses—
may all such human relations resolve their enmity and harbor no desire for retaliation.
When there are differences in speech and disputes do not cease, and people strike one another,
may all human relations wish for their two minds to be in harmony and never form knots of resentment.

Those who offer flattery while harboring malice, who slander and exclude the virtuous and good, and who seek only their own self-interest— may all members of the human community resolve to dwell in their hearts with loyalty and integrity,
and to honor and exalt the sages and the wise.

Believing slander and hating the upright; envying the virtuous and worthy; being arrogant and self-exalting—among all human relations, one should aspire to joyfully listen to loyal counsel and take pleasure in associating with those of virtue.
Regarding harsh speech, double-tongued talk, and the fondness for angry abuse, as well as harboring hidden malice to harm others— all such behaviors among the human race—
should one vow to forever sever evil words and treat all beings with a compassionate heart.
For those suffering from epilepsy or cholera, from impairment of the vital breath or heat-stroke, from sudden death from external spirits or nightmares—
may all members of the human community never lose their original mind and quickly encounter wondrous healing.
For those afflicted by consumption, exhaustion, pestilence, abscesses, carbuncles, or malignant swellings, and for all people entangled by foul diseases,
may they encounter a skilled physician at an early stage and preserve their lives.
May those who are blind, deaf, hunchbacked, or lame; those paralyzed by wind-disorders or afflicted with hemiplegia;
and all those with crippled limbs among the human race, wish to soon encounter divine remedies and attain complete physical forms.

May widowers, widows, orphans, and the solitary; the poor, the destitute, those suffering from hunger and cold, and the aged and infirm who have no one to turn to—may all members of the human community obtain the support of the benevolent and the virtuous, who shall provide for them throughout their lives.
Envious of favor, relying on personal kindness, arrogant, extravagant, licentious, and fierce— neglecting the domestic duties of the inner chambers and failing in all human relations—
one should vow to provide internal instruction within the private quarters, guarding one's will with integrity and purity.
The husband and wife were advanced in years and prayed for offspring, yet they did not obtain what they desired.
All people of human relations should pray to give birth to sons of merit and virtue, who may inherit the family and continue its lineage.

For all infants, both boys and girls, who have not yet outgrown their swaddling clothes and have perished prematurely from the cessation of nursing— may these children of meager merit be protected by divine beings,
and may their lives be prolonged and free from illness.
For those who have suffered miscarriages or injuries to their pregnancies, whose children die within the womb, or who experience difficult labors and cannot deliver—
may all women of such condition pray that both mother and child be preserved whole, and that their lives be kept secure.
They were unfilial toward their parents and failed to nurture their wives and children; resentment accumulated and their hearts became estranged from all human relations.
They should now vow to turn their minds toward filial piety and compassion, repenting to eliminate their past karma.
Regarding the five heinous crimes and the ten evil deeds, lack of benevolence and righteousness, lack of loyalty and trustworthiness, and all matters of human relations—
one should sincerely vow to reform them, repenting for and eliminating past transgressions.
The immeasurable merit from the fasts observed above is dedicated to all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm.
By earnestly exhorting them to cultivate the forty-eight vows, they shall be able to repent their karmic causes and immediately receive transcendence and deliverance.
I shall now reverently recite the Fruit-Vow Mantra of our Buddha, the Tathāgata. Namo ratnatrayāya.
Namo āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahā...

Miryaye kāyaṅgimaśapānaye ni deśpamaśamuta miśudata niśudaya sarvadaityagadastuti paduma miśudata svāhā.

(After reciting the mantra three times, ring the hand-bell and cymbals. (The Dharma Master contemplates all sentient beings of the dharma-realm, that through this they may all be universally delivered and reach the site of enlightenment. Having repeatedly received the benefit of the joy of the Dharma, they are further able to set forth vast vows.

May their practice and conduct be perfected to adorn the Dharma-body; never retreating from this mind, they shall expect the fruit of Buddhahood. (The ritual master recites a verse to praise the Triple Gem and proclaims the dedication of merit. This verse is from the *Sūtra on the Divine Transformations and Empowerment*. The verse says:)

I prostrate to the Buddhas of the ten directions and three periods of time, to the Three Constant Bodies, the Treasury of the True Dharma, and the assembly of those with supreme vows and the great bodhicitta mind; I now take refuge in all of them with perfect sincerity.
Having recited these verses to look up to and praise the Triple Gem of the Dharmadhātu, I pray that you will again grant your clear testimony at a later time. On this day, there was...

To the Triple Gem, [Name]: We have performed the Great Universal Deliverance Offering for the Holy and the Profane throughout the Dharma Realm, including the construction and maintenance of the ritual site, and the proclamation and execution of the liturgical rites.
These are now completed. A formal memorial has been prepared, which we shall now respectfully read aloud.

(When the recitation of the ritual petitions is finished, the assembly of practitioners steps forward to read the offering documents in sections. Once all have been read, one person further reads the official document from the Office of Merit regarding the details of the proceedings.)
(Reciting the verse of self-congratulation for the sake of the donors and the great assembly, he said:

"Taking the principle of the Dharma-realm as my basis, I give rise to the mind of the Dharma-realm; facing the objects of the Dharma-realm, I practice the offering of the Dharma-realm before the Buddhas of the ten directions."

Praising and expounding upon the Mahāyāna, one universally delivers those in the six realms through the gateway of great compassion. By practicing the three types of giving and perfecting the six perfections, this is called the true offering of the Dharma.
When the observance of the fast is completed, one rejoices for oneself and for others, making the vow that all sages and worthies [may likewise rejoice].
[The officiant] protects and mindfully attends to the intestines.
(The *biaobai* [offering prayer] is recited while ringing the bell; the incantation is chanted for the dismissal. The following is spoken:

"The clear night draws to a close, and this excellent banquet is about to disperse. Having fully performed the rites of the fast, we have truly accorded with the sentiments of all beings. Many protocols have been displayed..."

All things have a beginning and an end; according to the grand rites, one ought to perform the full ceremonies of welcoming and seeing off. Yet, the Sage dwells in perpetual stillness, fundamentally transcending coming and going.

To cause ordinary minds to achieve thorough awakening and return to the Truth—how could there not be skillful means? He provides them with the power of the Dharma and envelops them in the Buddha’s radiance.
Drawing from the left and pulling from the right, they exhaustively deliver all beings within the seven realms of existence; advancing and retreating, they enter with ease the nine grades of rebirth.

Having attained birth in the Land of Bliss, they immediately turn their thoughts back toward the mundane world, constantly giving rise to such great compassion and extending the path of universal salvation throughout the furthest reaches of the future.
Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses a mantra for dispatching [deities].
I shall now reverently recite it: Oṃ mārala mukkhya mu...
(Having finished reciting the mantra three times, strike the ghaṇṭā. Circumambulate the seats. Send the sages and worthies out of the maṇḍala hall. Perform the ritual of refining the wealth-horse.)

(The Dharma Master visualized that all the holy sages, each by their own majestic virtue, gathered and rescued those in the six realms of existence, causing them to each abandon their original karma and be reborn in the Pure Land. The entire great assembly departed, none without joy and exultation.)
The Ritual Manual for the Auspicious Assembly of the Dharma Realm of Sages and Ordinary Beings, Land and Water, Volume Six:
The Liturgical Texts for the Water and Land Rite. It is traditionally said that this originated with Emperor Wu of the Liang Dynasty. Formerly, Bai Qi [caused] a single pit at Changping...
When the number reached four hundred thousand, his transgressions were so great and his evil so extreme that he sank into the hells for a long time, with no means of escape.
Consequently, he appeared in a dream to Emperor Wu. Emperor Wu consulted with Master Zhigong and other masters regarding a strategy to rescue him.

They learned that within the Great Canon there was the ritual text for the Water and Land ceremonies; when they prayed according to it, a brilliant light filled the hall. From this, the rite was performed and transmitted to future generations. And...

At present, the texts for these are not found in the Tripitaka. The versions held at Kinkoji Temple are likewise disordered from beginning to end, and their overall structure and sequence cannot be discerned.
Furthermore, the monks and practitioners of the time have each produced works according to their own inclinations, resulting in slight variations among them.
As for the images of the upper and lower halls painted at Nanto, they follow the traditions of individual artists; though treated as established rules, they are by no means entirely accurate.
As for those who establish a *dharmapūjā* site (*dharmakṣetra*), they must raise funds through proselytization over many months and years before it can finally be accomplished.
With its elaborate ritual arrangements, it causes men and women, old and young, to arrive in great throngs like commoners watching a banner festival or the spring season;
they jostle feet and rub shoulders, with men and women intermingled in such numbers reaching thousands daily, yet they cannot avoid profaning the sacred.
The worthy [practitioner] may clash with spirits and deities; the losses will be many and the transgressions grave.
There will be calamity without merit, and frequently, the path to the *bodhimaṇḍa* will not be completed, leading instead to the retribution of evil. This is truly something to be feared.

Only the ritual texts compiled by the Dharma Master Zhipan of Siming are supremely refined and subtle, supremely concise and easy to follow. They are precise and meticulous without being burdened by excessive complexity.
It is extensive, yet concise and simple, without the flaw of omissions. Its original text exists only in the Four Ming (Zhejiang) region; it has not been seen in other quarters.
I have corrected it and re-carved it for printing, so as to circulate it widely. Nevertheless, this cannot be done lightly; one must raise [the matter] repeatedly.
If it were easy, it would inevitably lead to frequency; once there is frequency, [the spirit] will naturally arise.
It is easy [to fall into error]. Consequently, one becomes lax in sincerity and reverence, resulting in many transgressions; thus, instead of seeking blessings, one brings about calamity.
I hope you will all exercise caution in this matter. (Extracted from *Zhuchuang Sanbi*)
